profile: Cai Huabo (蔡华波, b. 1976, Jiujiang, Jiangxi) went to Shenzhen after high school. In 1999 he and his twin sister Cai Lijiang turned a tiny Huaqiangbei electronics-market stall into Longsys, now a major memory/storage maker (FORESEE, Lexar, Zilia). profile: Bern-born Hansjörg Wyss (b. 1935), an ETH Zurich civil engineer and Harvard MBA, founded Synthes USA in 1977 to sell AO bone-fixation plates and screws. A Giving Pledge signatory, he now concentrates on philanthropy, especially land conservation through the Wyss Foundation.
interesting_fact: He funded Harvard's Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering, and his Wyss Campaign for Nature pledged $1B+ to protect 30% of the planet by 2030. In 2024 he gave CHF 100M to the City of Bern, which made him an honorary citizen.
deep_cut_fact: While working in the steel industry in Brussels, he ran a side business selling airplanes. One of those sales introduced him to a surgeon who had co-founded Synthes, which led to his medical-device career. Earlier he worked as a textile-plant engineer and as a Chrysler project manager in Pakistan, Turkey and the Philippines.
current_role: Chairman, Wyss Foundation; founder and former chairman/CEO of Synthes; co-owner of Chelsea FC
research_notes: Aged 91 and very private; he rarely gives interviews. The foundation's contact form is the only published channel, and it warns about impersonators. Hooks: the conservation and land-protection work, the engineering background, and the Glenturret distillery he bought with Silvio Denz in 2019.

interesting_fact: She and Jiang Bin started GoerTek in 2001; the company grew from a microphone maker in Weifang into one of the world's largest makers of acoustic components and VR/AR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: A Harbin Institute of Technology graduate, she joined GoerTek in 2001 as manager of its marketing department and later led its operations leadership group before becoming vice president.
current_role: Co-founder and Vice President (per 2019 filing), GoerTek Inc. (SZSE: 002241)

profile: Glasgow-educated Scottish chartered accountant who married into Hong Kong's Kadoorie family (wife Rita is Sir Michael Kadoorie's sister). current_role: Private investor; Kadoorie-family shareholder in CLP Holdings (retired from CLP board 2016 and HKSH board 2017)

Apollo now runs about 80 hospitals and more than 7,000 pharmacies. current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Bestway Group (nephew Lord Zameer Choudrey is chairman)

In December 2025 his vehicle Ever Genius bought 75% of Easy Smart Group, a Hong Kong passive-fire-protection subcontractor that had the largest market share there. The company says it is now looking to diversify into AI and communications, and its shares surged. The listing appears to be the source of his Hurun valuation. He was earlier an executive director of Shin Hwa World (2019-2020).
interesting_fact: Easy Smart's 2026 annual report says Galaxy Equity Management, wholly owned by Chu, controls Ever Genius. After 30 June 2026 Ever Genius sold 102M shares (25%) to Terminus Consumer Ltd, leaving it with about 39.6%.
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Easy Smart Group Holdings (HKEX: 2442) via Ever Genius International / Galaxy Equity Management, which he wholly owns
research_notes: Very little public information; he is not on Easy Smart's board. MarketScreener lists him as a Hefei University of Technology graduate (unverified). Web search budget ran out mid-research, so the Chinese-language sources were not fully checked. Treat the billionaire valuation as volatile because it rests on a stock that surged on an AI pivot.

name: Zhang Shuangwang
profile: Zhang Shuangwang (张双旺), born 1943 in Jungar Banner, Inner Mongolia, was a local government official before founding Yitai in 1988. Yitai grew into a large Ordos-based group spanning coal mining, coal railways and coal-to-liquids, controlling listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal (SSE B-shares/HKEX). He is recorded as responsible person of the group's holding company, Yitai Investment.
interesting_fact: Yitai Coal's ultimate controller, Inner Mongolia Yitai Investment Co., is itself owned by 2,315 individual shareholders rather than one family vehicle; Zhang Shuangwang is its legal representative.
deep_cut_fact: In March 1988 Zhang gave up his post as deputy head of the Ikh Ju League (now Ordos) township-enterprise office and led 21 surplus government staff out of the civil service to start Yitai; he was later named a National Model Worker (1995).
current_role: Founder of Inner Mongolia Yitai Group; legal representative of Inner Mongolia Yitai Investment Co., the de facto controller of Yitai Coal (per 2022 annual report)
research_notes: Born 1943 (about 83). No death reports found and he is still on Hurun lists through 2026, but there is no recent public activity, so alive is marked unknown. Wealth is shared with Zhang Donghai, former Yitai Coal chairman. Very low public profile; the only route is Yitai Coal's board secretary/IR office. Current day-to-day chairman of Yitai Coal is Zhang Jingquan.

name: Zhang Donghai
profile: Zhang Donghai is the son of Zhang Shuangwang, who founded Ordos-based coal producer Yitai Group in 1988. Donghai joined in 2001, became group general manager in 2004 and long chaired Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal, which expanded into railways and coal-to-liquids. Zhang Jingquan succeeded him as Yitai Coal chairman in Dec 2019; the family shares the fortune.
interesting_fact: Yitai began in 1988 when his father quit a government post and led 21 surplus civil servants to start the company; Yitai Coal later became China's first coal company listed via B shares and expanded into coal-to-liquid fuels.
deep_cut_fact: In 2001, during Yitai's hardest period, he resigned a division-level post in the Inner Mongolia regional government to join a Yitai subsidiary as general manager; cost controls in his first year alone added about RMB 12 million, and he launched the 'Yitai clean coal' brand with national research institutes.
current_role: Reported as president/director of Inner Mongolia Yitai Group; chaired listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal until late 2019 (current group title not confirmed by official source)
research_notes: Low public profile; little recent English-language coverage. Fortune shared with father Zhang Shuangwang (Hurun). No verified published personal/office contact found; Yitai corporate websites did not load. Best route is likely Yitai Coal's company secretary/IR via HKEX or SSE filings.

profile: Born in Baghdad in 1936, Eliahu emigrated to Israel at 14 and grew up in a transit camp and south Tel Aviv. interesting_fact: He served in the Knesset (Dash/Democratic Movement, then his own Ahva faction) and chaired the Knesset's capital-markets subcommittee before quitting politics in 1981.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he worked as a messenger boy at Migdal -- the insurer he bought control of in 2012. His first agency (1955) ran from the corner of a motorcycle-repair garage in Tel Aviv's Shapira neighborhood, and he signed up clients by bicycle while also promoting entertainment shows.
current_role: Controlling shareholder and director, Migdal Insurance & Financial Holdings (stepped down as chair in 2022); chairman, Eliahu Insurance
research_notes: Aged ~90; no death reported. Hanan Melcer replaced him as Migdal chair (2022, Globes). Quote from honorary-fellow citation: 'The hardships forged me. Wealth never spoke to me.' No personal contact channel found; route via Migdal corporate.

name: Zhu Mengyi
profile: Zhu Mengyi (朱孟依, Chu Mang Yee, b. 1959) is from Fengshun county, Guangdong. He founded Guangzhou-born developer Hopson Development in 1992, listed it in Hong Kong in 1998 and later moved its headquarters to Beijing. His Zhujiang Investment group also holds transport infrastructure, energy, education and technology assets. He served on China's CPPCC national committee.
interesting_fact: Hopson was once one of Guangdong's five biggest private developers. In October 2021, during the Evergrande crisis, it agreed to buy a 51% stake in Evergrande's property-management arm, but the deal was suspended.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from Koupu village in Liuhuang town, Fengshun county, a Hakka/Chaoshan area of eastern Guangdong. He built the Zhujiang Investment group alongside Hopson, and Chinese media have called it his 'invisible' wealth empire.
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Hopson Development Holdings (HKEX: 754) and Zhujiang (Pearl River) Investment Group. Longtime chairman; his current board title was not verified.
research_notes: Extremely private; he gives essentially no interviews. Hopson's IR site (hosted by irasia) did not expose a contact email, and the web search budget ran out before a published IR/press email could be found. Check Hopson's latest HKEX annual report for the current board (family members may now chair it).

interesting_fact: Before Bending Spoons, the founders met while studying in Copenhagen and built a failed note-taking app called Evertale. A decade later Bending Spoons bought Evernote, the best-known note-taking app.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike his Padua-educated co-founders, Querella is the computer scientist of the group. He earned a computer science degree at the University of Turin and a computer engineering degree at the IT University of Copenhagen.
current_role: Co-founder, Bending Spoons S.p.A. (Nasdaq: BSP), Milan
research_notes: Keeps a very low public profile. CEO Luca Ferrari does nearly all the interviews. The company is listed in Hong Kong (867), and he owns about 47.9% through his wholly owned company Treasure Sea Limited.

name: Li Ganpo
profile: Founder of Jingye Group, a large private Chinese steelmaker (rebar, plate, sheet, rails) with interests in chemicals, pharma, logistics, tourism and 3D-printing metal powders. He started with a chemical plant in 1988, entered steel in 2002, and in 2020 bought British Steel out of insolvency; the UK government took control of British Steel in 2025.
interesting_fact: Jingye's first fortune came from chemicals (acid) before steel; the group also built roads, housing and schools and provides healthcare and higher education for employees and the local community.
deep_cut_fact: A former teacher, he founded a canning factory and a brewery in Pingshan county near Beijing in 1985, then the Jingye chemical factory in 1988; 'jingye' means 'dedication'. He served in the 11th National People's Congress from 2008.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Jingye Group (敬业集团), Hebei/Beijing
research_notes: Low media profile. British Steel ownership dispute with UK government (2025-26) is sensitive - avoid as an outreach hook. No published personal/press contact found; route would be via Jingye Group corporate office.

current_role: Co-founder and former chairman/CEO of Hsu Fu Chi (徐福记); retired from the business after Nestlé bought the family's remaining stake in 2025

profile: Li Xiangping heads Shandong Dongming Petrochemical, one of China's largest private 'teapot' refiners, based in Heze, Shandong. He took over a near-bankrupt small refinery and grew it into a group with about RMB 50bn in assets and 8,000+ staff. He has since pushed it from fuels into downstream chemicals. Li has also served as a delegate to the National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: Under Li, Dongming built the 20 Mt/yr Rizhao-Dongming crude pipeline, listed its subsidiary Hengchang Chemical in Singapore, and became the first private refiner in China to obtain crude-oil import qualification. In 2022 Shandong named him a 'provincial industry-leading entrepreneur'.
deep_cut_fact: Li set up an in-house 'brain trust' of 12 of China's top chemical experts to advise the group. His motto for fuel quality: '油品如同食品、滴滴都是承诺' (fuel is like food, and every drop is a promise).
current_role: Party Secretary and Chairman of the Board, Shandong Dongming Petrochemical Group (山东东明石化集团)

name: Ge Haiquan
profile: Founder, chairman and GM of Shijia Photons, a Hebi, Henan optical-chip maker listed on the STAR Market (he holds about 6.7%). It began in indoor optical cable and moved into optoelectronic chips in 2010. It now makes PLC splitter, AWG and DFB laser chips, with AI data-center demand driving growth since 2024.
interesting_fact: In 2024 revenue rose 42% to RMB 1.07B and net profit rose 234%, both driven by AI computing-power and datacom demand for its AWG chips used in data-center optical modules.
deep_cut_fact: Shijia grew out of a 2010 R&D tie-up with the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Semiconductors. A year later it was the first and only company in China able to mass-produce PLC optical splitter chips, and by 2015 those chips held over 50% of the global market. All of this was built from a small city in northern Henan.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Henan Shijia Photons Technology Co. (688313.SH)
research_notes: Low public profile in English-language media. The deep-cut fact is about his company rather than him personally. info@sjphotons.com is the company's general inbox. The board secretary/IR office on SSE filings is the formal route.

deep_cut_fact: Alongside optics, she has run Macau trading businesses for decades: director and legal representative of 联盈制服 (uniforms) since 1996, 迅盈行贸易 (trading) since 1998 and 联盈旗帜 (flags/banners) since 1999, per AFR's director disclosure.

He stepped down at 90 in Dec 2022; son Jai Shroff is now chairman and group CEO.

With his six children he formed Meijin Energy Group in 2000, now led by son Yao Junliang and grandson Yao Jinlong; listed Meijin Energy (000723) has moved into hydrogen.
interesting_fact: By the late 1980s he was reportedly Shanxi's richest man - a provincial leader dubbed the family 'the No. 1 household of Shanxi'. In 1996, aged 65, he told his heirs the family was only a 'passing god of wealth' holding money on society's behalf.
deep_cut_fact: Locals still call him 'the old party secretary'; he promised fellow villagers ten years of free coal gas, and the supply has reportedly stayed free for more than 30 years, alongside family-funded projects such as Renyi New Village and Renyi Primary School in Qingxu.
current_role: Founding patriarch and shareholder of Shanxi Meijin Energy Group (Qingxu, Shanxi); no current executive role - son Yao Junliang chairs the group
research_notes: Born c.1931 (aged 65 in 1996), so now about 95; no death report found but no recent news either - treat alive as unknown. Last on rich lists in 2010. Any outreach should go via Meijin Energy (SZSE 000723) board secretary; no published email found.

name: Pedro Brescia Moreyra
profile: Third-generation member (born 1971, son of Mario Brescia Cafferata) of the family behind Breca, Peru's largest conglomerate (Minsur tin/copper mining, TASA fishmeal, Rímac insurance, BBVA Perú stake, Melón cement, real estate). Formerly Breca's general manager, he now co-chairs the group with cousin Alex Fort Brescia and sits on many group boards.
interesting_fact: Breca's mining arm Minsur is one of the world's largest tin producers and, through Marcobre, runs the Mina Justa copper project; Pedro sits on both boards.
deep_cut_fact: A Universidad de Lima business graduate with a Kellogg MBA, he serves on the board of Aporta (Breca's social-impact platform) and is a director of the Instituto Peruano de Economía think tank.
current_role: Co-Chairman, Grupo Breca (Peru); Vice Chairman, Rímac Seguros
research_notes: Do not confuse with his uncle Pedro Brescia Cafferata (1921-2014). Family is very private; route via Breca corporate communications. Energy/mining angle (Minsur, Marcobre) fits the podcast.

name: Pan Xueping
profile: Pan Xueping (潘雪平) founded Changzhou-based Jiangsu Jinsheng Industry in 2000. In 2013 Jinsheng bought Oerlikon's natural-fibre and textile-components businesses (deal value about CHF 650m) and revived the historic Swiss Saurer brand. Pan chairs Shanghai-listed Saurer Intelligent Technology and is vice-president of China's textile machinery and textile engineering associations.
interesting_fact: Jinsheng's 2013 purchase of Oerlikon's textile units brought back the 160-year-old Swiss Saurer name. Pan said the new Saurer would be run operationally from Wattwil, Switzerland and financially from Shanghai.
deep_cut_fact: A textile-machinery engineer by background, before founding Jinsheng he ran a spinning-ring (钢领) factory at Pacific Group's Shanghai textile-parts works, then led the Jintan Textile Machinery Plant and was CEO of a Swiss spinning group's front-end spinning division.
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Jinsheng Industry (金昇实业) and Saurer Intelligent Technology (卓郎智能, SSE: 600545)
research_notes: Low public profile in English-language media. Name in Chinese: 潘雪平; Hurun's 'Jinsheng' is 金昇. Jinsheng also has large textile operations in Xinjiang (Litai Silk Road), a possibly sensitive topic. Best route is Saurer IR.

name: He Renbao
profile: He Renbao co-founded Zhejiang Yongtai Technology in 1999 in Linhai, Taizhou, with his wife Wang Yingmei, who chairs it. MarketScreener lists him as founder and director and as CEO from 2007. Yongtai makes fluorinated intermediates for pharmaceuticals and crop protection, plus battery materials such as LiPF6 and LiFSI lithium salts, and has expanded into the EV supply chain.
interesting_fact: Yongtai was the first Shenzhen-listed company to issue GDRs on the London Stock Exchange.
current_role: Co-founder, director and controlling shareholder (with wife Wang Yingmei), Zhejiang Yongtai Technology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002326)
research_notes: Fortune shared with his wife Wang Yingmei. MarketScreener lists a Kuang He as CEO since 2020, so his current executive title is unclear. He keeps a low profile, and I found no English interviews. zhengquan@ is the securities/investor-relations department inbox. The battery-materials angle (EV electrolyte salts) is relevant to energy.

name: Wang Yingmei
profile: Wang Yingmei is co-founder and, with He Renbao, joint actual controller of Zhejiang Yongtai Technology in Linhai/Taizhou, a fluorine-chemistry maker of pharmaceutical and crop-protection intermediates and new-energy materials such as lithium-battery electrolyte salts. She built the business from small local chemical plants in the 1990s and still runs it day to day.
interesting_fact: Yongtai describes itself as a fluorine-technology-centred maker of fluorinated pharma, crop-protection and new-energy (lithium battery) materials, with subsidiaries spanning electrolyte materials, fluorinated chips materials and lithium mining in Hainan.
deep_cut_fact: She started as a technician at Huangyan No.4 Chemical Plant (1987-92), then ran the Linhai Xingchen Chemical Plant (1992-97) and Linhai Yongli Fine Chemical Plant (1997-99) before founding Zhejiang Yongtai Chemical in 1999; she holds an EMBA and is a senior economist.
current_role: Chairwoman (since 2007) and General Manager (since Jul 2025), Zhejiang Yongtai Technology (SZ: 002326)
research_notes: Wealth shared with co-controller He Renbao. Very low media profile; board-secretary/securities office (zhengquan@) is the published route. Battery-materials angle is relevant to energy coverage.

name: Ji Xuewen
profile: Ji Xuewen co-founded Dynanonic (德方纳米) in 2007 with a RMB500,000 capital contribution alongside two partners. The company became a major supplier of nano-scale LFP cathode material for EV and energy-storage batteries. He was its signing company head around 2020, holding about 20%; his stake has since fallen through transfers to 7.53% (Q1 2026), and Kong Lingyong now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: Dynanonic started in 2007 as a RMB500,000 limited company set up by Ji Xuewen, Yang Haiyan and Wang Yunshi, and grew into a leading supplier of LFP cathode material for China's EV and grid-storage boom.
current_role: Co-founder and major individual shareholder (7.53% as of Q1 2026) of Shenzhen Dynanonic (SZSE: 300769), a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material maker; no current executive role confirmed
research_notes: Very low public profile and no English-language bio found. His stake has fallen sharply (about 20% in 2020 to 7.53% in 2026), so he is likely no longer a billionaire; the Hurun listing was 2022-23 only. 'Alive' is marked unknown only because no personal coverage exists; he is still listed as a shareholder in 2026. Relevant to the energy-storage theme. The only route is company IR.

name: Jin Liguo
profile: Jin Liguo (b. May 1973) founded Yiheda, a Dongguan-based one-stop supplier of standardized factory-automation components (a Chinese counterpart to Japan's Misumi) for non-standard automation equipment makers, including lithium-battery and electronics lines. He has run its predecessor since 1999 and has chaired the company since 2017; it listed on ChiNext in 2021.
interesting_fact: Yiheda's model is to standardize the thousands of small mechanical and electrical parts that custom automation-equipment builders need and sell them through a one-stop catalog, cutting design and procurement time for China's automation industry.
deep_cut_fact: With only a high-school education, he started as a technician at the Xingcheng Bearing Factory (1993-95), then worked as a salesman at a Shenyang aerospace special-equipment plant before taking over as general manager of Shenzhen Yiheda in 1999.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Dongguan Yiheda Automation Co., Ltd. (怡合达, SZSE ChiNext: 301029)
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts. Board office (secretary Zhang Meiqi) is the published route. Customers include new-energy/battery equipment makers - relevant energy angle.

name: Kong Lingyong
profile: Born 1978, a professor-level senior engineer and co-founder (2007) of Shenzhen Dynanonic, a leading maker of nano lithium iron phosphate (LFP), lithium manganese iron phosphate and lithium-supplement cathode materials for EV and energy-storage batteries. He is the company's core technology inventor and largest individual shareholder, and a deputy to the 14th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: He leads China's national nano energy-storage technology standards working group (SAC/TC279/WG7) and is an expert on ISO/IEC nanotechnology committees; Dynanonic now ships 4th-generation high-density LFP.
deep_cut_fact: Despite holding only a bachelor's degree, he is an external doctoral supervisor at Central South University and has won the China Patent Award and the title 'Guangdong Outstanding Inventor'.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Dynanonic Co. (SZSE: 300769), lithium-battery cathode materials
research_notes: Strong fit for an energy-storage/battery-materials episode. Board secretary is He Yanyan (IR route). Likely needs Chinese-language outreach.

name: Hong Zhenhai
profile: Hung Chen-hai (洪鎮海) co-founded Eclat Textile in 1977 with NT$500,000 and built it into one of Asia's largest makers of stretch and functional fabrics and sportswear for brands like Nike. He retired in June 2024, handing the chair to Wang Shu-wen while his son became president.
interesting_fact: Known in Taiwan as the 'father of functional fabric'; Eclat reportedly never posted an annual loss in its 40+ years and became the textile sector's highest-priced stock.
deep_cut_fact: Born to a farming family in Miaoli, he started as an apprentice in a dyeing plant; after studying in Japan in the early 1980s he wove Taiwan's first roll of stretch knit fabric in 1983, and began co-developing fabrics with Nike two years later.
current_role: Founder and retired chairman of Eclat Textile (儒鴻, TWSE:1476), Taiwan; left the board June 2024
research_notes: Taiwanese (Hurun lists 'China'). Retired; publicly stated succession should be by merit not family ('傳賢不傳子'). Email is Eclat's company contact from exchange filings. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Jiang Jinzhi
profile: Jiang Jinzhi (George Jiang) founded Greenwoods Asset Management in 2004; it grew into one of Asia's largest China-focused hedge fund managers (~US$20bn AUM in 2023) with offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Singapore. A long-term value investor, he has gradually stepped back from front-line management as newer portfolio managers took over.
interesting_fact: Before founding Greenwoods he was an early Chinese securities regulator/market builder: he ran the treasury-bond futures department at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, was assistant president of Guosen Securities and chairman of Yuehai Securities (HK).
deep_cut_fact: A Wuhan University management graduate with a master's in economics from the PBOC graduate school and a CFA charter; in a rare 2019 investor call he recalled peers mocking Greenwoods in 2012-15 as 'losing at the starting line by looking at fundamentals', and said the real risk is permanent capital loss, not volatility.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shanghai Greenwoods Asset Management (景林资产)
research_notes: Very low public profile; rarely appears in media. Best route is via Greenwoods corporate site (JS-only, no published email found). Greenwoods Asset Management HK files SEC Form ADV (CRD 161898).

name: Wu Sin-Yang
profile: Wu Sin-Yang (吳昕陽), of Taiwan's Shin Kong family, runs Shin Kong Mitsukoshi, Taiwan's largest department-store chain and a joint venture with Japan's Mitsukoshi. He became general manager in 2019, succeeding his brother Wu Hsin-ta, and later added vice chairman. He has pushed into outlets and transport-hub retail, winning the Taipei Main Station mall tender in 2026, and targets NT$100bn in sales.
interesting_fact: Under him SKM made its first move into outlet malls: Lifestyle Outlets – SKM Park, about 220 shops on 87,000 sq m on the former Caoyadao mall site in Kaohsiung, built with partner TOC.
deep_cut_fact: In 2021 he set SKM's three strategic engines as 'new businesses, new customers, new channels' (新事業、新顧客、新渠道), said more than ten expansion projects across Taiwan were under evaluation, and aimed to beat the company's NT$82bn annual sales record.
current_role: Vice Chairman and President (General Manager), Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Department Store (新光三越, SKM), Taiwan
research_notes: Hurun's 'SKM' is Shin Kong Mitsukoshi; Hurun China includes him as Taiwanese. He appears often at Taiwanese press events. Avoid raising the Feb 2025 Taichung store gas explosion. No dedicated press email published; the contact form is mainly for customers and vendors.

name: Liu Minghui
profile: Liu Minghui (Liu Ming Hui, b. June 1963) is the founder and president of China Gas Holdings, one of China's largest cross-regional city-gas distributors, piping natural gas to households and industry in hundreds of Chinese cities and expanding into LPG, integrated energy and renewables. He appears on Hurun's China and Global lists (est. ~US$1B).
interesting_fact: China Gas describes itself as China's largest cross-regional comprehensive energy supply and service provider; by its 2015 annual report it already distributed gas in 273 Chinese cities with ~38,500 employees.
current_role: Founder, chairman and president (总裁), China Gas Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 0384)
research_notes: Identity per Chinese Wikipedia disambiguation (刘明辉 1963年, 中国燃气创始人、总裁). Low international media profile. Company IR contacts are published in HKEX annual reports (site is a JS app, couldn't extract). Web search budget exhausted mid-lane, so no deep-cut fact.

name: Zhang Xiaolin
profile: Zhang Xiaolin (张晓琳) is the wife of Tan Ruiqing, longtime 5%+ shareholder and former vice-chairman of titanium-dioxide giant Lomon Billions (龙佰集团, 002601.SZ). The couple's wealth stems from their Lomon Billions stake, held directly and via Henan Yintai Investment, which Zhang co-owns. Exchange filings describe Henan Yinke International Chemical as jointly controlled by Tan and Zhang.
interesting_fact: Lomon Billions is one of the world's largest titanium dioxide producers; Tan Ruiqing's stake was about 8.3% in early 2026 before he sold ~1.35% of the company's shares via open-market trades in Feb-Mar 2026.
current_role: Co-owner (30.97%) of Henan Yintai Investment and co-controller of Henan Yinke International Chemical; director of Henan Yongxin Chemical
research_notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Identity confirmed via SZSE filings naming her as Tan Ruiqing's spouse (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2022-04-13/1212898666.PDF). Any approach would realistically go via Lomon Billions' board office / Tan Ruiqing. Alive status not explicitly confirmed, though she appears as a shareholder in a March 2026 filing.

name: Ho Tsz Wan
profile: Hong Kong-based wife of Lee Man Bun, CEO and executive director of containerboard maker Lee & Man Paper. Under Hong Kong's SFO she is deemed interested in the 1.30bn shares (30.35%) held by her husband, which is the basis of her Hurun listing shared with him; she is not an executive of the listed company herself.
interesting_fact: Lee & Man Paper's 2025 annual report lists her as a substantial shareholder deemed interested in 30.35% of the company through her husband Lee Man Bun, son of founder Lee Wan Keung.
current_role: Substantial shareholder (via spouse) of Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing (HKEX: 2314); reported director of Lee & Man Construction Holdings
public_contact: official_website: http://www.leemanpaper.com (Lee & Man Paper corporate site)
research_notes: Private individual with essentially no public profile; aggregator profiles (MarketScreener) say she was a Lee & Man Paper manager 2007-2012, a USC graduate (2003) and INED of Unipact Entertainment, unverified. Better outreach target is husband Lee Man Bun via Lee & Man Paper.

name: Niejuan
profile: Nie Juan (聂娟) co-founded the home-medical-device business that became Cofoe with her husband Zhang Min, starting with predecessor brand 'Haohushi' (好护士) in 2007. Cofoe (blood-pressure monitors, hearing aids, wheelchairs, consumables) listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2021; the couple jointly control it. She resigned as vice chair in January 2023 and is no longer an executive.
interesting_fact: Cofoe grew out of Zhang Min distributing blood-pressure monitors, wheelchairs and cupping devices before he finished junior college; at about 30 he created the Cofoe brand and moved from distribution into own-brand manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding the business, Nie Juan was a government employee: a clerk at the Yiyang Municipal Engineering Management Office (益阳市市政工程管理处) in Hunan.
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (with husband Zhang Min) of Cofoe Medical Technology (可孚医疗, SZ:301087); stepped down as vice chair in Jan 2023
research_notes: Low public profile; not an executive since 2023. Best route is Cofoe's board-secretary office (secretary Xue Xiaoqiao) via the IR email; husband Zhang Min is chairman/president.

name: Zhang Qin
profile: Zhang Qin co-founded SG Micro (圣邦微电子), a Beijing analog-chip designer started in January 2007 with chairman Zhang Shilong. It is China's No. 1 domestic analog IC company by revenue and No. 8 globally. Listed in Shenzhen (2017) and Hong Kong (2026), it is part-owned by her: she holds about 8% and belongs to the controlling group.
interesting_fact: SG Micro makes the signal-chain and power-management chips (amplifiers, converters, drivers) that sit in nearly every electronic system. 2025 revenue was about RMB 4.0bn, and Q1 2026 net profit roughly doubled year on year.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as an engineer: in July 1993 she earned an engineering bachelor's from the Beijing Institute of Light Industry (now Beijing Technology and Business University). She has been on SG Micro's board since its first month in January 2007 and has also been board secretary since 2012.
current_role: Executive Director, Vice Chairman, Deputy General Manager and Board Secretary, SG Micro Corp (300661.SZ / 03661.HK)
public_contact: ir_email: investors@sg-micro.com | contact_form: https://www.sg-micro.com/contact-us | official_website: https://www.sg-micro.com
research_notes: As board secretary she oversees SG Micro's investor relations, so the IR email effectively reaches her office. Low personal media profile. Chairman/CEO Zhang Shilong is the public face of the company.

name: Li Xing
appears_on: Hurun China (2006-2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
profile: Li Xing (b. 1971) founded Huanlejia in Zhanjiang, Guangdong in 2001 and remains chairman and co-controlling shareholder. The company began with canned fruit, seafood and quail-egg tins, and from 2014 built its 'Huanlejia' raw-pressed coconut juice into its biggest product line. It listed on ChiNext in 2021.
interesting_fact: Huanlejia moved into plant-protein drinks in 2014 when its canned-food niche plateaued; its coconut juice became the company's largest revenue source, alongside fruit canning.
current_role: Chairman, Huanlejia Food Group Co., Ltd. (Shenzhen ChiNext: 300997)
research_notes: Company bio: Chinese national with HK permanent residence, founded company 2001. Day-to-day leadership has passed to vice-chairman/president Li Zihao (from March 2025). The IR email is the board secretary's office; best route is via IR. No personal media presence found.

name: Gerald G Wong
profile: Gerald G Wong (黄钢) founded CIG in 2005-06, a Shanghai maker of optical modules and broadband/wireless equipment; it listed in Shanghai in 2017 and added a Hong Kong listing. Demand for high-speed optical modules for AI data centers has driven CIG's recent growth. He has been chairman and CEO since 2011.
interesting_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur, Wong spent 1984-2000 at AT&T Bell Labs and rose to vice president at Lucent Technologies. He has over 40 years in telecom.
deep_cut_fact: Before CIG, he co-founded Photon Bridge (光桥科技(中国)有限公司) in 2000. He holds both a bachelor's and a master's in electrical engineering and computer science from MIT, both conferred in June 1985.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Shanghai Cambridge Industries Group (CIG; SSE 603083 / HKEX 6166)
research_notes: Relevant to the data-center angle because CIG makes 800G/1.6T optical modules. The best route is the IR email or the board secretary office (board secretary: Jin Zeqing). Wong is a US/MIT-trained engineer, so outreach in English should work.

name: Wang Haijun
profile: Wang Haijun (王海军) founded Atour, China's largest mid-to-upscale hotel chain, in 2012-13 after years at Home Inns, Jinjiang Inn and as EVP of China Lodging (now H World). Atour listed on Nasdaq in 2022 and pairs hotels with a fast-growing sleep-products retail business. He is a Yanshan University graduate with a CEIBS EMBA.
interesting_fact: Atour also runs a large retail arm selling the pillows, bedding and mattresses guests use in its hotels, a key growth driver alongside its hotel network.
deep_cut_fact: Atour is named after Yaduo (亚朵) village in Nujiang, Yunnan: after leaving Hanting in 2012 Wang travelled to Bhutan and Nepal, then found in Yaduo the same simple contentment and named the brand after it. He long used the nickname 耶律胤 (Yelü Yin), a nod to his reported Khitan ancestry.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Atour Lifestyle Holdings (Nasdaq: ATAT)
public_contact: ir_email: ir@yaduo.com | pr_agency: Christensen Advisory - atour@christensencomms.com | official_website: https://ir.yaduo.com
research_notes: Hosts quarterly earnings calls in English/Chinese; IR via Christensen Advisory is the most practical route.

name: Shao Hongzhi
profile: Sha Hongzhi (沙宏志; listed by Hurun as 'Shao Hongzhi', company 'Sunlux') founded Nanjing Sunlord Electronics in August 1999 and is its legal representative and actual controller. Sunlord is one of China's leading domestic distributors of passive electronic components (60+ agency lines, 2,000+ customers); it listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Sunlord runs large bonded warehouse/logistics hubs in Nanjing, Shenzhen and Hong Kong with WMS and automatic labelling, plus subsidiaries in Singapore and Taiwan and offices in Thailand and Malaysia.
deep_cut_fact: Before its 2021 ChiNext IPO, Sunlord was first quoted on China's NEEQ 'New Third Board' in 2015; Sha holds an MBA from CEIBS.
current_role: Chairman, CEO and actual controller, Nanjing Sunlord Electronics Corp. (商络电子, SZSE: 300975)
research_notes: Correct Chinese name is 沙宏志 (Sha Hongzhi); Hurun's 'Sunlux' = Nanjing Sunlord Electronics (not Shenzhen Sunlord 002138). CEIBS MBA per MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/HONG-ZHI-SHA-A37YJ1/experience/). Best route: IR email / board secretary.

name: Jin Kun
profile: Jin Kun (靳坤) is the founder-chairman and controlling shareholder of Shanghai Beite Technology, an auto-parts maker founded in 2002 and listed in Shanghai in 2014. Beite makes steering-rack and shock-absorber piston rods, auto A/C compressors, precision parts and lightweight aluminium components. Wealth shared with Jin Xiaotang, his concert party in Beite filings.
interesting_fact: Beite's predecessor was Shanghai Beite Metal Products Co.; in 2024 Jin Kun's voting stake passively rose above 30% (triggering a takeover report) only because Beite cancelled shares returned under a performance-compensation agreement.
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Shanghai Beite Technology Group (SSE: 603009)
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal interviews found. Best route is Beite's board-secretary/IR mailbox (touzizhe@ = 'investor').

name: Jin Xiaotang
profile: Jin Xiaotang (靳晓堂) is the son of Beite founder and controlling shareholder Jin Kun, acts in concert with him, and holds ~8% of the Shanghai-listed auto-parts maker (steering rack bars, shock-absorber rods, A/C compressors, aluminium parts). He has been a director and general manager since January 2019; in 2025 the company renamed itself Shanghai Beite Technology Group.
interesting_fact: Beite is pivoting into humanoid robotics: in 2024 it set up Jiangsu Beite Robot Technology to make planetary roller screws, planning ~2.6m sets/yr in Kunshan plus a Thailand base, an RMB 1.85bn bet.
current_role: Director and General Manager, Shanghai Beite Technology Group (北特科技, SSE: 603009)
research_notes: Wealth shared with father Jin Kun (chairman, ~31.6%). Low public profile; route via company board secretary Liu Gongyou (IR email above). Role per 2024 acquisition report; check latest SSE filings to confirm GM title.

name: Jin Lianqin
profile: Jin Lianqin (金连琴), 59, is a director and co-controlling shareholder (with her husband, chairman Sun Qiuxin) of Zhenjiang-based Changqing Technology, a maker of specialty monomers and polymer additives that listed on the Shanghai main board in April 2023. She also heads Xinxin Oil Products and is GM of Zhenjiang Baoju Oil Additives.
interesting_fact: Changqing's predecessor was set up in June 2010 as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise held via a British nominee, Alan David Pow, on Sun Qiuxin's behalf to fit local investment-attraction policy; the nominee arrangement was unwound in Dec 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Before chemicals, she spent 13 years (1990-2003) as a clinical lab staffer in the testing department of the Danmian Group staff hospital, then worked in the lab of Danyang Yunyang People's Hospital until 2006.
current_role: Director and largest shareholder (~29.9%), Jiangsu Changqingshu New Materials Technology Co. (Changqing Technology, SSE: 603125)
research_notes: Hurun 'Changqing' = Changqing Technology (常青科技, 603125), not Changqing Agrochemical (002391). Low public profile; best route is the company securities office (board secretary).

name: Dai Tiantian
appears_on: Hurun China (2019-2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun China U40 (2020-2022)
profile: Dai Tiantian (b. 1983) co-founded Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) in 2007 with four Shanghai Jiao Tong University classmates; it makes the dominant laser-cutting CNC control systems and software (CypCut, TubesT) in China. He chaired the company until 2018 and is now a director, VP and software R&D chief, holding about 14% as one of five joint controllers.
interesting_fact: Friendess began in 2007 as an SJTU student startup with registered capital of just RMB 200,000; it listed on the STAR Market in 2019 among the first batch of companies and became the leading supplier of laser-cutting control systems.
deep_cut_fact: Both his bachelor's (2004) and master's (2007) degrees are from Shanghai Jiao Tong University; at founding he put in RMB 60,000 of the RMB 200,000 capital, six times each co-founder's RMB 10,000, and he holds the Chinese 'senior systems analyst' qualification.
current_role: Director, Vice President and Technical Director of Software R&D, Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology (688188.SH)
public_contact: ir_email: bochu@fscut.com | ir_email: bochu@bochu.com | official_website: https://www.fscut.com
research_notes: Male (the Hurun name can be misread). Low public profile, technical founder; chairman Tang Ye is the public face. Best route is the company IR mailbox.

name: Zhou Yong
profile: Zhou Yong (Alex Zhou) founded Linkerbot in 2023 to build low-cost, high-degree-of-freedom dexterous robotic hands (Linker Hand series) for humanoid robots and industry. Linkerbot claims >80% of the global high-DoF robotic-hand market by volume and was valued at ~US$3bn in an April 2026 round, with later reports of a ~$6bn raise.
interesting_fact: Before robotics he spent about a decade in global online communities; his previous company reached ~300 million users, less than 1% of them in China. He says: 'The hand is the last great hardware problem in robotics.'
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the Youth Class (gifted-teen program) at Huazhong University of Science and Technology at age 14; he set out to build a hand that beats the UK Shadow Hand at a fraction of the price.
current_role: Founder (described as CTO/CEO in different sources), Linkerbot (灵心巧手), Beijing
public_contact: ir_email: ir@linkerbot.cn | office_email: business@linkerbot.cn | official_website: https://www.linkerbot.cn
research_notes: Goes by Alex Zhou in English media (WIRED, Pandaily). Titles vary across sources (founder & CTO vs CEO). Very on-topic for a tech/hardware podcast; company is actively fundraising and media-facing.

name: Yi Weihua
profile: Yi Weihua (易伟华) co-founded WG Tech (沃格光电) in Xinyu, Jiangxi in December 2009 with Zhang Fujia. It started in flat-panel display glass processing, listed on the Shanghai main board in 2018, and is now pivoting to glass circuit boards (GCP) for Mini LED and semiconductor packaging. He left the board in March 2026 'for personal reasons', and Zhang Chunjiao became chairman.
interesting_fact: Yi has a technical background, and since 2019 he has personally led WG Tech's R&D push into glass-substrate circuit boards (TGV/GCP) for Mini LED backlights and advanced chip packaging. That puts the company in the glass-core substrate race relevant to AI and data-center chips.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from university in 1996, Yi started as a technician in Shenzhen and rose to manager and trader. In 2006 he started his own touch-screen sales business before founding WG Tech. He has said he wanted to 'gather a group of young people with dreams, character and ability to come together to do things that are meaningful to society.'
current_role: Co-founder and controlling shareholder, WG Tech (Jiangxi WG Optoelectronic, 603773.SH); stepped down as chairman and director in March 2026
research_notes: No longer chairman (resigned March 2026); Zhang Chunjiao (listed as sharing this wealth entry) is now chairman. In May 2026 the CSRC opened an investigation into a share-transfer disclosure, and he was fined in August 2026. Treat as sensitive and approach via company IR.

name: Zhang Chunjiao
profile: Zhang Chunjiao (张春姣, b. Dec 1972) is co-founder of WG Tech, a Xinyu, Jiangxi maker of optoelectronic glass and glass circuit plates founded in 2009 and listed in Shanghai in 2018. Her wealth (per Hurun) is shared with co-founder Yi Weihua, the former controlling shareholder. She became GM in Nov 2022 and chairman in March 2026 after Yi stepped down.
interesting_fact: WG Tech says it is one of very few companies globally with full-process capability for GCP (glass circuit plate) technology, now used for glass-core substrates for high-compute chip packaging, optical-module glass substrates and Mini/MicroLED displays — directly relevant to AI/data-center hardware.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the company she worked her way through WG Tech as assistant to the general manager, vice president, head of the marketing center and special assistant to the chairman; the company credits her with nearly 20 years in optoelectronic display and supply-chain management.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, WG Tech (JiangXi) Group Co., Ltd. (沃格光电, SSE: 603773)
research_notes: Name in filings is 张春姣 (input lists 张春娇). Board secretary is Gong Qingyu (龚庆宇); route via board office/IR email. Glass-substrate packaging angle fits the data-center theme.

name: Wan Zhijian
profile: Wan Zhijian (b. Feb 1979) is co-founder and ~18.7% shareholder of Nanchang Sanrui Intelligent Technology, a leading maker of electric propulsion systems (motors, ESCs, propellers) for drones and robot joints, also developing eVTOL power systems. He co-founded the firm in 2009 with his cousin, chairman Wu Min; it listed on ChiNext in April 2026.
interesting_fact: Sanrui sits on two Chinese policy themes at once - the low-altitude economy (drone power systems, ~49% of revenue from exports) and embodied-AI robotics via its CubeMars robot-joint brand launched in 2018; gross margin on main business was about 60% in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before drones, Wan spent a decade (July 1998 - June 2008) running an earth-and-stone haulage business, then joined his cousin's Nanchang Sanrui Technology as deputy GM in 2008. He studied rural economics at the Jiangxi Provincial Party School.
current_role: Vice Chairman (from Oct 2026), director and deputy GM, Nanchang Sanrui Intelligent Technology (301696.SZ)
research_notes: Elected vice chairman of the 2nd board on 27 Oct 2026 (cninfo 1225629729). Bound by concert-action agreement with Wu Min (cousin, controller). No personal public profile; route via company IR.

name: Sun Yaozhi
profile: Sun Yaozhi (b. 1951, Neixiang, Henan; Zhengzhou University graduate) built Wanxi Pharmaceutical in Xixia county, Nanyang, into Zhongjing Wanxi, maker of Zhongjing Liuwei Dihuang pills. He and Zhu Xincheng are the actual controllers of listed Zhongjing Food (300908.SZ); day-to-day leadership has passed to Sun Feng, chairman of Wanxi Pharma since Oct 2017.
interesting_fact: He served as a deputy to China's National People's Congress for Henan, first elected in 2008 and again in 2013 (12th NPC).
deep_cut_fact: Zhongjing Food, controlled by Sun and Zhu Xincheng, is headquartered in Xixia, billed as China's 'hometown of shiitake mushrooms'; its flagship is Zhongjing shiitake-mushroom sauce and it calls itself a partner of China's space programme.
current_role: Co-actual controller of the Wanxi group (Henan Wanxi Holdings / Zhongjing Wanxi Pharmaceutical, Zhongjing Food 300908.SZ); former chairman of Wanxi Pharmaceutical
research_notes: Listed as actual controller in Zhongjing Food's H1 2026 report (Aug 2026), but no recent public appearances found; alive status not directly confirmed. Not on the board; best route is Zhongjing Food IR / board secretary Wang Fei.

name: Lu Xinchun
profile: Tsinghua tribologist (b. 1966, Yantai) whose team began chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) research in 2000 and spun it out in 2013 as Hwatsing, now China's No.1 domestic CMP and wafer-thinning equipment maker, listed on the STAR Market in 2022. He was chairman until 2025 and remains chief scientist guiding R&D.
interesting_fact: His team launched China's first 12-inch CMP tool with domestic IP and an integrated grinding-polishing thinning tool, key equipment for chipmaking and advanced packaging; he won a 2025 Ho Leung Ho Lee Science and Technology Innovation Prize.
deep_cut_fact: An academic first: he earned his bachelor's and master's at Jilin University of Technology (1988, 1991), a PhD at the CAS Institute of Metal Research (1994), and did his postdoc at Tsinghua's State Key Laboratory of Tribology, the field of nano-scale friction behind CMP.
current_role: Chief Scientist, Hwatsing Technology (华海清科, SSE STAR: 688120); Chief Researcher, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering, Tsinghua University
research_notes: Academic-founder; stepped down as Hwatsing chairman in 2025 (Wang Tongqing is now chairman & GM) but remains chief scientist (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2273649). Routes: Hwatsing board office (secretary Chen Zhenyin) or Tsinghua Mechanical Engineering dept. Likely Chinese-language outreach needed.

name: Huang Zewei
profile: Huang Zewei (b. May 1984) built 联合创泰, a Shenzhen distributor of SK hynix memory chips. He sold it to Julong (now 香农芯创/Shannon) in a ~RMB1.6bn 2021 deal and joined its board, became co-chairman in July 2021 and chairman on 30 Oct 2025. The group's main-business revenue was ~RMB35.2bn in 2025.
interesting_fact: His business sits right in the AI/data-centre supply chain: SK hynix is Lianhe Chuangtai's core supplier, and the company sells its data-storage memory to China's leading internet firms for cloud-computing storage.
deep_cut_fact: He sold 联合创泰 twice: first to 英唐智控, then in 2020 he and partners bought 100% back for RMB1.48bn, and in 2021 he sold it again, this time to the Julong/Shannon listed vehicle for about RMB1.6bn.
current_role: Chairman, Shannon Semiconductor (香农芯创, SZSE: 300475); chairman of subsidiary 联合创泰 (Lianhe Chuangtai)
research_notes: Hurun lists the source as 'Shannon'/Retail; this is 香农芯创 (memory-chip distribution). Directly held 24.9m shares at end-2025, plus stakes through 深圳/无锡新联普 partnerships. Strong data-centre/memory angle. Best route is through the IR/board-secretary office (secretary 曾柏林).

name: Le Weiping
profile: Le Weiping (b. 1973) spent ~11 years at US plasma-power maker Advanced Energy in Shenzhen and Shanghai before founding CSL Vacuum (Hengyunchang) to localise plasma RF power systems for chip equipment. deep_cut_fact: Early in his career he was Communist Youth League secretary and deputy head of student affairs at Sinopec Changling Refinery's training centre (now Hunan Petrochemical Vocational Technology College), and is credentialed as an applied engineering research fellow.
current_role: Chairman, founder and actual controller of Qingdao Huicheng Environmental Technology Group (惠城环保, SZ300779)

name: Zheng Rong

deep_cut_fact: She joined the Ya'an Chemical Plant in 1971 as a workshop worker and worked her way up through deputy chief accountant and deputy director to factory director before leading the 2001 privatization; she is a senior economist and a Sichuan Province Model Worker.

profile: Australian-national entrepreneur (b. March 1968, master's degree) who has run Zhangjiagang-based Azure (formerly Aucksun / 澳洋顺昌) since 2007. It grew from metal-sheet logistics into LED chips and, via subsidiary Tenpower (天鹏电源), cylindrical lithium cells for power tools and small power systems. research_notes: Input 'Banma' refers to his Banma (Zebra) investment vehicle, not Alibaba's Banma auto-OS JV. Keeps a low public profile; no published personal or office contact found. Search rate limits cut research short; current Bianlifeng role not re-verified for 2026.

name: Wang Qian
profile: Wang Qian, a Tsinghua and USC-trained robotics researcher, ran a quant fund in the US before closing it in 2023 to found X Square Robot in Shenzhen. The embodied-AI startup builds general-purpose robot foundation models (WALL-A, open-sourced WALL-OSS) and reached a valuation above US$2.8bn in 2026, with backers including Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan and Xiaomi.

name: Chen Mei-chi

She was a director from 2006 until her term ended in August 2025, and she now serves as company adviser.

deep_cut_fact: Before Zhongda existed, she was finance department manager at Zhanyun Machinery (1998 to July 2006), the predecessor workshop her husband ran as managing partner. She then served as a director of Zhongda from 2006.
current_role: Co-actual controller and adviser, Ningbo Zhongda Leader Intelligent Transmission (SZSE: 002896); legal representative of controlling holder Ningbo Zhongda Lide Investment
public_contact: ir_email: china@zd-motor.com (board secretary / securities affairs) | official_website: http://www.zd-motor.com
research_notes: Low profile. The 2025 annual report lists her as company adviser and co-actual controller, so she is presumed alive. Board secretary Wu Xujun handles IR. Robotics and automation is a good podcast angle. Cen Guojian is the public face.

name: Yuan Wenjie
profile: Yuan Wenjie (袁文杰) chairs Baotou Tianhe Magnetics, an Inner Mongolia maker of sintered NdFeB and SmCo rare-earth permanent magnets for EVs, wind turbines, efficient appliances and electronics. With his sons Yuan Bo and Yuan Yi, he controls about 70% of the company, which listed on the Shanghai main board in Jan 2025.
interesting_fact: Tianhe's revenue rose from RMB 1.15bn in 2020 to RMB 2.885bn in 2022 on demand for high-performance magnets for EV motors and wind power. The company is based in Baotou's rare-earth high-tech zone.
deep_cut_fact: According to the sponsor's IPO report, a technical team centred on Yuan Wenjie has been developing and producing sintered NdFeB magnets since 1993, nearly from the start of China's rare-earth permanent-magnet industry. The company itself was founded in 2008.
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller of Baotou Tianhe Magnetics Technology Co. (SSE: 603072)
research_notes: Low media profile with no personal interviews found. He is relevant to the energy theme through magnets for wind turbines and EVs. Best route is the board secretary's office via the IR email. Not to be confused with a Dalian University of Technology professor of the same name.

name: Ding Shizhe
profile: Ding Shizhe (丁师哲, b. May 1991) is the son of Betta Pharmaceuticals founder Ding Lieming, maker of Conmana (icotinib), China's first home-grown small-molecule lung-cancer targeted drug; Hurun lists the family's stake jointly. A Saint Louis University graduate (biochemistry + economics), he joined Betta and rose through strategic partnerships to the board in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: He handles Betta's in-licensing and business development: he pushed through the MCLA-129 and ensartinib projects, struck partnerships with InventisBio and Agenus, and led Betta's equity investment in US cancer-drug developer Xcovery.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Saint Louis University in the US with a combined biochemistry-and-economics background, and served as executive deputy GM of 'Betta Dream Factory' (贝达梦工场), the company's incubator platform.

research_notes: Father-son relationship per media reports of company filings (https://m.jiemian.com/article/14889899.html). Wealth is family-held with Ding Lieming, who is the actual controller. Contact via Betta IR.

name: Lyu Gang
profile: Born 1962, Lyu Gang has run Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical, a Xinchang-born drugmaker now based in Hangzhou, since its days as Zhejiang Xinchang Jingxin Pharma; he has been chairman since 2004 when it listed in Shenzhen. With his wife he controls ~36% of the company, which focuses on CNS and cardio/cerebrovascular drugs (2025 revenue RMB4.07bn) and is seeking a second listing in Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Jingxin's only approved innovative drug is the insomnia treatment dimdazenil (Jingnuoning); it is also developing JX2201 for elevated lipoprotein(a), and is pursuing an HKEX dual listing with CITIC Securities as sole sponsor.
deep_cut_fact: His formal education started with a mechanical-engineering associate degree from Zhejiang Radio & TV University (1987); he later did Peking University Guanghua's EMBA (2000) and a China Pharmaceutical University pharmacy certificate (2004), and earned senior-economist title in Dec 2022.
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical (002020.SZ; Hong Kong H-share listing filed Sept 2026)

name: Wang Donghai
profile: Wang Donghai (b. ~1965) is the founder and controlling shareholder of Bestsun Energy (Baichuan), a city-gas distributor based in Langfang, Hebei, with pipeline gas, LNG and gas-station operations around Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and in Hubei. He has built Baichuan's businesses since 1992 and remains chairman and general manager of the listed company.
interesting_fact: Bestsun is a family-controlled listed gas utility: Wang is the actual controller via Langfang Baichuan Asset Management, and he founded both an urban-construction developer and the gas company before taking it public.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent eight years (1984-1992) working at the Yongqing County Economic Commission in Hebei; he later served as a vice-chair of the Yongqing county CPPCC and a member of the Hebei provincial CPPCC.
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Bestsun Energy (Baichuan Energy, SSE: 600681); chairman, Baichuan Investment Group
research_notes: Bestsun Energy = Baichuan Energy (百川能源). Published board-office email (board secretary Li Simeng) is the best route. Little English-language coverage.

name: Gao Jianrong

Zhongyin built a Suzhou-area real estate business and around 2007-08 took over listed shell S*ST Tianhua, renamed Zhongyin Co. (600745), which in 2015-16 swapped out property assets for Wingtech's phone ODM business.
interesting_fact: The listed company Zhongyin took control of around 2008 (S*ST Tianhua, later Zhongyin Co.) is today Wingtech Technology, one of China's largest smartphone ODMs and owner of chipmaker Nexperia.
current_role: Chairman / actual controller, Tibet Zhongyin Group (西藏中茵集团, 'Join In'), a Suzhou-based property and investment group
research_notes: Hurun 'Joinin' = 中茵 Zhongyin/Join In. Very low public profile; little biographical info online (ChinaVitae reportedly lists him as born 1963 in Zhejiang, but I could not open the page to verify). (600745) and its Suzhou-area property business until it was reverse-merged into Wingtech Technology in 2016; Gao exited most of his stake in 2017. name: Shao Xionghui
profile: Shao Xionghui (邵雄辉, b. 1976) controls Shanghai Zhaomin (Hurun English 'Hajime'), a ChiNext-listed maker of precision engineering-plastic parts for auto powertrain, thermal-management and appliance systems. He joined its Japanese-invested predecessor Zhaomin Precision Plastics in 2003, rose to general manager, took over the business in 2012 and has been chairman and GM since 2019; re-elected June 2025.
interesting_fact: He started out in tourism, not manufacturing: from 1996 to 2003 he worked in the Japan department of Hunan Huatian International Travel Service, rising to deputy head, before moving into the Japanese-founded plastics firm he would later own.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he spent seven years (1996-2003) at Hunan Huatian International Travel Service's Japan department, going from staff member to deputy department head; his Japan background carried into Zhaomin Precision Plastics (Shanghai), where he worked his way up from manufacturing-department head.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai Zhaomin New Material Technology (肇民科技, SZSE: 301000)

name: Jiang Yongzhong

interesting_fact: Silan is one of China's few privately founded IDM chipmakers, designing and fabricating its own power devices and ICs, and is controlled jointly by its seven founders alongside China's national 'Big Fund' as a major shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs Hangzhou Mecarel (美卡乐) Optoelectronics, Silan's LED-packaging subsidiary building a premium 'Mecarel' brand of high-reliability LED display pixel tubes; its revenue grew about 48% in 2024.

He joined in 1998 and rose from vice GM to executive vice GM to vice chairman, a role he still holds; he owns roughly 72 million shares.
interesting_fact: Oriental Yuhong, founded in 1995 and listed in Shenzhen in 2008, has gone global: it set up a plant in Trinidad and Tobago with Lake Asphalt (2013) and broke ground on a factory and logistics centre in Prairie View, Texas in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond waterproofing, he has been executive director of a Beijing film and TV media company, Beijing Xingle Yinghua Film & Television Culture Media, since 2011, and was a director of environmental firm Beijing GeoEnviron (高能环境) from 2002 to 2009.
current_role: Vice Chairman and Director, Beijing Oriental Yuhong Waterproof Technology Co. (SZSE: 002271)
research_notes: Low media profile compared with chairman/founder Li Weiguo. Best route is the board secretary's office (stocks@yuhong.com.cn).

name: Zheng Shaobo
profile: Zheng Shaobo (郑少波) is one of seven co-founders of Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, who act together as its controlling group under chairman Chen Xiangdong. Silan is a major Chinese maker of power semiconductors, analog ICs and MEMS, now expanding into silicon-carbide chips for EVs.
interesting_fact: Silan has moved fast into silicon carbide: it began building a SiC power-device line in 2022, passed 5,000 wafers a month by 2024, and is building an 8-inch SiC line in Xiamen planned for 720,000 wafers a year.
deep_cut_fact: Silan began in 1997 as Hangzhou Silan Electronics, founded by Zheng and six colleagues: Chen Xiangdong, Fan Weihong, Jiang Zhongyong, Luo Huabing, Song Weiquan and Chen Guohua. All seven are still named together as the company's controlling group almost three decades later.
current_role: Director, Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (600460.SH); director of affiliate Shiteng Technology
research_notes: Low-profile engineer-founder; Chairman Chen Xiangdong is the public face. Approach through Silan's securities affairs office (IR email published in shareholder-meeting notices). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Chen Qiong

The firm began as a drug maker in the early 1990s and pivoted to nutraceuticals after 2000; it calls itself the world's No.2 gummy and softgel solutions provider, earns 60%+ of revenue abroad and filed for a Hong Kong listing in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Sirio ranks third globally in nutrition-and-health-food solutions by 2024 revenue, and is building a plant in Thailand (due 2027) with planned capacity of 2.4 billion gummies a year.
deep_cut_fact: A pharmacist by training (master's degree), she started as a formulation researcher at the research institute of the Tuobin pharmaceutical factory in Shantou, then was quality head at Shantou Meiji Pharmaceutical before co-running Sirio.
current_role: Director and Deputy General Manager, Sirio Pharma Co., Ltd. (仙乐健康, SZSE: 300791), Shantou

name: Su Zengfu
profile: Born c.1940-41 in Yuhuan, Zhejiang, Su rose from supply clerk to director of a township pressure-cooker parts factory, then in 1994 co-founded cookware brand Supor with his son Su Xianze; it listed in Shenzhen in 2004 and became China's top pressure-cooker brand. The family sold control to France's Groupe SEB from 2006-2011 and Su moved into stainless faucets, pharma, ports, logistics and property.

research_notes: Now about 85-86; no recent (2024-26) news found and no death report found, so alive status unverified. No published personal/office contact; family no longer tied to listed Supor (chaired by SEB's Thierry de La Tour d'Artaise). Son Su Xianze is the more public family member.

name: Chen Haibin
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur (b. 1969, CEIBS EMBA) who started a diagnostics business in 1996 and founded Dian in 2001; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2011 and grew into one of China's largest independent clinical laboratory networks, combining lab services with IVD product distribution. Chairman since 2019 (previously also GM); remains the controlling shareholder as of 2026.

current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Dian Diagnostics Group (迪安诊断, SZSE: 300244), Hangzhou
research_notes: Former Zhejiang CPPCC member; chairs the Zhejiang Health Industry Federation. IR/board secretary (Tao Jun) is the realistic route; Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Gao Lufeng

current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Segway-Ninebot (九号公司, SSE STAR: 689009)

name: Jiang Chun
profile: Jiang Chun (姜纯), born 1960 in Wuhu, has spent 40+ years in copper processing. He built Truchum (楚江新材) into a major maker of copper strip, wire and specialty alloys, later expanding into carbon-fiber composites and high-end equipment via acquisitions; he is the controlling shareholder and chairman.
interesting_fact: Jiang has used acquisitions as Truchum's main growth engine, steering a traditional copper-processing business into advanced materials such as carbon-fiber composites for aerospace.

current_role: Chairman, Anhui Truchum Advanced Materials & Technology (Chujiang New Materials, SZSE: 002171), Wuhu

name: Xu Xinjian
profile: Founder of the Sunrain (太阳雨) and Micoe (四季沐歌) brands. He built Solareast, based in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, from a small workshop into one of China's largest solar water-heater makers. It is listed in Shanghai, also owns the kitchen-appliance brand Sacon (帅康), and has been moving into air-source heat pumps and other low-carbon heating.
interesting_fact: His solar-thermal company grew from a small workshop in Lianyungang into a leader of China's solar water-heater industry, the world's largest. Its brands Sunrain and Micoe became household names.

current_role: Chairman, Solareast Holdings (日出东方, 603366.SS) and its controlling shareholder Sunrain Holding Group (太阳雨控股集团)

Kexing makes recombinant-protein drugs.

It traces back to a 1989 Shenzhen venture set up to commercialise the work of academician Hou Yunde, the 'father of Chinese interferon'. That venture's vaccine arm became the separate Sinovac.

current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Kexing Biopharm (科兴制药, SSE STAR: 688136)

name: Que Weidong

Quechen listed in Shanghai in December 2020; he remains general manager.

current_role: General Manager and Director, Quechen Silicon Chemical Co. (605183.SH, Wuxi); previously also chairman

He has been chairman and GM since 2020.

name: Wang Bingkun
profile: Born in 1972 in Houjie, Dongguan, a furniture hub, Wang started out distributing furniture brands. In 2004 he put in all his savings plus loans from relatives and friends to co-found the mattress brand De Rucci with Lin Jiyong. It became China's top-selling mattress brand, has 1,400+ stores and listed in Shenzhen in 2022.
interesting_fact: De Rucci opened 600+ stores in its first five years. In 2010 it opened what it calls China's first private 'healthy sleep' club, and it set up a German subsidiary in 2014.

current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & General Manager, De Rucci Healthy Sleep Co. (慕思股份, SZSE: 001323)

interesting_fact: De Rucci built one of China's largest mattress retail networks (about 4,200 shops in 2020) plus showcase facilities outside China within ~16 years of founding.

profile: Shanghai-born Hong Kong resident Tang Jianxing (b. 1957) joined DBG Technology in Daya Bay, Huizhou as a minority shareholder in 1998 and grew it from a single-customer SMT assembly shop into an EMS provider for Huawei, Xiaomi, Samsung, Honor and others, now ranked about 14th globally. It is expanding into automotive electronics, including via the acquisition of France's All Circuits.
interesting_fact: Tang says DBG's goal is to break into the global top 10 EMS providers within 3-5 years, explicitly benchmarking itself against Jabil; the company celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a salesman at Shanghai's No. 1 Commerce Bureau (1975-82), and in May 1984 was posted by Sanyo to Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei, rising to factory manager over a decade; when the cassette-recorder business collapsed in 1997 he put his severance money into DBG.
current_role: Chairman, CEO and general manager, Huizhou DBG Technology Co. (SZSE: 300735)
research_notes: Gave a long 30th-anniversary interview to China Securities Journal (2025), so open to press. Route via board office email. Avoid the 2000s shareholder-control dispute mentioned in profiles.

name: Luo Huabing
profile: Luo Huabing (罗华兵) is one of seven co-founders of Silan Microelectronics, a Hangzhou-based chip designer and maker of power semiconductors (IGBT, MOSFET, SiC, IPM). The seven, led by chairman Chen Xiangdong, are jointly the company's actual controllers. He remained a director as of 2025 filings.
interesting_fact: Silan has become one of China's fastest-moving silicon-carbide players. It started a SiC power-device line in 2022 and by 2024 had capacity above 5,000 wafers a month, serving the EV, solar/storage and industrial markets.
deep_cut_fact: In 1997 Luo was one of six colleagues who joined Chen Xiangdong, then a senior executive at Huayue Microelectronics, in founding Hangzhou Silan Electronics, the forerunner of today's Silan Microelectronics.
current_role: Director and one of the seven joint actual controllers, Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (600460.SH)
research_notes: Low public profile, and almost all coverage focuses on chairman Chen Xiangdong. His June 2025 share-reduction filing confirms he is still a director. Formal route: the Silan board secretary / IR office.

name: Lin Qibin
profile: Lin Qibin (林启彬), a Taiwanese entrepreneur born in 1953, founded Changchun Engley, a maker of lightweight car-body structural and crash-management parts for premium carmakers. He was executive director/chairman from the company's founding until 2022 and now sits on the board, alongside running Changchun Hongyun Yunduan Technology and chairing holding vehicle Engley Industrial (Cayman).
interesting_fact: Engley supplies body and crash-safety parts to FAW-Volkswagen, Beijing Benz, Volvo Asia Pacific, BMW Brilliance, SAIC-VW, SAIC-GM, Geely and Hongqi, focusing on vehicle lightweighting.
deep_cut_fact: He is a graduate of Ta Hwa University of Science and Technology (大华科技大学) in Hsinchu, Taiwan, and built his auto-parts business in Changchun, home of FAW.
current_role: Director (founder, former chairman), Changchun Engley Automobile Industry Co. (英利汽车, SSE STAR: 688584)
research_notes: Taiwan national, age 73 per 2025 annual report. Stepped back from chairman role in 2022; control now with the next generation of management. Very low media profile; IR email is the practical route.
