research_notes: Non-executive, low-profile. Holdings: Chen Wenbin 36.14%, Yan Ming 23.72%, Chen Ningfeng 21.10% (May 2025 HKEX circular). Deep-cut source is an aggregator (MarketScreener); verify before use. Education per company site: finance BA (Shanxi Univ. of Finance & Economics), EMBA (CKGSB).

name: Guo Li
profile: Guo Li (郭力) appears on Hurun (2015-2021) as a CDH Investments shareholder. Aggregator profiles describe a Ms. Guo Li who joined CDH in its founding year (2002) and serves as CFO of CDH Investments Management (HK). She previously worked at Arthur Andersen (1997-2001), is a CPA and graduated from the Central University of Finance and Economics.
interesting_fact: CDH grew out of the direct-investment department of China International Capital Corp (CICC). It was spun out in 2002 by six founders led by Wu Shangzhi and Jiao Zhen, with GIC, China Investment Guarantee and Zurich Capital, and became one of China's largest PE firms.
current_role: Reported CFO / early partner, CDH Investments (鼎晖投资)
research_notes: Identity only moderately confirmed: the CFO background comes from data aggregators (mergr.com, marketscreener), not an official CDH page. Very low profile. Any approach would go through CDH corporate channels (cdhfund.com).

name: Ji Yue
profile: Ji Yue (计越) has been a venture investor in China since 1999, working at Walden International, Vertex Management and CIV before joining Sequoia Capital China as a TMT partner. He led or participated in deals including Dianping (Sequoia was its only Series A investor), Ele.me, Tuniu, Ganji, Douban, Noah Wealth and Maple Leaf Education, plus AI-era bets such as 4Paradigm and Sensors Data.
interesting_fact: Sequoia was Dianping's sole Series A investor — a bet Ji Yue was involved in that later became part of Meituan-Dianping.
deep_cut_fact: He said he would rather spend an hour trying a product as a 'novice user' than sit through an hour-long meeting he doesn't understand, and that investors should never be in the spotlight (36Kr Open Day, Shanghai, 2013).
current_role: Partner, Sequoia Capital China (now HSG/HongShan), TMT investing; current title not confirmed in 2024-26 sources
research_notes: Self-described as preferring to stay out of the spotlight; no personal channels found. A 'Yue Ji' linked to Hongshan sits on GalaxyCore's board per aggregator data (unverified). Best route likely via HSG.

name: Ge Yaolun
profile: Ge Yaolun (about 65) founded Qingdao-based Hailir, a crop-protection (pesticide) maker, after a career in Laixi's rural supply cooperatives and agri-input firms. He chaired the company through its Shanghai listing (SSE: 603639); his son Ge Jiacheng is now chairman and GM, and Ge, his wife Zhang Aiying and son jointly control the group.
interesting_fact: Hailir is a family-controlled pesticide group from Laixi, Qingdao; Ge stepped back to 'lifetime honorary chairman' and handed the chairmanship and CEO role to his son Ge Jiacheng, a former accountant at Alcatel-Lucent's Qingdao unit.
deep_cut_fact: Ge began as head of the fruit station at the Tangjiazhuang supply-and-marketing cooperative in Laixi, then deputy director of the Wangcheng co-op, and ran the fruit company of Qingdao Dongfang Peanut Group before moving into agrochemicals.
current_role: Director and lifetime honorary chairman, Hailir Pesticides and Chemicals Group (SSE: 603639)
research_notes: Largely retired from operations; son Ge Jiacheng (chairman/GM) is the active leader. Outreach is better via the company board office.

name: Guo Peng
profile: Hurun lists Guo Peng (郭鹏) as the owner behind Puyang Iron and Steel, the private Hebei Puyang Iron & Steel (part of Hebei Puyang Industrial Group) in Yangyi Town, Wu'an, Handan. In 2020 it was named one of the five groups into which Wu'an planned to consolidate its 14 steelmakers. No public source found confirming his title.
interesting_fact: In Wu'an's 2020 consolidation plan, which merged 14 local steel companies into five groups, Puyang Iron and Steel was chosen as one of the five surviving group platforms.
research_notes: Could not confirm his role. Baidu and the company site (pygt.cn) were unreachable. His last Hurun appearance was 2021. The company is private and unlisted, so it has no IR channel. Verify through a Chinese corporate registry before outreach. Low-priority, very private.

name: Li Xianhua
profile: Born 1974; co-founded JinkoSolar in 2006 with brother Li Xiande and Chen Kangping, first to supply wafers to elder brother Li Xianshou's ReneSola. As first GM he ran production and quality; Jinko became the world's top module shipper. He remains a director and one of three founders jointly controlling ~55% via Jinko Investment.
interesting_fact: The Li brothers' 'iron triangle' (Li Xiande on strategy, Li Xianhua on manufacturing and process quality, Chen Kangping on finance) ran Jinko for ~20 years, taking it to NYSE in 2010 and STAR Market in 2022; a Jinko executive called Li Xianhua 'a technical expert, very professional in production management and quality control'.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he ran a car-repair business; in 2006 he and Li Xiande sold their own assets to register Desheng Solar and Jinko Energy, and before that he managed Yuhuan Sunshine Energy (2000-06), his elder brother's early solar firm.
current_role: Co-founder and director, JinkoSolar (晶科能源, SSE 688223) and JinkoSolar Holding (NYSE: JKS); director of Jinko Power (晶科科技)
public_contact: ir_email: ir@jinkosolar.com (JinkoSolar Holding investor & media inquiries) | official_website: https://www.jinkosolar.com/en
research_notes: Hurun lists Chinese name as 李先华 but company filings use 李仙华 (same Jinko co-founder). Very low public profile, no personal channels; route via JinkoSolar IR/board office. Jinko Holding approved renaming to 'Jinko Holdings Limited' (Oct 2026). Avoid elder brother Li Xianshou topic.

name: Li Shilun
profile: Li Shilun (李世伦), born 1962 and holding a PhD in engineering, spent 1988-2022 at Zhejiang University's School of Mechanical Engineering. He was part of the academic group behind Jingsheng M&E, which makes crystal-growth furnaces and equipment for solar and semiconductor silicon and SiC. His wealth comes from his stake in Jingsheng Investment, the controlling holding company.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng grew out of Zhejiang University's mechanical engineering school. Several founders and directors are ZJU professors, and it became one of China's main suppliers of monocrystalline silicon growth furnaces for the solar industry.
deep_cut_fact: He taught and did research at Zhejiang University's School of Mechanical Engineering for 34 years (Aug 1988-Jul 2022) before retiring. He was a Jingsheng director 2010-2015 and chaired its supervisory board from Dec 2019.
current_role: Director of Shaoxing Shangyu Jingsheng Investment (controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical, SZSE: 300316); retired Zhejiang University professor
research_notes: Academic co-founder rather than an operator. He no longer appears among listed-company officers in the 2025 annual report, probably because China's 2024 Company Law changes led many firms to abolish supervisory boards. Highly relevant to the solar and semiconductor equipment theme. Route is via the company securities office.

name: Mao Quanlin
profile: Mao Quanlin (毛全林, b. 1970) is a co-founding executive and shareholder of Jingsheng, the Shaoxing-based maker of crystal-growth furnaces and equipment for solar-grade silicon, semiconductors and silicon carbide. He has been a director and (senior) vice president since 2010, focused on production management; his wealth comes from Jingsheng shares held directly (~0.8%) and through the founders' holding vehicle.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng is a core supplier of the monocrystalline silicon furnaces behind China's solar boom and has expanded into SiC substrates and semiconductor equipment, directly relevant to energy and chip supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: His formal schooling stopped at junior middle school (初中), yet he rose on production-management experience to the board of a high-tech equipment maker and shares a Zhejiang Provincial Science & Technology Award (first prize).
current_role: Director and Vice President, Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical Co. (晶盛机电, SZSE: 300316)
research_notes: Not the controller (Cao Jianwei / Qiu Minxiu are). Low public profile; route via Jingsheng board office. Good fit for an energy-focused show (solar/SiC equipment).

name: Xiao Zhengqiang
profile: Born 1971 in Henan, Xiao Zhengqiang and his brother Xiao Gaoqiang (general manager) built Luoyang Xinqianglian into a maker of large slewing bearings, wind-turbine main-shaft bearings and tunnel-boring-machine bearings, supplying wind OEMs such as Mingyang and Envision. Listed on ChiNext in 2020; he has been chairman since 2016.
interesting_fact: Xinqianglian's growth came from localising large wind-turbine main-shaft bearings, long dominated by foreign suppliers, as Chinese wind OEMs pushed domestic sourcing.
deep_cut_fact: Before bearings, he spent 13 years (1992-2005) as deputy head then head of the expatriate camp of French contractor Dumez on Lot 3 of the Xiaolangdi Dam on the Yellow River, after starting as a purchasing supervisor for the Xiaolangdi services company in 1990. He has a high-school education.
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller, Luoyang Xinqianglian Slewing Bearing (300850.SZ, ChiNext)
research_notes: Strong fit for energy (wind) angle. Route via board secretary Kou Congmei's office.

name: Gao Qiang
profile: Gao Qiang (b. 1973), a Hong Kong University chemistry PhD, co-founded Shanghai Haoyuan Chemexpress in 2006 with fellow HKU chemist Zheng Baofu. The company sells life-science research reagents (MedChemExpress brand) and provides APIs/intermediates and CDMO services; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Gao serves as director and deputy GM.
interesting_fact: Haoyuan's catalogue of intermediates covers key building blocks for drugs such as ticagrelor, palbociclib and lenacapavir, while its reagent arm supplies labs worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a chemistry master's at Lanzhou University (1999) and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (2004), worked as an HKU chemistry researcher until 2006, then founded the company within months of leaving academia.
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Deputy General Manager, Shanghai Haoyuan Chemexpress (皓元医药, SH:688131); co-actual controller with chairman Zheng Baofu
public_contact: ir_email: hy@chemexpress.com | office_email: info@chemexpress.com | official_website: https://www.chemexpress.com.cn
research_notes: Scientist-founder, low media profile; chairman Zheng Baofu is the main public face. Hurun lists wealth shared with Liu Yan. IR phone 021-58338205 published.

name: Qiu Jiajun
profile: Qiu Jiajun (b. 1965), a China Pharmaceutical University graduate and senior engineer, worked at Zhejiang Xinchang Pharmaceutical Factory from 1988 to 1996 before founding Guobang in 1996 as a small county plant making feed additives and veterinary drugs. It grew into a global supplier of antibiotic APIs, intermediates and animal-health products and listed in Shanghai in August 2021, with Qiu still chairman.
interesting_fact: Guobang started in animal health because that market was less crowded, then moved into human APIs; it has ranked among China's top 100 pharmaceutical manufacturers for ten consecutive years (2016–2025).
deep_cut_fact: The company name comes from the phrase 立人立国，兴业兴邦 ('build people, build the nation; grow industry, strengthen the country'). Qiu likens routine products to home cooking and new drugs to fine dishes: you have to master the basics before you can innovate.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guobang Pharma Ltd. (国邦医药, SSE: 605507), Xinchang, Zhejiang
research_notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Chen Jingjing. Board secretary is 彭德光 (per cninfo). Best route is Guobang's investor-relations/securities office.

name: Chen Jingjing
profile: Chen Jingjing (陈晶晶) and her husband, chairman Qiu Jiajun, are the actual controllers of Guobang Pharma, a Xinchang, Zhejiang-based maker of active pharmaceutical ingredients, veterinary APIs and chemical intermediates, listed in Shanghai in 2021. She holds no executive post; her stake is held largely through Xinchang Qingyu Investment Development, which she controls.
interesting_fact: Guobang is one of the world's largest suppliers of macrolide and quinolone antibiotic APIs and China's largest producer of intermediates such as sodium borohydride, selling to 117 countries; its subsidiary helped draft standards for the Chinese Veterinary Pharmacopoeia.
current_role: Co-actual controller of Guobang Pharma (国邦医药, 605507.SH) with husband Qiu Jiajun; controls Xinchang Qingyu Investment Development
research_notes: Annual report lists her occupation as 'none' (no executive role); husband Qiu Jiajun is the public face and best contact route via Guobang IR. No interviews or personal channels found.

name: Quan Qiuhong
profile: Born 1970, Quan Qiuhong (female) founded Beijing BGT International Environmental Technology in 2004 after a decade in water-treatment sales and management in Zhengzhou; BGT listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext and specialises in industrial water treatment and zero-discharge reuse of high-salinity wastewater. The company has since expanded into salt-lake lithium extraction and mineral development.
interesting_fact: BGT's core technology recovers resources from high-salt industrial wastewater (e.g. from coal-chemical plants), and it has pivoted that know-how into salt-lake lithium extraction, an energy-transition angle.
deep_cut_fact: She started out in 1995 as the Central China sales agent for Peninsula (半岛) Water Treatment, then became deputy GM (Hong Kong side representative) of its Zhengzhou JV and ran Zhengzhou Dahe Water Treatment Equipment before founding BGT in 2004.
current_role: Chairwoman, controlling shareholder and founder, BGT Group (倍杰特, SZSE: 300774)
research_notes: Hurun's 'BGT' = 倍杰特 (identified via cninfo filings). Water/lithium angle relevant to energy and data-center cooling topics. Route via company board office.

name: Xia Jun
profile: Xia Jun (夏军, b. 1975) has run Shenzhen Create Century Machinery, a maker of CNC machine tools such as drilling/tapping and machining centres used in electronics and auto-parts production, since 2005. The listed company Jinsheng Precision acquired Create Century around 2015-2016 and later refocused on it; Xia became the controlling figure and chairman, and the group was renamed Create Century. He co-holds his stake with Ling Hui.
interesting_fact: Listed company Jinsheng (劲胜), originally a phone-casing maker, bought Create Century to pivot into high-end CNC machine tools; it eventually shed the old business and took Create Century's name, with Xia taking control around 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Xia started out as a salesman (业务员) and later a manager at Zhuhai Beisute (珠海倍速特) enterprise group before becoming executive director and GM of Shenzhen Create Century Machinery in December 2005. He completed an EMBA programme at Tsinghua.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Guangdong Create Century Intelligent Equipment Group (创世纪, SZ:300083)
research_notes: Best route is the board-secretary office (secretary Wu Yongbing) via ir@szccm.com. 2026 press coverage includes a patent dispute and a CSRC Guangdong warning letter on disclosure; avoid those topics.

name: Ling Hui
profile: Ling Hui is the wife and acting-in-concert party of Xia Jun, chairman and GM of Create Century (创世纪), a Shenzhen/Dongguan maker of CNC machine tools and drilling/tapping centres for 3C electronics and general industry. Her wealth (listed jointly with Xia Jun) comes from their stake in the company. She does not appear to hold an executive role.
interesting_fact: Create Century's CNC machining centres are widely used to make smartphone and laptop casings. Xia Jun began as a salesman at Zhuhai Beisuite before running Shenzhen Create Century Machinery from 2005.
current_role: Shareholder and person acting in concert with her husband Xia Jun, controller of Guangdong Create Century Intelligent Equipment Group (300083.SZ)
research_notes: Private, non-executive; media coverage of her is limited to share-sale disclosures (e.g. 2024 reduction, per NBD https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2025-02-26/3767697.html). Better to approach Xia Jun via company IR.

name: Zhang Yingjiu
profile: Zhang Yingjiu (张迎九, b. 1969) co-founded Yangling Metron in Shaanxi in 2015 with Wu Ying and others. Metron makes the electroplated diamond wire used to slice silicon wafers for solar panels and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020. He was its second-largest shareholder, and his stake drove his Hurun ranking in 2020-21. He also left the company's board.
interesting_fact: Metron's diamond wire is an unglamorous but critical input to the solar boom. It is used to saw polysilicon ingots into the thin wafers in most of the world's PV panels.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serving physics professor at Zhengzhou University's School of Physics and Engineering. Metron's prospectus credits the 'Jia Haibo and Zhang Yingjiu team' with being first in the industry to launch multi-wire diamond-wire production equipment ('one machine, six wires'), which raised output per machine.
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (about 12.6% in 2025), Yangling Metron New Material (美畅股份, SZSE 300861); professor, School of Physics and Engineering, Zhengzhou University
research_notes: A scientist-investor who gives almost no interviews. In 2025 he disclosed plans to sell part of his stake (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202505201676133954_1.pdf). Relevant to the energy/solar angle. Possible routes are the Metron board secretary office or his Zhengzhou University faculty page, but no published personal email was found.

current_role: None - former chairwoman of Changsheng Bio-technology (delisted); serving a life sentence

name: Zhu Yuguo
profile: Zhu Yuguo (朱玉国) founded Shandong Changxing Group in 1986; it became China's largest maker of vacuum couch rolls, a key part of paper machines. Forbes China ranked him No.102 in 2006 (RMB5.71bn).
interesting_fact: He planned to both build and operate turbines - up to 100 x 50MW wind farms over 5-10 years - arguing that owning the whole chain could cut a wind farm's payback to about three years.
deep_cut_fact: His case for wind was blunt: coal will run out one day, so new energy is the long bet - he said this while still running one of China's top paper-machinery component businesses.

deep_cut_fact: He chaired Shanghai Hanbell for 17 years (1994-2011), then served as a director until 2020; he controls it through a chain running from Hanbell Investment Holding (Taiwan) via BVI and Panamanian holding companies.
current_role: Actual controller of Shanghai Hanbell Precise Machinery (SZSE: 002158) via Taiwan's Hanbell Investment Holding; chairman 1994-2011, director 2011-2020
research_notes: Taiwanese national, listed under China by Hurun. No longer on the Shanghai Hanbell board; the Taiwan parent (Hanbell Precise Machinery, Taoyuan) may be a better route. Romanised name may appear as Liao Che-Nan.

name: Xu Ligang
profile: Xu Ligang (徐立刚, mid-40s) holds a PhD in power electronics from Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and co-founded Nanjing-based X-chip in 2018 with fellow NUAA alumnus Wen Zhenlin. X-chip designs high-reliability analog power-management chips and DC/DC micro-modules; it listed on ChiNext on 7 Aug 2026 and surged ~360% on debut.
interesting_fact: X-chip's IPO priced at 23.45 yuan and opened 360% higher on day one (peaking near 129.90 yuan), making Xu and co-founder Wen Zhenlin newly minted chip billionaires in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding X-chip he worked as an engineer at Shenzhen Qingxuan Electronics and at Silergy's Hangzhou arm, then ran the Zhuzhou Zhanxin business unit; X-chip's leadership and independent directors are largely fellow NUAA power-electronics alumni.
current_role: Co-founder, co-controlling shareholder, Director & General Manager, Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor (展芯股份, SZSE ChiNext: 301707), Nanjing
research_notes: Hurun 'X-Chip' = 江苏展芯半导体 (Zhanxin). Chairman is co-founder Wen Zhenlin; Xu is GM. Company focuses on military/high-reliability power chips, so expect low media appetite. Route via IR email.

name: Xie Shuli
profile: Xie Shuli (b. 1972), a Tongji University chemistry graduate, built Shanghai YCT Electronics from a component trading firm (run as GM from 2001) into a listed authorised distributor of electronic components, largely for automotive customers, which now also designs its own analog and mixed-signal chips (power management, drivers, automotive CIS). He controls about 52% of the company.
interesting_fact: YCT has moved up the value chain from pure distribution into in-house chip design (power-management, signal-chain and mixed-signal SoCs), alongside distributing memory, MCUs and passives.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in chemistry from Tongji University in 1996, his first job was as a sales manager at Shantou Ultrasonic printed-circuit-board company (1996-99), before he became a director of Hong Kong Taixin and later GM of Shanghai YCT.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai YCT Electronics Group (Yachuang Dianzi, SZSE: 301099)
research_notes: Hurun's 'YCL' appears to be YCT (Shanghai Yct Electronics, 雅创电子); name and Chinese characters match the chairman/controller. Board secretary/CFO: Fan Xiaolei. Web search budget ran out; bio from exchange-disclosed data.

name: Wu Hehong
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Xinrui' (China). Not researched: the lane's web-search quota ran out before this person was reached, and direct fetches of likely company sites returned nothing usable.
research_notes: Needs a follow-up pass. Search the Chinese name plus the company (Xinrui) on the exchange filings (SSE/SZSE/HKEXnews) to confirm identity, role and the company's IR email.

name: Wang Zhangxing
profile: Wang Zhangxing, from Shaoxing, Zhejiang, started in construction contracting and in January 2001 founded Shanghai Jiashijia Holding. The private group centres on self-operated commercial property (building-materials and home-furnishing malls, department stores, hotels) and expanded into developments in Beijing, Zhengzhou, Chengdu and Urumqi in the mid-2000s.
interesting_fact: He was ranked in the Hurun Rich List top 50 in 2005, and has appeared on Hurun China lists from 2005 through 2026.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999 he bought a former pharmaceutical warehouse on Shanghai's Yishan Road for RMB 36m to build housing. When a tenant offered RMB 10m a year in rent, he turned it into the Jiashijia building-materials mall, which grew from 15,000 to 60,000 sq m.
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Jiashijia Holding (Group) Co. (per a dated profile; current status unverified)
research_notes: The list's 'City' source of wealth is assumed to refer to Jiashijia's mall/'city' business, so the match is probable but not certain. The profile dates from about 2005-06. He has been president of the Shaoxing Enterprises Association in Shanghai. No published contacts found; private group.

name: Wan Zhang
profile: Wan Zhang (万章) is one of five co-founders of Shanghai Friendess (柏楚电子), a spin-out of Shanghai Jiao Tong University founded in 2007 that dominates China's market for fiber-laser cutting CNC control systems. The company listed on the STAR Market in 2019; the five founders jointly control it, with Wan holding about 11%.
interesting_fact: Friendess began as a student startup next to Shanghai Jiao Tong University, backed by the Shanghai university-student entrepreneurship fund, and its laser-cutting controllers became the market leader in China.
deep_cut_fact: When the company was registered on 11 Sept 2007 with 200,000 yuan of capital (half pledged by SJTU's technology-transfer center), Wan Zhang and three of the co-founders each put in just 10,000 yuan.
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (~11%), Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology (Bochu, 688188.SH)
research_notes: Very low profile; could not confirm his current executive title. Chairman/public face is Tang Ye. Route via company board secretary (Zhou Zhiyu).

name: Su Jianguo
profile: Su Jianguo (b. c.1955) founded Changzhou-based Leili in 1993, when China's micro-motor industry was in its infancy, and built it into a major maker of motors for air conditioners and appliances (listed in Shenzhen 2017). Now run day-to-day by his son Su Da, Leili has diversified into EV motors, medical micro-motors (Dingzhi Technology) and robot components such as hollow-cup motors and dexterous hands.
interesting_fact: Before its 2017 IPO nearly 90% of Leili's revenue came from home-appliance motors; it has since opened a Vietnam plant (2019) and started mass-producing hollow-cup motors for robots in 2024, with a subsidiary (Zhongke Lingxi) building dexterous robot hands.
deep_cut_fact: Leili's first product was an air-conditioner motor, developed by an early technical team drawn largely from an established state-owned enterprise in Changzhou.
current_role: Founder and actual controller, Jiangsu Leili Motor Co. (SZSE: 300660), Changzhou; son Su Da is general manager and legal representative
research_notes: Hurun pairs him with son Su Da, who now fronts the company and gives interviews (e.g. The Paper, July 2026) - Su Da is the better outreach target. A team-profile page (pitchhub.36kr.com) says Su started in 1979 as a salesman at Wujin No.3 Electronic Components Factory; verify against prospectus.

name: Su Da
profile: Su Da (苏达) runs Changzhou-based Jiangsu Leili Motor, the micro-motor maker his father Su Jianguo founded in 1993; its first product was an air-conditioner motor. He has steered Leili from ~90% home-appliance revenue (pre-2017 IPO) into EV motors, medical micro-motors (via Dingzhi Tech) and now robotics/embodied-AI components such as coreless motors and dexterous hands.
interesting_fact: Roughly one in three air conditioners and one in five washing machines worldwide uses a Leili motor. Its high-end motors now reach 100,000 rpm.
deep_cut_fact: Leili controls Anhui Zhongke Lingxi, a USTC-incubated dexterous-robot-hand maker. Su splits embodied-AI commercialisation into three tiers: service, then industrial/commercial, then elder care. He predicts service robots scale first and end up with an EV-like market structure (Paper, July 2026).
current_role: General Manager, Jiangsu Leili Motor Co. (江苏雷利, SZSE: 300660)
research_notes: Emails are for the board secretary (Yin Chenglong) and the securities representative, as published in Leili's reports. Su speaks to media ('Vibrant China' tour 2026), so he is relatively accessible. Good robotics/electrification angle. Listing shared with Su Jianguo.

name: Pu Yilong
profile: Pu Yilong (浦益龙, b. Feb 1961) turned a Wuxi copper-tube factory he ran from 1994 into Jiangsu Longda Superalloy, a STAR Market-listed maker of cast and wrought high-temperature alloys for aero-engines and gas turbines. He has been chairman/GM since 2004 and is a Jiangsu provincial people's congress deputy.
interesting_fact: Longda's superalloys go into aircraft engines and gas turbines — the same turbine supply chain now in demand for on-site data-center power generation.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in July 1978, aged 17, at the Houqiao construction company in Xishan, rising to engineering-team manager before taking over the Wuxi Longda copper-tube factory in 1994.
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Jiangsu Longda Superalloy Co. (隆达股份, SSE STAR: 688231), Wuxi; also acting board secretary
research_notes: Gas-turbine/superalloy angle fits an energy/data-center podcast. He is personally acting as board secretary (2026), so the IR mailbox may reach his office. Source is Longda's 2025 annual report.

name: Ou Xinhua
profile: Engineer-founder who set up Shanghai Prisemi in Nov 2009, a fabless designer of power semiconductors (TVS/ESD protection devices, MOSFETs, Schottky diodes, power-management ICs) for consumer electronics, with Xiaomi among its major customers. He controlled 100% of the company before its 2021 STAR Market listing and was re-elected chairman in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Prisemi was his first startup, and he kept 100% control of it right up to its STAR Market IPO filing, with no outside VC shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Prisemi he was an R&D engineer and project manager at Shanghai Guangyu Ruixin Microelectronics and then technical director at Suzhou Jingxun Technology.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shanghai Prisemi Electronics (芯导科技, STAR Market: 688230)
research_notes: Low public profile with no interviews found. Prisemi does power and protection chips, mainly for phones and consumer devices, so the data-center link is indirect.

name: Jing Shiping
profile: Jing Shiping (b. 1969) built Hengmingda from a Shenzhen packaging-printing shop into a Kunshan-based maker of precision flexible and metal structural parts for smartphones, tablets, laptops and VR/AR devices. He has chaired the listed company since 2017 and controls it with family members; it now also supplies metal structures for EV chargers, energy storage and PV inverters.
interesting_fact: Hengmingda has moved beyond consumer electronics into new energy, supplying precision metal structural parts for charging piles, battery-swap cabinets, home and C&I energy-storage systems and PV inverters to leading Chinese new-energy firms.
deep_cut_fact: Jing started out at Hong Kong's Dasheng company and the Hengmingda packaging & printing plant in Bao'an, Shenzhen, and ran Kunshan Hengmingda Packaging Materials from 1999 before pivoting the business into electronics components; he holds an MBA.
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Hengmingda Electronic Technology Co. (SZSE: 002947)
research_notes: Family-controlled (Jing Shiping, Jing Tianping, Jing Jingping, Xia Chen, Jing Jiang); Jing Tianping is legal rep/GM. Energy-storage component angle fits the podcast. Route via securities affairs office email.

name: Zhang Rongming
profile: Zhang Rongming founded Beijing lingerie group Aimer, one of China's leading premium intimate-apparel brands (Aimer, Aimer Men, Aimer Kids and others). He started in 1992-93 by taking over a failing Beijing garment factory. Aimer listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021, and he remains controlling shareholder, chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Aimer's first bra, launched in 1993, sold for RMB49 when average monthly urban wages were around RMB190. From the start he aimed to match international brands on quality, and he borrowed RMB800k from friends because banks would not lend without collateral.
deep_cut_fact: He was a materials scientist teaching at the Beijing Steel and Iron Institute (now USTB) when he heard shape-memory alloy could be used in bras. In 1991 he developed a 'super-elastic memory-alloy bra underwire', which he used as his technology stake to take over Huamei Garment Factory.
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Aimer Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603511)
research_notes: Gives occasional long-form interviews (36Kr, SCMP 2026 profile). The materials-science and 'hard tech for the softest product' story is a natural entrepreneurship hook. Route requests through Aimer's securities/IR office.

name: Xu Bing
appears_on: Hurun China (2020-2026); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020-2026)
profile: Xu Bing (徐兵) and Huang Shaoxiong control Compass Technology (指南针) through holding company Guangzhou Zhanxin. Compass is a Beijing-based retail stock-analysis software and fintech firm that listed on ChiNext in 2019 and has since moved into brokerage (Mega/麦高 Securities) and fund management. Xu has run Guangzhou Zhanxin since 2010.
interesting_fact: Compass grew from selling stock-analysis software to retail investors into a licensed financial group by acquiring a securities brokerage and a fund manager, using a software customer base to build a broker.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, Xu served 1984-1997 in the Guangzhou Military Region Air Force logistics department, then worked 1997-2008 at Guangzhou Nanhu Golf Club (assistant GM, later director), according to Compass's annual report.
current_role: General manager of Guangzhou Zhanxin Communication Technology; co-actual controller (with Huang Shaoxiong) of Beijing Compass Technology (SZSE ChiNext: 300803)
research_notes: Low profile and not an executive of the listed company. He holds a Hong Kong (non-permanent) resident ID. Not to be confused with SenseTime co-founder Xu Bing (徐冰). The route is via the Compass securities office.

name: Wang Zhongshan
profile: Wang Zhongshan (王忠善, aged ~62), founded Tianjin-based gold-jewellery maker and retailer Mokingran in 2000 after starting as an apprentice gemstone setter in the 1990s. The company listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024; he holds ~23.7% directly and, with his family, controls ~60%. Rising gold prices lifted the stake into Hurun's China list in 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he was named an official inheritor of Shandong Province intangible cultural heritage for gold-jewellery craftsmanship, and was honoured for 'outstanding contribution to the jewellery industry' on the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Mokingran he worked as an apprentice doing gemstone inlay and processing in the 1990s, and in January 2013 was recognised as Weifang's 'First Folk Art Master' (首届民间工艺大师).
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Mokingran Jewellery Group (梦金园黄金珠宝集团, HKEX: 2585)
research_notes: Family business: wife is an executive director and son is general manager. Route via IR email in the 2025 annual report.

name: Qiao Yuhua
profile: Born 1966, an accountant by training who rose from cement/iron plant bookkeeper in Qipanjing (Otog Banner, Ordos) to found the Shuangxin chemical group in 2000. Shuangxin turns calcium carbide into polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and derivatives used in construction, paper, fibres, PVB film and water-soluble film; he controls ~62% of the voting rights of the SZSE-listed unit.
interesting_fact: Shuangxin listed on the Shenzhen main board in late 2025 and is using IPO funds to move downstream from PVA into PVB (laminated-glass interlayer) and VAE emulsion products.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (1986) was at the Qipanjing cement & iron plant; he then worked four years at the ICBC Qipanjing office in Otog Banner before returning to the plant as finance chief - he holds an accounting degree from the Central Institute of Finance and is a senior engineer.
current_role: Actual controller and director, Inner Mongolia Shuangxin Environment-Friendly Material (001369.SZ, listed Dec 2025); chairman, Shuangxin Resources
research_notes: Energy-intensive coal-chemical business in Ordos (carbide, captive power) - relevant to energy angle. Low media profile; route via board office of Shuangxin Materials.

name: Li Yi
profile: Li Yi (Archer Li) founded 51WORLD in Beijing in 2015, evolving it from a VR startup into a digital-twin and simulation platform used for autonomous-driving testing, transport hubs, smart factories, water management and energy. Backed by Sky9 Capital from its Series A, 51WORLD listed on the HKEX main board; he now pitches it as a data engine for embodied AI and robotics.
interesting_fact: His stated goal is to build a 'Digital Twin Earth' - a complete virtual replica of the world - by 2030; 51WORLD's simulation platform serves nearly a hundred intelligent-driving customers.
deep_cut_fact: On investor Sky9 Capital's founder page he lists as his favorite quote: 'Pessimists are always right but optimists are more likely to succeed.'
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, 51WORLD (Beijing 51World Digital Twin Technology; HKEX-listed)
research_notes: Goes by 'Archer Li' in English. aes@51aes.com is 51WORLD's published customer-service email (no dedicated press address found). Data-center/energy angle: digital twins for energy sites and factories; recent focus on robotics training data.

name: Chen Jifeng
profile: Chen Jifeng (b. 1968), a USTC plasma-physics graduate and professor-level senior engineer, built Beijing Worldia into a maker of ultra-precision superhard (diamond/CBN) cutting tools, listed on the STAR Market in 2019. He controls about a third of the company and is pushing it into CVD diamond functional materials such as heat sinks, optical windows and acoustic parts.
interesting_fact: Worldia now sells CVD diamond heat-sink materials and diamond optical windows — diamond's extreme thermal conductivity makes it a candidate for cooling high-power chips, a theme relevant to AI/data-center hardware.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from USTC's Department of Modern Physics (plasma physics) he spent 1992-2000 as an engineer at the State Building Materials Bureau's Synthetic Crystals Research Institute, then ran Beijing Xiboer (2000-10) before building Worldia.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Beijing Worldia Diamond Tools (沃尔德, SH:688028)
public_contact: office_email: info@worldiatools.com | press_email: marketing@worldiatools.com | official_website: https://www.worldiatools.com
research_notes: Technical founder in a data-center-adjacent niche (diamond thermal materials) — good podcast angle. Co-actual controller listed as Yang Nuo. Company hotline 400-766-9898 published; board secretary is Chen Huanchao.

name: Yang Nuo
profile: Hurun lists Yang Nuo with Chen Jifeng for Worldia, a Beijing-headquartered maker of ultra-precision diamond and superhard cutting tools listed on the STAR Market. Chen (b. 1968) is chairman, general manager and controlling shareholder with about 33.5%; Yang Nuo held about 0.98% as of March 2026. Their relationship is not stated in the filings found; she is likely a family member.
interesting_fact: Worldia started in 2006 as a small Beijing company with registered capital of just RMB 500,000 and grew into a listed specialist in ultra-precision and high-precision superhard cutting tools and superhard materials.
current_role: Individual shareholder (about 1%) of Beijing Worldia Diamond Tools Co., Ltd. (沃尔德, SSE STAR: 688028); Hurun lists her wealth jointly with chairman Chen Jifeng
research_notes: Very low profile and no biography found; the shareholding is from https://quote.cfi.cn/gdtj/93382/688028.html . Chen Jifeng is the public face, and the company securities office (board secretary 陈焕超) is the only route.

name: Cai Baogui
profile: Cai Baogui (蔡报贵, b. 1971) founded Ganzhou-based JL MAG Rare-Earth in 2008, building it into the world's No.1 producer of high-performance NdFeB permanent magnets by output and sales in 2024. Its magnets go into EV motors, inverter air-conditioners, wind turbines, robots and humanoid robotics; the company is listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong and he remains chairman and co-controller.
interesting_fact: JL MAG became the world's largest rare-earth permanent magnet maker by production and sales in 2024; wind power and EVs are core markets, and it is expanding into humanoid-robot motors.
deep_cut_fact: A 1993 fine-chemicals graduate of Nanchang University, he first taught at the university (1993-94), then spent eight years as a production manager at a Dongguan plastics factory before running his own plastics-electronics plant; since 2008 he has also chaired Lide Wind Power (Jiangxi). He earned a Tsinghua EMBA in 2022.
current_role: Chairman, JL MAG Rare-Earth Co. (金力永磁, 300748.SZ / 6680.HK); co-actual controller
public_contact: ir_email: jlmag_info@jlmag.com.cn (JL MAG board office/IR) | official_website: https://www.jlmag.com.cn
research_notes: Strong energy fit: rare-earth magnets for wind turbines and EVs, plus his own wind-power company (Lide Wind Power). Chaired JL MAG board meetings through Aug 2026. Co-controllers with Li Xinnong and Hu Zhibin.

name: Ao Fengting
profile: Inner Mongolia entrepreneur who founded Mengtai Group (formerly Ordos Mengtai Coal & Power), an integrated coal, power and aluminium producer in Ordos. He has been on the Hurun list every year since 2010 (9th in Inner Mongolia in 2024, RMB 5.3bn) and reportedly is a vice-president of the China Ethnic Trade Promotion Association.
interesting_fact: Mengtai follows the classic Inner Mongolia 'coal-power-aluminium' integration model, using its own mine-mouth coal power to run energy-intensive aluminium smelting.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Inner Mongolia Mengtai Group (coal, power, aluminium; Ordos)
research_notes: Very low profile with minimal public information; the biography above comes from a Hurun-derived list (maigoo.com/news/725273.html). I could not reach a company website or published contact. Identity is matched by name and company only.

name: Zhang Zhimin
profile: Born 1951, Zhang Zhimin has chaired Shenzhen-based T&S Communications since December 2000. T&S makes passive optical components, notably high-density MTP/MPO fibre connectors and fibre flex circuits used in hyperscale data centres, and its value has surged with AI computing build-outs; he shares the Hurun listing with his wife Cai Bo.
interesting_fact: T&S's high-density MTP/MPO fibre connectors are widely used in large data centres worldwide, making it a direct beneficiary of the AI data-center boom.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1984 as an interpreter and later head of sales at China-Japan (Shenzhen) Leasing, one of Shenzhen's early Sino-foreign ventures, before he ran Shenzhen Zhonghe Optical and moved into fibre optics.
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen T&S Communications (太辰光, SZSE: 300570)
research_notes: Excellent fit for a data-center podcast (optical interconnect supplier). His board term ran to Sept 2026 per the 2025 annual report; confirm re-election.

name: Cai Bo
profile: Cai Bo (蔡波, b. 1972) is a long-time executive and member of the controlling shareholder group of Shenzhen T&S Communications, a maker of passive optical interconnect components (ceramic ferrules, MT ferrules, high-density MPO connectivity) used in hyperscale and AI data centers and telecom networks. She joined in 2000 as overseas sales manager and has been board secretary since 2011; her wealth is shared with chairman Zhang Zhimin, her husband.
interesting_fact: T&S's high-density optical connectivity products sell globally into large data centers; its 2025 annual report ties growth to the AI compute build-out and new technologies such as silicon photonics and CPO, a direct link to the podcast's data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: An English major, Cai taught at a school affiliated with China Zhenhua Group from 1992 to 2000 before joining T&S in December 2000 as its overseas sales manager, building the export business that now dominates its revenue.
current_role: Board Secretary and Overseas Market Department Manager, Shenzhen T&S Communications (太辰光, SZ:300570)
research_notes: As board secretary she personally runs the IR channel, so zqb@china-tscom.com reaches her office directly. English-speaking; strong data-center/optical-interconnect angle.

name: Wen Hongfu
profile: Wen Hongfu (aged ~61) is the founder and co-controlling shareholder (with Fang Hong and Wen Ya) of Omat (欧莱新材), a maker of high-performance sputtering targets for flat-panel displays, integrated circuits and solar. Omat listed on the STAR Market in May 2024. He also runs its subsidiaries making high-purity metals and indium products.
interesting_fact: Omat's shares opened 176% above their 9.60-yuan offer price on their STAR Market debut on 9 May 2024. Sputtering targets are a key material in semiconductor and display fabs, a supply chain China has been trying to localise.
deep_cut_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur, Wen was a university teacher at Anhui Institute of Technology (formerly Huainan Mining Institute). He then worked at China National Metals & Minerals Import & Export's Shenzhen trading arm and was assistant GM of Guangdong Metallurgical Shenzhen Import & Export Co.
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and CTO, Guangdong Omat Advanced Materials Co., Ltd. (Shanghai STAR: 688530)
research_notes: The Hurun source name 'Omat' is Guangdong Omat Advanced Materials (欧莱新材). He is also the CTO, so the company is a semiconductor-materials angle that may suit the podcast.

name: Liang Meizhen
profile: One of three actual controllers of S.C New Energy, a Shenzhen solar-equipment maker founded in 2003 that builds PECVD, diffusion, texturing/etching and automation tools for crystalline-silicon PV cell lines; it listed on ChiNext in 2018. She directly holds about 7% and controls about 11% of voting rights (incl. shares held by her son), per 2025 filings. No executive role found.
interesting_fact: 'SC' in the Hurun listing is S.C New Energy (捷佳伟创), one of China's main suppliers of solar-cell manufacturing equipment, whose PECVD tools deposit anti-reflective and passivation layers on PV cells.
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (acting in concert with Yu Zhong and Zuo Guojun) of Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创, 300724.SZ)
research_notes: Identity inferred from Hurun 'SC' + green energy and confirmed by S.C New Energy filings naming 梁美珍 as co-actual controller. Appears to be a passive shareholder with no public profile; better interview targets are chairman Zuo Guojun or CEO Yu Zhong.

name: Hu Yuhang
profile: Hu Yuhang (胡宇航, b. 1976) is a co-founder of 37 Interactive Entertainment, one of China's biggest mobile/web game publishers (titles such as 'Puzzles & Survival' and 'Douluo Dalu' games). He has run its R&D brand 37 Games since 2013. His stake rose to 7% in 2020, and he was re-elected to the board in 2025 as vice chairman.
interesting_fact: He is the developer-side co-founder, leading 37 Games' studios while the group grew into one of China's top game exporters. In 2019 he was named a 'Craftsman Spirit Figure of the Game Industry' (游戏行业匠心精神人物).
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Lanzhou University in China's northwest, far from 37's Guangzhou base, and later took an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business (CKGSB).
current_role: Vice Chairman, 37 Interactive Entertainment (三七互娱, SZSE 002555); long-time President of 37 Games (R&D arm)
research_notes: He is low profile in English-language media. In December 2025 regulators (CSRC/SZSE) penalised several 37 Interactive directors, including him, over a 2018 related-party disclosure (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202512051794542444_1.pdf); avoid that topic. Best route is 37 Interactive IR or the board secretary (Wang Sijie).

name: Hu Xinrong
profile: Shenzhen engineer who co-founded Xinyichang with Song Changning in 2006; the two are its controlling shareholders. Starting with capacitor aging-test machines, the company became a leading Chinese maker of LED (incl. Mini LED) die bonders and expanded into semiconductor die-attach and lithium-battery equipment. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Xinyichang began in 2006 making aluminium electrolytic capacitor aging-test machines, then used that know-how to break into LED die bonders, and later developed six-head high-speed die bonders for Mini LED and chip-packaging die bonders for semiconductors.
deep_cut_fact: He worked his way up from the shop floor: a technician at Shenzhen Huachang Electronics, then technician and equipment supervisor at Shenzhen Datong, before running two small Bao'an workshops (Hengchang machining plant and Yichang electronics factory) that preceded Xinyichang.
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and core technical staff, Shenzhen Xinyichang Technology (Hoson, SSE STAR: 688383)
research_notes: Hurun's 'Xinyichang' = 新益昌 (Hoson). Low media profile; route via board secretary Liu Xiaohuan's office (hoson@szhech.com, listed in 2024 interim report). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Hsin Chung-Herng
profile: Hsin Chung-Herng (辛忠衡; the input's 辛忠卫 appears to be a typo) chairs Taiwan Union Technology, a Taiwanese maker of copper-clad laminates and prepregs for printed circuit boards. Demand for its high-speed, low-loss laminates in AI servers and data-center switches has driven a surge in its share price, putting him on the Hurun list in 2026.
interesting_fact: TUC began in 1974 as Taiwan Union Glass, an optical-glass maker, and only switched to copper-clad laminates in 1997; its 'ThunderClad' low-loss materials are now used in AI server and high-speed networking boards.
current_role: Chairman, Taiwan Union Technology Corp. (TUC, 台燿科技, TPEx: 6274)
research_notes: Strong AI/data-center supply-chain angle. Very low public profile; no interviews found. profile: Ren Luozhong (任罗忠), born 1962, is a long-time co-builder of Robam (老板电器), the Hangzhou kitchen-appliance maker known for range hoods. deep_cut_fact: He is one of the nine individual co-founders named in NHU's 1999 incorporation, alongside Zhang Pingyi, Yuan Yizhong, Shi Cheng and others, with Xinchang Synthetic Chemical Plant (renamed NHU Holding Group in Nov 2009).
current_role: Director, NHU Holding Group (新和成控股集团), controlling shareholder of Zhejiang NHU Co. (新和成, SZSE: 002001)

name: Zhong Hangen
profile: Zhong Hangen (b. 1964) has worked in agrochemicals since 1982. He ran the Dafeng county veterinary-drug plant and the Dafeng agrochemical plant before founding Huifeng, a crop-protection and pesticide maker in Dafeng, Yancheng, Jiangsu, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He is still controlling shareholder and leads the company. He is also a vice-president of the China Crop Protection Industry Association.
interesting_fact: He was named one of Jiangsu's first 'Top 10 Outstanding Patent Inventors' and has also been honoured as a National Outstanding Young Entrepreneur and a Jiangsu provincial model worker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Huifeng he was director of the Dafeng county veterinary-drug factory and then of the Dafeng agrochemical plant. He has managed agrochemical businesses continuously since 1982, when he was about 18.
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and chairman/GM, Jiangsu Huifeng Bio Agriculture (SZSE: 002496, 'Huifeng')
research_notes: Hurun listed him 2014-2017, and the company's value has fallen since. The company has a 2018 environmental-compliance history, so avoid it as an outreach topic. The IR mailbox is the published board-office address.

name: Zou Chenghui
profile: Chinese solar entrepreneur who founded Akcome in 2006, a maker of solar module components (aluminium frames, EVA) that expanded into PV power plants and heterojunction (HJT) cells; Akcome listed in Shenzhen in 2011 and he was chairman from 2011. Akcome was delisted from the Shenzhen exchange in June 2024, and his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Akcome was an early Chinese mover in heterojunction (HJT) solar cells: at SNEC 2023 it unveiled a 730 W n-type HJT module (AK iPower 7.0) on 210 mm wafers.
current_role: Founder and (former) chairman / controlling shareholder, Akcome (Zhejiang Akcome New Energy Technology, ex-SZSE 002610)
research_notes: Akcome was delisted in 2024 after its share price fell below exchange thresholds and a CSRC disclosure investigation into the company and Zou - wealth likely far below the Hurun figure; sensitive subject, low-priority outreach target. No current published contacts found. Delisting source: https://pv-magazine.com/2024/06/21/chinese-pv-industry-brief-akcome-confirms-delisting-from-the-shenzhen-stock-market

name: Sun Weiting
profile: Sun Weiting (孙伟挺), born 1963, founded Huafu in 1993 with co-founder Chen Lingfen, with whom Hurun lists his wealth as shared. Huafu is one of the world's largest makers of colour-spun (melange) yarn and supplies global apparel brands. It now runs a 'cotton to sock' supply chain including Xinjiang cotton operations, and he has chaired the listed company since Dec 2008.
interesting_fact: Huafu describes itself as one of the world's largest colour-spun yarn makers. It says it holds the most patents in the colour-spun yarn industry and is the yarn of choice for major global apparel brands.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Huafu, he was a government official: textile-company planner (1982-87), deputy director at Zhejiang's Light Industry Department (1987-90), and deputy head of Shaoxing's Yuecheng District (1990-93). He started the company in 1993.
current_role: Chairman of Huafu Fashion Co. (SZSE: 002042) and of parent Huafu Holding
research_notes: Co-actual controller with co-founder Chen Lingfen (vice chairman and president), with whom Hurun shares the wealth listing. The textile business has limited overlap with energy or data centers. Route is via the board office.

name: Chen Lingfen
profile: Chen Lingfen (陈玲芬, b. 1963) co-founded Huafu with Sun Weiting in 1993 and has been vice chairman since, adding the president role in 2009. Huafu is one of the world's largest makers of melange (colour-spun) yarn, supplying major global apparel brands, with large spinning operations in Zhejiang and Xinjiang. She also serves as the company's head of accounting.
interesting_fact: Huafu calls itself one of the world's largest melange-yarn suppliers and says its yarn is a first choice of major global fashion brands; the 'Huafu' mark is a China Well-Known Trademark.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Huafu she spent 1981-1993 as a civil servant and trader in Shaoxing: deputy section chief at the Shaoxing Economic Cooperation Office, then office director and finance manager at Shaoxing Yueling Trading Co.; she later earned a Renmin University EMBA.
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairman and President, Huafu Fashion Co. (华孚时尚, SZSE: 002042); co-controller with husband Sun Weiting
research_notes: Wealth shared with husband Sun Weiting (chairman). Route via board office email. Avoid Xinjiang-cotton controversy in outreach.

name: Zhu Muzhi
profile: Hurun China listed Zhu Muzhi 2014-2021 for Xin Nanfang Group, the Guangzhou real-estate and traditional-Chinese-medicine conglomerate. Public sources name Zhu Layi (elder brother of Hopson founder Zhu Mengyi) as Xin Nanfang's founder (1994); no source links the name 朱沐之 to the group, so this may be an alias, alternate name or family member - unverified.
interesting_fact: Xin Nanfang, the group behind this listing, pivoted early from property into TCM, investing for over a decade in artemisinin anti-malaria projects across Africa with Prof. Li Guoqiao, and backs Deng Lao herbal tea.
current_role: Unknown - no public record found under the name 朱沐之; Hurun (2014-2021) ties the fortune to Guangdong Xin Nanfang (New South) Group
research_notes: Identity unresolved: zero search hits for 朱沐之. If the journalist means Xin Nanfang's founder, that is Zhu Layi (a former barefoot doctor and Guangzhou TCM College graduate). Do not use facts here for outreach without confirming the person.

name: Gu Shaofeng
profile: Gu Shaofeng, a Shanghai Jiao Tong University graduate and ex-Microsoft technical lead, co-founded Paipaidai in 2007 — China's first online P2P lending platform — and was its CEO, CTO and strategy chief before it became FinVolution, a NYSE-listed fintech operating credit platforms in China, Indonesia and the Philippines. He has chaired the board since 2020 and is its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: Paipaidai, which he co-founded with Zhang Jun and Hu Honghui, was China's first P2P lending platform and listed on the NYSE in 2017 before rebranding as FinVolution.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he founded Podlook (菠萝网, 2006), which grew to one of China's largest podcast aggregators with ~26,000 channels on under RMB100k of startup capital; he worked unpaid, saying 'many on this team don't take salaries — like me.' A natural hook for a podcast pitch.
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Innovation Officer, FinVolution Group (信也科技, NYSE: FINV)
public_contact: ir_email: ir@xinye.com | pr_agency: finv@tpg-ir.com (The Piacente Group, IR agency) | official_website: https://finvolution.gcs-web.com/board-member/shaofeng-gu
research_notes: Podcast-founder background (Podlook) makes him an unusually good fit. IR contacts from a 2023 6-K exhibit; verify against latest earnings release. Official bio page: finvolution.gcs-web.com.

name: Gu Zhengqing
profile: Gu Zhengqing, born in the 1980s, founded Suzhou Shihua in 2010 at age 27 to make functional composite materials (adhesive, conductive and shielding coatings on PET/PI films) for consumer electronics. Small customised parts won it a place in Apple's supply chain, and it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He and his wife Kuai Lili control it through Yefuyou Investment.
interesting_fact: Shihua got into Apple's supply chain by taking the small, high-spec custom parts that larger foreign suppliers found too low-volume to bother with; it grew from one or two Apple parts to more than 100 certified ones.
deep_cut_fact: Shortly before Spring Festival, while driving home, he got the call that Shihua's material would go into the iPad. He dropped off his family and drove straight back to Suzhou without eating; the plant ran until New Year's Eve 2011 and restarted on the third day of the holiday. He calls this the company's 'first pot of gold'.
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller of Suzhou Shihua New Material Technology (世华科技, SSE STAR: 688093); stepped down as general manager in July 2026
research_notes: Hurun calls the company 'Shihua' and lists him with his wife Kuai Lili. He says 'entrepreneurship is forced on you' (创业都是逼出来的), which suits a founder-story podcast. Board secretary per cninfo: 计毓雯. GM resignation reported at https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1527702.shtml

name: Kuai Lili
profile: Kuai Lili (蒯丽丽, b. 1985) is a director and, since 2026, one of only two actual controllers of Suzhou Shihua New Material Technology, a STAR Market-listed maker of functional electronic materials and high-performance optical films used in consumer electronics. She co-owns holding company Yefuyou Investment (40%) with her husband, chairman Gu Zhengqing (60%).
interesting_fact: In 2026 the founders' five-person concert-party agreement was dissolved, leaving Kuai Lili and Gu Zhengqing as Shihua's sole actual controllers; she appeared on Hurun's China Under-40 self-made list in 2021.
current_role: Director and co-actual controller (with husband Gu Zhengqing) of Suzhou Shihua New Material Technology (世华科技, 688093.SH)
research_notes: Low public profile; husband Gu Zhengqing (chairman) is the public face. Spouse relationship and 40% Yefuyou stake per 2025 prospectus (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-08-29/1224607144.PDF). Shihua is a 'little giant' specialised SME; no personal channels found.

name: Li Guoping
profile: Li Guoping (李国平) founded Danyang-based Tongli Risheng, a leading maker of elevator and escalator components (guide rails, structural parts) supplying global brands such as Schindler and Otis; it listed in Shanghai in 2021. He has since steered it into new energy by taking control of Beijing Tianqi Hongyuan, an energy-storage system integrator, and the company was renamed Tongli Tianqi.
interesting_fact: The elevator-parts company now builds containerised battery energy-storage systems: its Tianqi Hongyuan unit's team has worked on over 3 GWh of storage projects and was named a 2025 'best energy storage system integrator', a strong energy-podcast angle.
deep_cut_fact: Li began in 1980 as a machine operator and cashier at a rubber-thread factory in Daoshu, Danyang, then spent 1985-2001 at the Daoshu Shenyang elevator-decoration factory rising from salesman to sales chief, sales manager and deputy factory head before running his own firm, Danyang Risheng, from 2001.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Jiangsu Tongli Tianqi Technology (同力天启, SH:605286; formerly Tongli Risheng 同力日升)
research_notes: Self-made from the factory floor; very relevant pivot from elevators to grid-scale energy storage. Best route: board secretary Liu Liang via zqb@jstljx.com.

name: Yam Yu
profile: Yam Yu (任宇) controls Hong Kong-listed International Business Settlement Holdings (formerly Chaoyue Group). He owns 12.89bn shares (55.79%) through BVI vehicle Long Grand Ltd, plus 750m shares bought directly in March 2026. IBS runs supercomputing servers for Bitcoin mining and cloud mining, and began IC-chip trading in December 2025.
interesting_fact: In November 2025, IBS bought 1 EH/s of cloud-mining hashrate for a year from a subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed Bitdeer, paying about US$15m in Bitcoin. It mined about 117.5 BTC in FY2026 and held 234 BTC at 31 March 2026.
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~59%) of International Business Settlement Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 0147) via his wholly owned Long Grand Limited
research_notes: He is not a director; the board is led by executive directors Yuen Leong, Chan Siu Tat and Lou Ming. The company's published office line is +852 2549 9988 (Causeway Bay). Recent news reports a proposed HK$563m acquisition of an AI-chip business. The data-centre/compute and Bitcoin-mining angle fits the podcast. Little personal information is public.

name: Wang Yaolin
profile: Yaolin Wang (王耀林, b. 1963), a US-trained pharmacologist, spent 18 years as a drug-discovery scientist at Schering-Plough and Merck. In 2015 he left to build InventisBio in Shanghai with other returnee PhDs. The company developed the targeted cancer drugs befotertinib (EGFR) and garsorasib (KRAS G12C), both out-licensed, and listed on the STAR Market in July 2022.
interesting_fact: InventisBio's KRAS G12C inhibitor garsorasib (格索雷塞) targets a cancer mutation long considered 'undruggable'. It reached approval in China, putting this ex-Merck lab scientist's startup among the few groups with a drug against that target.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his pharmacology PhD at SUNY Stony Brook and did postdoctoral research at Baylor College of Medicine in 1992-97. He then worked as a principal scientist at Schering-Plough (1997-2009) and Merck (2009-15), and only founded his company at 52.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, InventisBio (益方生物, SSE STAR 688382), Shanghai
research_notes: He is a US citizen with Chinese permanent residency and comfortable in English, having spent 20+ years in US pharma. Co-controllers are Jiang Yueheng (board secretary) and Dai Xing. Best route is ir@inventisbio.com. A 2019 Endpoints News article covers his decision to leave Merck (https://endpts.com/?p=60394).

name: Yan Deping
profile: Yan Deping (严德平) left a teaching job in 1997 to start a small commercial print shop in Hefei, then pivoted around 2000 into paper cups and later biodegradable (PLA) food-service ware. Hengxin now supplies cups and packaging to tea and coffee chains such as Luckin and Mixue, and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Hengxin is a national 'little giant' specialist in biodegradable tableware, with annual capacity of around 9 billion cups and containers serving China's booming tea-and-coffee chains.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 11 years as a teacher at Hefei Forestry Vocational & Technical School; at 34 he started 'Hengxin Printing' with second-hand presses, doing design, printing and sales himself, and the paper know-how led him into paper cups.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hefei Hengxin Life Science & Technology (恒鑫生活, SZSE ChiNext: 301501)
research_notes: Hurun lists the company as 'HXIN'. Co-founded with spouse Fan Yanru. Company holds online investor Q&A sessions (e.g. 15 May 2026).

name: Yu Lanjun
profile: Yu Lanjun (于兰军), a Liaoning businessman, is deputy GM of Liaoning Lingyuan Gangda Group Industrial and runs Shenyang Jinhaoxin Trading and Shenyang Zhongtuan Technology. In 2022 he became the largest shareholder and actual controller of Jilin-based TCM drugmaker Tonghua Golden-Horse, where he holds 190m shares (19.66%); he holds no executive post there.
interesting_fact: He became Tonghua Golden-Horse's controller in 2022 when a Chengdu court awarded him 80m shares owed by the previous controller, Beijing Jinshang Alliance, which then formally agreed to his taking control.
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller (19.66%) of Tonghua Golden-Horse Pharmaceutical (通化金马, SZSE: 000766); deputy GM of Liaoning Lingyuan Gangda Group Industrial
research_notes: Very low profile; no interviews or biography found. Day-to-day leadership at Tonghua Golden-Horse is chairman/GM Zhang Yufu. Part of his stake is pledged. The IR email belongs to the company, not to him.

name: Tang Zhuolin
profile: Tang Zhuolin (唐灼林, 'Victor Tang', b.1963) founded Dongfang Precision in Foshan in 1996, growing it from a workshop making printing/packaging machinery into a leading corrugated-box equipment maker, listed in 2011. He expanded via acquisitions (Italy's Fosber 2014, Baisheng marine engines, EDF, Tiruna, Agnati) and in 2025 sold the Fosber overseas corrugated-line business for ~€817m, pivoting to high-end smart equipment, outboard power and AI+robotics.
interesting_fact: The Fosber corrugated-line business he bought into in 2014 was sold in 2025 for a final consideration of about €817m, funding a pivot to robotics and marine power.
deep_cut_fact: Dongfang Precision started out in agricultural-product packaging printing before Tang moved it into corrugated-carton equipment, growing it from a 'small workshop' into a group, as he recounted at a 2024 Nanhai chairmen's salon marking nearly 30 years.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangdong Dongfang Precision Science & Technology (SZSE: 002611), Foshan
research_notes: Co-controller with brother Tang Zhuomian per 2011 IPO docs. Manufacturing/robotics pivot is a podcast angle.

name: Liu Peichao
profile: Liu Peichao (刘培超), a Shandong University mechanical-engineering master's graduate, quit a job at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Suzhou medical-engineering institute to build a desktop robot arm in 2014, founding Dobot in Shenzhen in 2015. Dobot became a leading collaborative-robot maker (desktop, industrial cobots, now humanoids), listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024 and is pursuing a ChiNext A-share listing; he owns roughly half the company.
interesting_fact: Dobot started with a low-cost desktop robotic arm for makers and classrooms in 2014 and grew into one of the world's top collaborative-robot vendors by shipments, now also building humanoid robots.
deep_cut_fact: As a Shandong University freshman he won the campus phone-card sales agency; after being recommended for postgraduate study he led classmates in business-plan contests and worked weekends as an outdoor team-building coach. He left the CAS medical-engineering institute to start up without telling his family.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, Shenzhen Dobot Corp (越疆科技, HKEX: 2432)
research_notes: Named a national 'Ten Thousand Talents' tech-entrepreneur leader (2019). Gives media interviews on robotics. Sensitive: in July 2026 co-founder/ex-COO Song Tao publicly disputed shareholdings ahead of the A-share IPO; avoid the topic.

name: Li Xinnong
profile: Li Xinnong (李忻农), born 1969, is a Beihang-trained materials engineer who co-controls Ganzhou-based JL MAG Rare-Earth with chairman Cai Baogui and Hu Zhibin. JL MAG is one of the world's largest makers of high-performance NdFeB permanent magnets used in EV motors, wind turbines and, increasingly, humanoid-robot motor rotors. He has been a director since 2008.
interesting_fact: JL MAG's product list now includes motor rotors for embodied/humanoid robots and rare-earth recycling, alongside the NdFeB magnets that go into EV traction motors and wind turbines.
deep_cut_fact: He studied metallic materials and heat treatment at Beihang University (BS 1991, MEng 1995) and his first post-graduate job was deputy chief engineer at Zhuhai Tiannian Bioengineering (1995-98) - a biotech detour before rare-earth magnets.
current_role: Director and co-actual controller (~9.1%), JL MAG Rare-Earth Co. (SZSE: 300748; HKEX: 6680); Executive Director & GM, Hunan Boxun Investment Holding Group
research_notes: Non-executive at JL MAG; very low media profile. Relevant to energy/EV/robotics supply-chain themes (rare-earth magnets).

name: Guan Jianzhong
profile: Guan Jianzhong founded Zhejiang Jiahua Energy Chemical, a Jiaxing (Zhapu port) chemicals and industrial-steam/energy producer that backdoor-listed in 2014 via Huafang Textile. He was its chairman and controlling shareholder and appeared on the Hurun China list 2015-2021, but stepped down from all roles at the company in August 2020.
interesting_fact: Jiahua Energy went public in 2014 not by IPO but via a 100% asset swap with listed Huafang Textile (华芳纺织), a backdoor listing that turned a textile shell into a chemicals and energy company.
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Zhejiang Jiahua Energy Chemical (嘉化能源, SSE: 600273); resigned all company posts in August 2020

He has no current company role, so the listed IR emails (board secretary Wang Qingying; securities rep Zhang Bingyang) are company contacts, not his. Probably low priority.

profile: Southeast University-trained semiconductor engineer who founded Wuxi Chipown, a fabless designer of power-management ICs (AC-DC/DC-DC converters, gate drivers) for appliances, industrial and automotive uses. profile: Co-founder (b. 1968) with husband Zou Zhinong and Zhu Guodong of TFC Optical Communication, a Suzhou maker of passive optical components and high-speed optical-engine packaging. name: Rui Fubin
profile: Founder-chairman of Jiangnan Group, which designs, makes and sells power cables and electrical-equipment wires from Yixing's Guanlin town, a Chinese cable-making hub. He took the company public on the Hong Kong main board in April 2012 (raising roughly HK$546-789M) and later led its privatisation, with the shares delisted on 23 May 2023.
interesting_fact: Jiangnan Group listed in Hong Kong in April 2012 and was taken private again 11 years later, delisting in May 2023 - putting a major Chinese grid-cable supplier back under founder control.
current_role: Chairman and President, Jiangnan Group (江南集團), power-cable maker based in Guanlin, Yixing, Jiangsu (status after 2023 privatisation not re-verified)
research_notes: Relevant to energy/grid angle (power cables). Company now private; website sits behind bot protection and no published contact was found. Web search budget exhausted, so only Wikipedia was checked.

name: Song Yuqing
profile: Song Yuqing (宋玉庆, b. c.1960-62, Nantong, Jiangsu) started in petrochemicals and moved Zhongdeng into Xi'an real estate in 2001, building a 'petrochemicals + property' group that later spread into finance, tourism and film. A Hurun regular 2009-2015 and often in Shaanxi's top ten, he saw the group hit a debt crisis after taking on four urban-village redevelopment projects.
interesting_fact: Zhongdeng's first big Xi'an move was winning a 71-mu plot in the Economic & Technological Development Zone at auction in 2003 for RMB98m, billed then as 'the north city's first auction'; it became the Zhongdeng Jiayuan estate.
current_role: Founder of Zhongdeng Group (中登集团), Xi'an; formally exited the group's shareholding and board in 2015 but reported to still run it; current status unclear
research_notes: Sensitive: NBD (Nov 2018) reports Zhongdeng became a court-listed defaulter (30+ enforcement cases, >RMB2bn) and Xi'an Intermediate Court searched its HQ in Oct 2018; in 2015 Song and family transferred group shares to his brother Song Yu (88%) and Shen Weiding (12%). Wealth likely much reduced. Searches found no recent (post-2018) news or official contact. Avoid as outreach target or approach with care.

name: Xu Zhiwei
profile: Founded Longliqi in Changshu, Jiangsu in 1986. It became known for snake-oil skin cream, florida water (花露水), toiletries and health supplements. In 2012 he also launched the e-commerce platform 聚好商城 (Juhao Mall) as its CEO. Hurun China listed him from 2005 to 2017.
interesting_fact: Longliqi's best-known product is snake-oil cream (蛇油膏), a mass-market Chinese toiletry brand he built from Changshu starting in 1986.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Jiangsu Longliqi Group (隆力奇), Changshu (as of 2023)
research_notes: Zh Wikipedia reports that in Feb 2023 he was placed on bail by Suzhou police over alleged illegal fundraising, possibly linked to a shareholder dispute at Juhao Mall; check the current status before any outreach. No published contact email found. Search budget was exhausted, so research was limited.

name: Zhang Yibin
profile: Zhang Yibin (张亦斌) is understood to be the founder of New Sea Union, a Suzhou telecom-equipment firm founded in 1997 and listed in Shenzhen in 2006. It later diversified into optical communications, LED chips (with the CAS Nano institute), quantum communications and electric-vehicle stakes. Hurun listed him with Ma Lingzhi from 2009 to 2017.
interesting_fact: New Sea Union co-founded LED chip maker Xinnajing with the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Suzhou nano institute in 2011, building a full epitaxy-to-package LED lighting chain with 40 MOCVD reactors.
current_role: Founder and former chairman, New Sea Union Technology Group (新海宜, SZSE: 002089), Suzhou (not current chairman; current chairman is Huang Fei)
research_notes: Mapping of 'New Sea' to 新海宜 (002089) is inferred from Hurun's industry and co-listed name; his founder role was not confirmed in an accessible source. The company has carried ST/*ST (special-treatment) status, he no longer chairs it, and he has been off Hurun since 2017. The wealth figure is stale; low priority.

profile: Ma Lingzhi (b. Sept 1962) co-founded Suzhou-based telecom-equipment maker New Sea Union (Xinhaiyi, SZSE: 002089, listed 2006) with her husband Zhang Yibin, the largest shareholder; she was the No. 2 shareholder (16.46% at end-2019). She rose from marketing director to vice president and stepped down in 2019.

deep_cut_fact: She started her career in 1986 as a teacher at Suzhou Vocational University, then became marketing director of Suzhou Haiyi Telecom Equipment, the predecessor business, before helping build New Sea Union.
current_role: No current public role found; co-founder and former vice president (resigned 2019) of New Sea Union Technology Group (Suzhou)

name: Tang Yongqing
profile: Tang Yongqing founded Jiangsu Yulong Steel Pipe in Wuxi in 1999 and chaired it through its Shanghai listing, making welded steel pipe (LSAW, SSAW, ERW) used mainly for oil and gas transmission lines and structural steel. The family later exited; the listed shell became Shandong Yulong Gold and voluntarily delisted in 2025.
interesting_fact: Yulong's line pipe went into oil and natural-gas transmission, and by 2014 it had developed corrosion-resistant pipe for oil/gas gathering lines, coal-chemical plants, power-station heat exchangers and seawater-desalination systems.
deep_cut_fact: He set up the company in December 1999 with RMB 8 million (80% of capital) — RMB 2 million in cash plus RMB 6 million of net assets he took over from the old Jiangsu Yulong Steel Pipe Group — registered in Wuxi's Huishan district.
current_role: Former chairman and co-actual controller of Jiangsu Yulong Steel Pipe (SSE 601028); no current listed-company role found
research_notes: Off the rich lists since 2017; listed company changed hands and was delisted in 2025, so old Yulong contacts are stale. No current published contact found. Oil/gas pipe gives a loose energy angle. Search budget exhausted.

profile: Shen Guangqian (b. 1961) led Beijing Leadman Biochemistry, an in-vitro diagnostics maker of biochemical reagents, as chairman and president and took it public on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2012. He resigned in March 2018; control of Leadman has since passed to Guangzhou High-tech Zone Science & Technology Holding, a state-owned investor.
interesting_fact: Under him Leadman built a reference laboratory to ISO 17025/ISO 15195 standards, unusual for a Chinese diagnostics firm, to make its own key raw materials and reduce reliance on imports.
current_role: Former chairman and president (to March 2018) and large shareholder of Beijing Leadman Biochemistry (SZSE: 300289); current role not found
public_contact: office_email: leadman@leadmanbio.com (Leadman company email; he no longer runs the firm)
research_notes: Stepped down from Leadman in 2018 and has no current public role found; very low profile. Alive status not verified (no recent mention found; web search budget exhausted). Leadman contact is a weak route.

deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he took over a struggling local enterprise, overhauled its equipment, talent and products, and grew annual sales to nearly 100m yuan by 1999, earning a local reputation as a turnaround 'nengren' (go-getter).

name: Dong Li
profile: Dong Li founded Shenzhen-born battery maker Leoch in 1999 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2010. Leoch is China's top lead-acid battery exporter (100+ countries, ~$1.4B+ turnover) and has added lithium and energy-storage products for telecom, data-centre and grid use; he was re-elected executive director in 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he announced a 4GW/yr lithium battery factory in Anhui aimed partly at telecoms and data centres, while backing bipolar lead technology via US startup Gridtential - insisting lithium 'will not kill lead.'

current_role: Founder, Chairman & Executive Director, Leoch International Technology (HKEX: 842)
