interesting_fact: ASAC made the R5 mooring chains holding China's deep-water rig 'Haiyang Shiyou 981' (which rode out Typhoon Meihua in 2011), delivered the world's first R6-grade mooring chain in 2021, and led drafting of ISO 20438 on mooring chains - relevant to offshore oil and floating wind.
deep_cut_fact: To learn quality standards he wrote a registered letter to a Beijing research institute asking for China's national anchor-chain standard, and got it. In winter 1995 he flew alone to Singapore and on day 17 landed an $800,000 order that saved the factory; he named it 'Asian Star' hoping it would become 'the star of Asia'.
current_role: Founder and non-executive director (re-elected May 2026), Jiangsu Asian Star Anchor Chain Co. (ASAC, SSE: 601890), Jingjiang; son Tao Xing is chairman
research_notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (offshore oil & gas, offshore wind mooring). Son Tao Xing (b. 1990, Univ. of Melbourne) is chairman/legal rep and more media-facing (Liaowang Dongfang Weekly interview, 2024). Board secretary tel 0523-84686986.

name: Liu Jiangshan
profile: Liu Jiangshan (刘江山) founded the Shahe Carbon Black Factory in Shahe, Hebei in 1994 with 6,000 t/yr capacity and chaired it through its conversion into Longxing Chemical, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Longxing is now a top-10 Chinese carbon black and silica maker for tyres, with bases in Hebei, Henan, Shanxi and Chongqing. Liu Pengda has been chairman since 2020.
interesting_fact: From a 6,000-tonne carbon-black works in 1994, Longxing grew into a national 'green factory' (2023), uses an 'industrial internet + energy management' model, and was starting trial output on a 200,000 t/yr Shanxi line in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Longxing's high-dispersion silica (白炭黑) spent years in development: production started in 2014, and only in 2020 did it reach mass production qualified by tyre makers, diversifying the company beyond carbon black.
current_role: Controlling shareholder & actual controller (~19.5%), Longxing Chemical (龙星化工, SZSE: 002442); former chairman
research_notes: Family business: brothers and relatives are also shareholders. No published IR email found in the searched filings; the route is Longxing's securities department via SZSE filings or the irm.cninfo.com.cn interactive platform. As Sany's long-time chief engineer he led its concrete-pump-truck technology; he remains a Sany Heavy director and executive president.

current_role: Director and executive president of Sany Heavy Industry (SSE: 600031); director, executive president and chief engineer of Sany Group

research_notes: Low public profile. His chip-design background (Apex, Geehy MCUs) gives some semiconductor angle. Route via the Ninestar securities office.

interesting_fact: Baotailong's board describes Jiao as the founder who spent years 'deep in the coal-chemical industry' and notes he is a deputy to China's National People's Congress.
current_role: Founder, actual controller and honorary chairman (since June 2026), Baotailong New Materials (SSE: 601011), Qitaihe, Heilongjiang
research_notes: Stepped back from the chair in June 2026. Company's published securities-office mailbox (board secretary Liu Xin) is the only public route found. Low media profile.

name: Wu Haijun
profile: Wu Haijun (吴海军, b. 1966, Rudong, Jiangsu) founded New World Group in Shenzhen in 1995, which grew into Hasee, the low-price PC and gaming-laptop maker that was China's No. 2 domestic computer brand by 2008. Hasee tried four times to list on ChiNext (2010-2013) without completing an IPO; the company remains private and still sells laptops and gaming PCs.
interesting_fact: Hasee became a household name in China in 2002 with its CCTV ad slogan '四千八百八，奔四扛回家' (take a Pentium 4 home for 4,880 yuan), a price-war move that undercut major brands.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his company, Wu was a schoolteacher in Rudong County (1984-88), then earned a master's degree in power engineering (动力工程) at Southeast University (1991-94) and briefly worked at AVIC's Shenzhen group in 1994.
current_role: Chairman & president, Shenzhen Hasee Computer Co. (神舟电脑) and its parent Shenzhen New World Group (新天下集团), per most recent available bios
public_contact: official_website: http://www.hasee.com/ | contact_form: http://www.hasee.com/about/contact (corporate contact page; HQ switchboard +86-755-36388585, general service@hasee.com)
research_notes: Very low international profile; no press/IR contact published (company is unlisted). Deep-cut bio comes from a user-edited Chinese bio site (maigoo) - double-check before use. Approach via Chinese-language letter to Hasee HQ. Current status not confirmed by 2025-26 sources.

name: Wang Weifeng
profile: Wang Weifeng (王伟峰), son of founder Wang Boxing, helped run Jiangsu Zhongli Group, a Changshu maker of specialty cables and solar (Tenghui PV) products; he was GM from 2019 and chairman from Aug 2022. Zhongli is now a subsidiary of state-linked Xiamen C&D, chaired by Zhuang Yu'an, and Wang no longer appears among its officers.
interesting_fact: Zhongli, founded in 1988, grew from communication/specialty cables into solar via its Tenghui (腾晖) PV subsidiary; it now sells cables to rail, marine, mining and new-energy markets in 80+ countries.
deep_cut_fact: He studied for his undergraduate degree at York University (Canada) and later earned an MBA from Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
current_role: Former Chairman & GM of Jiangsu Zhongli Group (002309.SZ); no longer listed in its management after Xiamen C&D (建发股份) took control. Current role not found.
research_notes: Family lost control of Zhongli in a restructuring (now controlled by Xiamen C&D, 600153.SH); avoid financial topics. No published personal contact found. Education detail from aggregator (MarketScreener); verify before use. Hurun pairs him with father Wang Boxing.

name: Wang Yonghui
profile: Founded Guangzhou-based Xiangxue Pharmaceutical in 1997, a traditional Chinese medicine maker listed in Shenzhen; has served as chairman and general manager since 2010 per third-party data. Also listed as director of related entities such as Guangzhou Kunlun Investment.
interesting_fact: Founded Xiangxue Pharmaceutical in December 1997 and still runs it as chairman/GM.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Xiangxue Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300147), Guangzhou
research_notes: One aggregator lists Huang Weihua as chairman from 2019, conflicting with others; verify current title in latest CNINFO annual report. No public personal channels found; route via company board secretary (contact in annual report). Searches limited by budget.

name: Chen Shumei
profile: Chen Shumei (b. 1963) is listed by Hurun jointly with Xiangxue Pharmaceutical chairman Wang Yonghui. She sat on the board of Guangzhou Xiangxue Pharmaceutical (SZ:300147, modern TCM) from 2010 to 2016, after posts in Huangpu district foreign-trade bureau and as GM of Kunlun Technology; she is now a supervisor of Kunlun Investment.
interesting_fact: Before entering business she worked as an engineer at the Guangzhou Wanbao Group washing-machine factory, the same Wanbao group where Wang Yonghui was a technical-development head.
deep_cut_fact: Her official bio lists an early civil-service post as deputy section chief at the Guangzhou Huangpu District Foreign Economic & Trade Bureau before she ran Kunlun Technology.
current_role: Supervisor, Kunlun Investment (controlling holder of Guangzhou Xiangxue Pharmaceutical); former Xiangxue director (2010-2016)
research_notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Xiangxue is currently ST-flagged and in pre-restructuring per 2026 filings, so approach via the company board office may be slow. Hurun last listed her 2020.

name: Huang Zhaochun
profile: Huang Zhaochun (黄昭纯) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2014-2015 with an estimated $470M, held jointly with Huang Hongming, from the property developer Chuanghong (创鸿). No English-language or accessible Chinese sources could be found to confirm the company's location, his current role or recent activity.
current_role: Listed with Huang Hongming as owner of Chuanghong (创鸿), a real-estate group, on the Hurun China list (2014-2015). Current role not verified.
research_notes: Very low public profile and dropped off Hurun after 2015. Identity and company details are unverified (Baidu Baike was blocked from this environment). Not a strong podcast fit (real estate).

name: Shen Jiansheng
profile: Shen Jiansheng (沈健生) is co-controlling shareholder, with Shen Yulan, of Yinbang Clad Material, one of China's largest makers of aluminium clad plate, strip and foil for brazing. Its products go mainly into heat exchangers for cars and home appliances. The company listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2012, and he still runs it as chairman and GM; he sat on the board as recently as April 2026.
interesting_fact: Yinbang is among China's largest producers of aluminium brazing clad materials. These are the sheets inside car radiators and air-conditioner heat exchangers, a supply chain that also matters for thermal management in EVs and data centres.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2023 he led Yinbang to Aluminium Stewardship Initiative Performance Standard certification for its Wuxi plant, saying 'We are pleased to pass the ASI Performance Standard certification.' He framed it as a step toward green, low-carbon and digital management.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Yinbang Clad Material Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300337), Wuxi
public_contact: contact_form: Investor Q&A via the Panorama (全景网) investor relations interactive platform, as stated in company notices; board secretary Gu Yiming handles investor communication
research_notes: Low public profile. The company website (yinbang.com) was access-restricted from here. The published IR email and phone are in the company's annual reports on cninfo.com.cn. Heat-exchanger materials give an angle into energy and data-centre cooling.

name: Shen Yulan
profile: Shen Yulan (b. 1988) is the son of Yinbang founder/chairman Shen Jiansheng; father and son jointly control Wuxi-based Yinbang Clad Material, a maker of aluminium-alloy clad strip and foil for brazed heat exchangers (auto, HVAC, power). The pair held ~80% pre-IPO before the 2012 ChiNext listing; a May 2026 filing still names him a controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Yinbang developed its own brazing aluminium-alloy clad plate/strip/foil in 2005, the core product behind its growth supplying heat-exchanger makers.
deep_cut_fact: He was listed first among the 45 individual founding promoters when Yinbang was converted into a joint-stock company on 8 Dec 2010, when he was about 22.
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and actual controller (with father Shen Jiansheng) of Yinbang Clad Material Co. (SZSE: 300337); not a listed executive
research_notes: Low public profile; father Shen Jiansheng is chairman and the public face. IR email is from the 2012 prospectus; confirm in the latest annual report. Best route is via the company securities office.

name: Su Tingbao
profile: Born 1954, Inner Mongolia-based mining entrepreneur. Founded Rongda Mining in Dec 2001 (lead-zinc/non-ferrous exploration, mining and processing); in 2014 Chihong Zinc & Germanium bought his remaining 49% of Rongda for shares and cash, making him Chihong's largest individual shareholder. Has since gradually sold down part of that stake.
interesting_fact: The 2014 deal folded his privately built Rongda Mining into Chihong, one of the world's leading germanium producers, turning a private miner's stake into ~250m listed shares.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from university he worked as a fuel attendant at the Gaoqiao petrol station in Huludao, Liaoning, then in the Gaoqiao development zone's general office, before going into mining in the late 1990s.
current_role: Chairman, Rongda Mining (Xinbaerhu Youqi, Hulunbuir); largest individual shareholder of Yunnan Chihong Zinc & Germanium (600497.SH)
research_notes: Very low-profile; Chinese-language sources only. Chihong is state-controlled (Chinalco/Yunnan Metallurgical), so its IR desk is not his office. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Wang Weibin
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2014-2021) for Suntrans (real estate, arts). A Prabook profile says he founded Suntrans Group at 25 with RMB100,000, built businesses in biology, IT and Beijing real estate, and in 2000 formed Beijing Suntrans Tiandi Technological Development Corp. to make educational software. Little else is published in English or Chinese search results.
interesting_fact: Per Prabook, he invested RMB20m in 'Suntrans Intelligent Educational Software' covering junior and senior high-school maths, physics and chemistry.
current_role: Founder, Suntrans Group (Beijing) (per a single third-party bio)
research_notes: Very low public profile; only one third-party bio found (Prabook, unverified, page blocked to direct fetch). Chinese company name for Suntrans not confirmed. No published contacts found.

name: Zhu Jinhui
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Mingtai'. Searches in English and Chinese could not link a person named Zhu Jinhui to Henan Mingtai Aluminum (SSE: 601677) or any other Mingtai company, so identity could not be confirmed.
research_notes: Unverified identity: name romanization may differ (Chinese characters unknown). If this is Henan Mingtai Aluminum (601677, Zhengzhou/Gongyi), check its annual report for controlling shareholders before outreach.

name: Hu Delin
profile: Hu Delin (胡德霖, Hurun lists as 胡德林) was founder, chairman and co-controlling shareholder of Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Academy (EETI, SZSE 300215), a high/low-voltage electrical equipment testing firm. He died on 3 May 2023 aged 72; the company announced it on 26 June 2023.
interesting_fact: He led the 1999 restructuring of the state-run Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Research Institute into a private company and took it public on ChiNext in May 2011.
research_notes: Deceased (May 2023, source: Sina Finance 2023-06-26). Son Hu Chun (胡醇, Hurun co-listee) is now controlling shareholder of EETI (300215.SZ).

name: Hu Chun
profile: Hu Chun (b. 1978) is the son of Hu Delin, who led the privatisation of the Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Research Institute (founded 1965, restructured 2000) into EETI, one of China's largest third-party testing labs for high/low-voltage electrical, wind, solar and EV-charging equipment. He was chairman in 2019-21 and 2022-23 and remains its controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: EETI runs national testing centres for electrical products, smart-grid switchgear and explosion-proof equipment, and is an accredited IECEx and IECEE-CB lab, making it a key gatekeeper for China's grid and renewable-equipment makers.
deep_cut_fact: Long before becoming chairman in November 2019, he served as a director and deputy general manager of the testing institute from 2002 to 2016. In July 2026 the company disclosed he had become a Canadian citizen.
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Academy Co. (EETI, SZSE: 300215); no longer a director since June 2025
public_contact: contact_form: http://www.eeti.cn/Contact/ | official_website: http://www.eeti.cn (company; general service email eservice@eeti.cn)
research_notes: Company site is EETI (eeti.cn); the company is chaired by Yuan Lei since July 2025. Board governance disputes in 2022-23 between Hu Chun and his father Hu Delin were widely reported, so avoid that topic. No personal public channels found; route via company board secretary/IR (SZSE 300215).

name: Chen Wei
profile: Chen Wei (陈玮), a Xiamen University accounting PhD and former university lecturer, spent about seven years at Shenzhen Capital Group (rising to president) before founding Oriental Fortune Capital in 2006. The VC firm now manages close to RMB 40bn and has backed 600+ companies (e.g. Kunlun Tech, Jiuxian.com). He remains chairman and an active industry spokesman.
interesting_fact: When the 2008 crisis led LPs to cancel staged commitments, Oriental Fortune's first fund shrank from RMB 900m to under RMB 350m; Chen says he personally borrowed RMB 80m to keep the firm going.
deep_cut_fact: He came to venture capital by accident: in 1999, aged 35 and just back from a visiting-scholar stint in the Netherlands, he wanted to join the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, but the ChiNext board was delayed and hiring frozen, so he applied to Shenzhen Capital instead.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shenzhen Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海); chairman of the Shenzhen Venture Capital Association
research_notes: Source of wealth 'Oriental Fortune' = Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海), not Eastmoney (东方财富). Very public VC figure; frequent speaker at Chinese VC forums. No published press email found; the company website did not load from here. Best route: the firm's official channels.

name: Tang Guoqiang
profile: Tang Guoqiang (汤国强, b. c.1957), from Liyang, Jiangsu, chaired Shunfeng Photovoltaic International when it listed in Hong Kong in July 2011. Through his company Peace Link he owned about 29.65% of the solar-cell maker. He left the chair in mid-2013, before the group's 2014 takeover of Wuxi Suntech, and has kept no public profile since. Hurun listed him once, in 2014.
interesting_fact: He came to solar late. His earlier jobs were running Liyang Economic Development Corp (metals wholesale, 1990-96), deputy GM of a Liyang fine-chemicals maker (1996-2003) and a director of a Zhenjiang property developer (2003-07). He joined Jiangsu Shunfeng PV's board only in April 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Per the company's 2011 annual report, his formal education ended with a high-school diploma from Jiangsu Province Liyang Middle School in 1977, the year China restored the national college entrance exam.
current_role: Former chairman (2011-2013) of Shunfeng Photovoltaic International (HKEX: 1165, now Shunfeng International Clean Energy); no current role found
research_notes: Identity confirmed from Shunfeng PV's 2011 annual report on HKEX (chairman; 100% owner of Peace Link, which held 29.65%). MarketScreener shows his chairmanship ending 1 Jul 2013. No current activity or published contact found. Not the actor Tang Guoqiang. The '1977 college-exam' note is historical context, not a claim about him.

name: Xu Qi
profile: Xu Qi (徐琦) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2010-2021 for Sunleader, an electronic-components business. A third-party data aggregator (MarketScreener) lists a Qi Xu as CEO of Shenzhen Sunleader Electronic Group (founded 1993), but no primary source was found to confirm details.
current_role: Reportedly CEO, Shenzhen Sunleader Electronic Group (unverified)
research_notes: Very low public profile; no official company website, interviews or contacts found. Not to be confused with Sunlord Electronics (顺络电子, 002138), a different company. Would need Chinese business registry (e.g. Qichacha) research to confirm.

name: Guo Hongsheng
profile: Shenyang-born (1962) engineer-entrepreneur who founded the SBS Group in 1996, building Shenyang Blue Silver Industry Automation Equipment (tyre/rubber-processing automation, digital factory systems) into a Shenzhen-listed company. In 2017 he bought Dürr AG's industrial cleaning & surface-processing business, now SBS Ecoclean, which he runs from Germany as Group CEO.
interesting_fact: A Chinese automation founder who personally runs a German Mittelstand engineering group: SBS took majority control of Dürr Ecoclean (founded 1956, Filderstadt) on 1 April 2017 and he has been its Group CEO since.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the SBS Group in 1996 under the motto "technology drives the future" - a line Ecoclean still prints in his official management bio.
current_role: Founder of Shenyang Blue Silver (SBS) Group / Blue Silver Industry Automation Equipment (SZSE: 300293); Managing Director & Group CEO, SBS Ecoclean Group (Germany)
research_notes: Name spellings vary (Guo Hongsheng / Hongsheng Guo / Hong Sheng Guo). Best route is probably via SBS Ecoclean in Germany (English-language corporate comms) rather than the Shenyang listed company. Industrial cleaning for EV/battery and hydrogen components could be a podcast angle.

name: Yao Xiaoqing
profile: Yao Xiaoqing (姚小青) founded Tianjin Chase Sun Pharmaceutical, a Shenzhen ChiNext-listed maker of traditional Chinese medicine injectables (notably Xuebijing) and formula granules. He led it as chairman for years; in 2024 he resigned all posts a year early as state-owned Chengdu Xingcheng Group took control, though he remained a ~10% holder.
interesting_fact: Chase Sun's control passed to Chengdu's state-owned Xingcheng Group; Yao resigned as chairman and legal representative on 1 April 2024, a year before his term ended, while keeping about 10.24% of the shares.
current_role: Founder and ~10% shareholder of Tianjin Chase Sun Pharmaceutical (300026.SZ); stepped down as chairman April 2024, no current company post
research_notes: Low public profile; no longer holds a role at Chase Sun. Any outreach would have to go via Chase Sun's board secretary/IR office (published in its exchange filings), which no longer represents him.

name: Ye Zhehua
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2014-2021) with Ye Jian as owners of 'Kunlun', a real estate/investment group (net worth ~US$470m). Searches in English and Chinese (叶哲华 昆仑) returned no verifiable information linking this person to a specific company.
research_notes: Could not identify which 'Kunlun' entity this is (many unrelated Chinese firms use the name). Needs Chinese business-registry lookup (e.g. Qichacha) to confirm; no public contacts found.

name: Ye Jian
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2021 (with Ye Zhehua) with wealth from 'Kunlun' in real estate and investment (~US$470m). Searches could not tie this name to a specific Kunlun-branded company; there are several unrelated Kunlun groups (Kunlun Tech, Kunlun Energy, etc.).
research_notes: Identity not confirmed: the Kunlun entity behind this Hurun listing could not be identified; do not assume a link to Kunlun Tech or Kunlun Energy. No public contacts found.

name: Hu Zuliu
profile: Fred Hu Zuliu is a Harvard-trained economist who worked at the IMF, then became Goldman Sachs' Partner and Chairman of Greater China. In 2010 he founded Primavera Capital, an Asia growth-equity firm that backed Alibaba, Ant Group, ByteDance, Kuaishou, Xpeng and Yum China; he still runs it and chairs its investment committee.
interesting_fact: Primavera initiated or led investments in Alibaba, Cainiao, Ant Group, Yum China, ByteDance, Xpeng, Kuaishou and SenseTime; Hu also sits on the boards of UBS Group and ICBC.
deep_cut_fact: Before economics he trained as an engineer, earning a Master in Engineering Science at Tsinghua before his Harvard PhD; he is also a trustee of Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study and co-chairs The Nature Conservancy's Asia Pacific Council.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Primavera Capital Group; non-executive chairman, Yum China
public_contact: press_email: media@primavera-capital.com | ir_email: ir@primavera-capital.com | office_email: contact@primavera-capital.com | official_website: https://www.primavera-capital.com/
research_notes: Frequent speaker at WEF, Milken and HKU AsiaGlobal events; conference circuit is a natural route. Writes WEF agenda pieces.

name: Xu Jie
profile: Xu Jie (徐捷) founded Phoenix Healthcare, which grew from private hospitals into China's largest private hospital group by beds and visits and listed in Hong Kong in 2013 as the 'first private-hospital stock'. In 2016 China Resources took control; her family vehicle SpeedKey exited and she stepped down as chair. No public role since.
interesting_fact: Phoenix Healthcare's 2013 Hong Kong IPO made it the first listed private-hospital operator from mainland China; it pioneered investing in and managing public and SOE-owned hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2013 IPO prospectus, she bought the Jilin City Trauma Hospital (吉林市创伤医院) in 1988 and personally served as its legal representative and hospital director until 1995, before investing in hospitals in Dalian and Wuxi and founding Beijing Phoenix in 2007 with RMB45m of her own capital.
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Phoenix Healthcare Group (now China Resources Medical, HKEX: 1515); current role not publicly reported
research_notes: Very low public profile since the 2016 China Resources takeover; company contacts (China Resources Medical) no longer represent her. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Huang Mingsong
profile: Huang Mingsong (黄明松), born 1971, holds a master's degree. He leads CSG Smart Science & Technology, founded in Shanghai in 2002 with links to the University of Science and Technology of China. Listed in 2011, it makes smart power-distribution automation, EV charging and energy management systems, industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics is a strategic investor.
interesting_fact: CSG Smart combines grid tech (distribution automation, EV energy management) with industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics invested about RMB 618m as a strategic investor in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before scaling CSG Smart he ran a cluster of USTC-linked ventures, including Anhui Keda Luneng Technology and Anhui Keda Smart Grid Technology. He also sits on the board of the Shanghai Fuke Intelligent Robot Research Institute.
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (about 24.6%), CSG Smart Science & Technology (科大智能, 300222.SZ), Shanghai
research_notes: 'CSG Smart' = 科大智能 (not China Southern Grid). A 2026 report says Wang Tingting succeeded him as president (CEO) ahead of a Hong Kong listing application; he remains chairman per the latest board filings we found. IR email is the board-secretary address from the Jan 2025 board-election notice.

name: Huang Ruohong
profile: Huang Ruohong (Wong Yeuk Hung, 黄若虹) founded Redco Properties, a Shenzhen-headquartered residential developer listed in Hong Kong, and is its controlling shareholder (about 40%). He has chaired the board since March 2017. The company, like many Chinese developers, has been working through a difficult property market.
interesting_fact: He became Redco's board chairman and an executive director in March 2017 in his capacity as controlling shareholder, after building the developer from its Fujian/Jiangxi roots into an HKEX-listed group.
deep_cut_fact: He holds the Hong Kong title of Justice of the Peace (JP), is a member of a national CPPCC committee and serves as vice chairman of the Hong Kong Federation of Fujian Associations.
current_role: Executive Director and Chairman, Redco Properties Group (HKEX: 1622)
research_notes: Known in HK filings as Wong Yeuk Hung. No published IR email found; check latest HKEX annual report for company secretary / IR contact. Avoid referencing the company's debt situation in outreach.

name: Mo Shuming
profile: Dongguan-born entrepreneur who co-founded Guangdong Mingcrown Group (名冠集团) in 1994 with Mo Zhiming. The family conglomerate spans construction, real estate, steel/new materials (Huaguan), Xinhui Port logistics, hotels, schools and a golf club; it is now chaired by Mo Guanliang and ranks among Guangdong's top 500 companies.
interesting_fact: Mingcrown is pivoting into culture-tourism: in March 2026 it won Dongguan's first land auction of the year for RMB 730m to build the Mingcrown Oasis theme-park project, and signed a strategic deal with Tencent Cloud in April 2026.
current_role: Co-founder (and long-time vice chairman) of Guangdong Mingcrown Group, Dongguan
research_notes: Very low public profile; the group site names him only as co-founder. A 2012 Xinhui district government page called him vice chairman of Mingcrown. Day-to-day leadership is now Mo Guanliang (chairman) and Mo Guanjing (president). Hurun listed him jointly with Yao Hesong. Best route is the group's corporate email.

name: Xia Hua
profile: Xia Hua (夏华) left a law lectureship at China University of Political Science and Law to found menswear company Eve (依文) in 1994, building it into a leading Chinese menswear brand. She now focuses on Eve China Handmade, which links rural ethnic-minority embroiderers in Guizhou, Yunnan and Sichuan with global fashion through digital pattern libraries and IP licensing.
interesting_fact: Her China Handmade platform works with more than 25,000 rural embroiderers; she cites a Miao artisan, 'Grandma Pan', whose family embroidery business earns over 1.8 million yuan a year.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Eve she quit her teaching post and became a shop-floor salesperson at a Xidan mall in Beijing, becoming its top seller within a month by studying which stores' bags shoppers carried. She later funded an 'Eve Distinguished Professor' fund at her alma mater CUPL (2003).
current_role: Chairwoman, Eve Group (依文集团), Beijing; founder of Eve China Handmade; vice chair, All-China Chamber of Commerce (ACFIC); NPC deputy
research_notes: High-profile public figure in China (NPC deputy, ACFIC vice chair, frequent Xinhua interviewee); best route is via Eve Group corporate office. Hurun listing 'Eve' = 依文.

name: Gong Sheng
profile: Gong Sheng is the long-serving president of Jiangsu Shagang Group, China's largest private steelmaker (about 40m tonnes of crude steel in 2023). He took over as president from founder Shen Wenrong in 2011, after serving as vice president, and holds a shareholding in the group. He still runs operations under chairman Shen Bin.
interesting_fact: He succeeded founder Shen Wenrong as Shagang's president in 2011 and has run day-to-day operations of China's biggest private steelmaker for more than a decade.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2026 he personally led a site visit to Shagang's Huaigang special-steel subsidiary, which reflects his hands-on, plant-floor management style.
current_role: Standing Executive Director and President, Jiangsu Shagang Group (Zhangjiagang)
research_notes: Low public profile, and there is almost no personal biography online. The best route is the Shagang Group board office (集团董事局 常委办公室) email. Listed arm: Jiangsu Shagang Co (002075.SZ).

name: Wan Jie
profile: Beijing-born (1962) founder-chairman of Artron, set up in Shenzhen in 1993 as a high-end art printer. He expanded it into China's largest art-data and online art portal (artron.net) with bases in Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen. A long-time CPPCC National Committee member, he also served as a vice-president of the Palace Museum Academy.
interesting_fact: Artron grew from fine-art book printing into a digital art database business; in 2022 Wan used his CPPCC proposals to push metaverse and digital-culture infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2014 'Two Sessions' he proposed a national copyright-registration system for Chinese calligraphy and paintings to clean up forgery in the art market.
current_role: Chairman, Artron Art Group (雅昌文化集团), Shenzhen
public_contact: official_website: https://www.artron.net/ | office_email: help@artron.net (general Artron portal helpdesk, not personal)
research_notes: Best route is via Artron Group corporate channels; little English-language coverage. Industry listed as Print but now primarily art data/culture.

name: Zhang Yaping
profile: Shanxi entrepreneur Zhang Yaping (张亚平) started in coal trading and mine acquisitions, then founded Donghui in 2003. It was once China's largest stamp-charged coke producer and now has about 19bn yuan in assets. The group spans coal, non-ferrous metals, new materials and tourism, and holds 7.5% of Shanghai-listed Kexin Development.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Donghui paid A$160M for an Australian copper-gold miner, making it the first private Shanxi company to buy mines overseas. The group has since added Wutai Mountain tourism, a Marriott hotel, EV in-wheel motors and modern agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: Hurun's 2017 business-jet owners report listed him with an Embraer Legacy 650, then the only private jet owned by a Shanxi tycoon. He first built capital as a coal trader and by buying the Dengjiazhuang mine in Liulin county.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shanxi Donghui Energy Group (coal, coking, non-ferrous metals, new materials, cultural tourism)
research_notes: Very private; no official group website or press contact found. In June 2026 Shanxi securities regulators fined Donghui's investment arm over undisclosed share buying in Kexin Development. Approach cautiously, in Chinese. Hurun's 'Donghui Coal Coking & Chemicals' (2010-12) now trades as Shanxi Donghui Energy Group.

name: Chen Jianxing
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-2021) as sharing a Wens Foodstuff fortune with Wen Xiaoqiong, one of the Wen family members named as actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (Guangdong pig and poultry producer). No public filings or press found naming a 陈建兴 in a Wens director or executive role.
interesting_fact: Wens grew from a 'seven households, eight shares' rural partnership in 1983 into a company with thousands of employee-shareholders, after introducing an all-employee shareholding scheme in 1986.
current_role: Shareholder associated with Wens Foodstuff Group (per Hurun listing); no current public role found
research_notes: Could not confirm identity or role from public sources; appears to be a passive family shareholder rather than an executive. Contact only via Wens corporate channels (website/IR). Very low public profile.

name: Wen Xiaoqiong
profile: Wen Xiaoqiong (温小琼) is one of the Wen family members named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group, China's largest hog and broiler producer. Wens was founded by her father Wen Beiying (per press reports) in 1983. She was among the top pre-IPO individual shareholders and is a passive shareholder rather than a manager.
interesting_fact: Wens began in 1983 when Wen Beiying raised 8,000 yuan from seven village families in Xinxing, Guangdong to start a chicken farm; it became China's largest livestock company, listing in Shenzhen in 2015.
current_role: Member of the Wen family group named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (SZSE: 300498); no executive role disclosed
research_notes: Very private; no public profile. Listed among Wens actual controllers in the 2023 annual report. Only route is the Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn). Hurun listing was shared with Chen Jianxing (also a listed controller).

name: Wen Junsheng
profile: Wen Junsheng (温均生) is a member of the founding Wen family behind Wens Foodstuff Group, China's large pig/poultry producer founded by his father Wen Beifen in 1983. He remains on the 10-person actual-controller group named under the family's renewed concert-party agreement (2025), per the company's 2026 interim report.
interesting_fact: Per Jiemian, he is Wen Beifen's eldest son and the father of Wen Jiaolong, the first third-generation family member added as an actual controller and to the Wens board.
current_role: One of the 10 actual controllers (Wen family concert group) of Wens Foodstuff Group (300498.SZ)
research_notes: No personal profile/executive post found; low public profile. Approach via Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn, tel published 0766-2292926). Alive status not explicitly confirmed, but listed as controller in Aug 2026 filing.

name: Liu Rongjiao
profile: Hurun lists Liu Rongjiao (with Wen Junsheng) as a shareholder in Wens Foodstuff Group, China's large pig and chicken producer founded in Guangdong. Wens' 2024 interim report names a '刘容娇' (variant character) among the 10 people making up the Wen family / actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Wens' 2024 interim report defines its actual controller as the 'Wen family', a group of 10 individuals including 刘容娇, rather than a single founder.
current_role: Member of the Wen family (actual controllers) of Wens Foodstuff Group, per company filings
research_notes: Hurun spelling 刘荣娇 vs filing 刘容娇 (likely same person, not confirmed). No public profile; passive family shareholder. Only route is Wens board-secretary office.

name: Yan Juran
profile: Yan Juran (b. 1962) joined the predecessor of Wens Foodstuff, China's big Guangdong-based pig and poultry producer, in 1983 and rose through vice president, technical director and executive VP to president. He was president until around 2019/20 and remains a board director; he is one of the pre-IPO founding natural-person shareholders (2.80% in 2018).
interesting_fact: A Wens 'lifer': he joined the company's predecessor in 1983 with a high-school education and worked his way up to group president of one of China's largest livestock companies.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2005 he has been vice-chairman of the Beiying Charity Foundation of Xinxing County, Guangdong (广东省新兴县北英慈善基金会), Wens' hometown charity.
current_role: Director, Wens Foodstuff Group Co. (SZSE: 300498); director, Guangdong Yuncheng Investment Holding
research_notes: Still listed as a Wens director in an Aug 2026 board resolution (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-08-31/1225537760.PDF). Low public profile; no personal channels found. dsh@ is the Wens board-secretary office email.

name: Sun Pengsheng
profile: Sun Pengsheng (b. 1958) is chairman and one of four co-controlling shareholders (acting in concert) of Jiangsu Nhwa Pharmaceutical, a Xuzhou-based maker of central nervous system drugs. He rose through Xuzhou state pharma factories and has led the Nhwa group since 1996; in April 2026 he bought 200,000 more Nhwa shares.
interesting_fact: He holds about 4.9% of Nhwa directly, and with three partners in a contractual acting-in-concert pact controls roughly 48% of the company directly and via Xuzhou Nhwa Investment.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1976 as a factory worker at Xuzhou No. 2 Pharmaceutical Factory, then from 1980 rose from technician to director at Xuzhou No. 3 Pharmaceutical Factory; he was once named one of Xuzhou's 'Top Ten Outstanding Youths' and is a CEIBS EMBA.
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Nhwa Pharmaceutical Co. (SZSE: 002262), 7th board
research_notes: Company general email published on the corporate site; also Jiangsu provincial People's Congress deputy. Route via company board secretary office.

name: Guo Yongfang
profile: Founder of Xiamen Meiya Pico (founded September 1999), which grew into a leading Chinese electronic-data-forensics and cybersecurity company and listed in Shenzhen in 2011. In 2019 she and other shareholders sold stakes to state investor SDIC, which became the controlling shareholder; the company was renamed Guotou Intelligence in January 2024. She still held 109.56 million shares in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: The company she founded is described as China's leading electronic-data-forensics firm; in 2021 it extended its blockchain virtual-currency forensics to NFTs.
current_role: Founder and >5% shareholder (about 12.7%) of Guotou Intelligence (国投智能, formerly Meiya Pico, 300188.SZ)
research_notes: Female founder, low public profile. Holding confirmed in Feb 2026 share-reduction notice (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202602101819860269_1.pdf), which says she is not a controlling shareholder. A same-name associate professor at Hebei University of Technology is a different person. IR email belongs to the company's board office.

name: Dai Wenjian
profile: Sichuan University finance graduate who was reportedly one of the partners in NVC Lighting (雷士照明) before starting a logistics business in 2005. He built Huochebang, a truck-cargo matching app launched in 2013, which merged with Yunmanman in Nov 2017 to form Manbang (Full Truck Alliance). He later moved into beef cattle farming (Dafeiniu).
interesting_fact: His first attempt at logistics matching - handing about 20,000 satellite navigation units to truckers - failed and lost over 30 million yuan before he pivoted to an app.
deep_cut_fact: Before the app, he ran 13 QQ chat groups of about 500 cargo owners and drivers each across provinces south of the Yangtze, then moved ~60% of those cargo owners onto his own platform.
current_role: Founder of Huochebang (Truck Alliance, merged into Manbang/Full Truck Alliance); reported chairman of Guizhou Aishang Dafeiniu (cattle farming)
research_notes: Sixth Tone romanizes his name as 'Dai Jianwen'. MarketScreener notes he resigned from the Full Truck Alliance board (date not seen). Current role at Dafeiniu sourced only from cnpp.cn profile (https://www.cnpp.cn/focus/231635.html). No published personal contacts found.

name: Gui Guojie
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2018-2021) with wealth from 'Zhongfang' (real estate). A MarketScreener/Zonebourse insider profile for 'Guo Jie Gui' lists him as a director of China Real Estate Group Union Investment Co., Ltd.; 'Zhongfang' (中房) plausibly abbreviates China Real Estate, but no source ties the two together.
current_role: Possibly Director, China Real Estate Group Union Investment Co., Ltd. (unconfirmed match)
research_notes: Very little public information; Chinese and English searches for 桂国杰 returned nothing substantive. Possible match: https://zonebourse.com/insider/GUO-JIE-GUI-A2CTYK/ . Verify via Chinese company registries before outreach.

name: Zhang Peike
profile: Zhang Peike (张佩珂) chairs Sunshine Global Circuits, a Shenzhen PCB maker founded in 2001 (predecessor 深圳明阳电路科技有限公司) and listed on ChiNext in Feb 2018. Zhang is also its legal representative. The company makes PCBs for AI acceleration cards, servers, optical modules and communications backplanes, exporting to Europe, North America and SE Asia.
interesting_fact: Sunshine's PCB product lines now include boards for AI acceleration cards, heterogeneous computing servers and optical modules, a direct link to data-center hardware.
current_role: Chairman and Acting General Manager, Sunshine Global Circuits Co., Ltd. (明阳电路, SZSE: 300739)
research_notes: Personal biography not found in sources read. Company has European arm (Sunshine PCB GmbH) and in 2023 acquired Vision Industries Malaysia (iconnect007). Best route is via the listed company's board secretary/IR.

name: Yan Shengjun
profile: Yan Shengjun (严圣军) built Tianying from Jiangsu into a listed environmental-energy group (China Tianying, Shenzhen-listed) focused on waste-to-energy incineration, sludge and food-waste treatment. Under him it has pivoted into new energy, licensing Energy Vault's technology to build a 25MW/100MWh gravity energy storage plant in Rudong, Jiangsu, connected to the grid in 2024.
interesting_fact: China Tianying's Rudong plant is billed as the world's first commercial-scale gravity battery: cranes lift composite blocks made partly from waste (soil, coal ash, fibreglass from retired wind blades) when power is cheap and lower them to generate power later.
deep_cut_fact: At the March 2022 groundbreaking Yan said the project would help Rudong become a Yangtze Delta 'zero-carbon industrial centre'; Tianying's deal with Rudong county also covers tidal-flat solar, offshore wind, hydrogen and a zero-carbon data centre.
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, China Tianying Inc. (000035.SZ)
research_notes: Strong energy/data-center fit (gravity storage, zero-carbon data centre plans). Low personal media profile; no personal channels found. Company site ctyi.com.cn was unreachable from here; route via China Tianying IR / board office. Hurun listed wealth jointly with Mao Hongju.

name: Mao Hongju
profile: Mao Hongju (b. 1968) and husband Yan Shengjun, the chairman, control China Tianying via two Nantong holding companies. Tianying grew from waste-to-energy and environmental services into a 2014 reverse-merger listing spanning wind, solar, green hydrogen/ammonia and gravity storage. She has been a director and VP since 2014.
interesting_fact: China Tianying is Energy Vault's partner on the 25 MW/100 MWh gravity energy storage system in Rudong, Jiangsu, next to a wind farm; it was connected to the State Grid in Dec 2023 and billed as the first commercial utility-scale non-pumped-hydro gravity storage plant.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike many founder-spouses listed as passive shareholders, she holds professional titles as a senior engineer and senior economist, and has served as Tianying's vice president since its 2014 listing (per her 2026 board nomination resume).
current_role: Director and Vice President, China Tianying Inc. (SZSE: 000035), Hai'an, Jiangsu; joint actual controller with husband Yan Shengjun
research_notes: Husband Yan Shengjun (chairman) is the public face. IR email is that of board secretary Lu Ping as published in the 2026 interim report (securities rep: zhangmma@cnty.cn). IR email is the reliable route.

name: Zhu Hanping
profile: Zhu Hanping founded Sanfeng Intelligent in 1999, a maker of intelligent conveying/automation equipment that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2011. He is the company's legal representative, chairman and holds roughly 40% of its shares.
interesting_fact: A 2019 Shanghai Securities News profile described him as having stuck with manufacturing for 20 years, saying that after earning some money working for others he wanted to build a Chinese industrial company.
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hubei Sanfeng Intelligent Conveying Equipment (Sanfeng Intelligent, SZ:300276)
research_notes: Alive status not explicitly confirmed; sources indicate he still controls the company as of 2026 data. Shares wealth with Zhu Zhe. Best route likely via company board secretary/IR of Sanfeng Intelligent (300276).

name: Li Yongkui
profile: Li Yongkui — wealth from Strong (China) Estimated net worth $470M (Hurun China, 2021).
research_notes: Hurun China lists Li Yongkui (李永奎), source of wealth 'Strong', food & beverages. Searches in English and Chinese did not turn up the company or person, so identity is unconfirmed. Try a Chinese company registry check for the legal representative of a food company named Strong (斯壮/斯强?).

name: Filip Sedic
profile: Bosnian-born Swedish inventor based in Hong Kong who founded beauty-tech brand FOREO in 2013 (LUNA, ISSA, UFO devices). Earlier he co-founded Lelo and the feminine-care brand Intimina. He still leads FOREO and its FAQ Swiss skincare line.
interesting_fact: FOREO's name stands for 'for everyone'; Sedic says 'We are probably the most copied brand in the world' and doesn't mind if copiers improve things.
deep_cut_fact: Before consumer products, he ran a digital marketing agency in Sweden in the 1990s and worked at Ericsson from 2000 to 2005.
current_role: Founder and CEO / 'chief imagination officer', FOREO (Swedish beauty-tech brand)
research_notes: Press email is FOREO Sweden's Marketing & PR manager from a Cision release (Nordic market); may be regional. Sources variously title him CEO, Chief Innovation Officer or chief imagination officer.

name: Xue Junteng
profile: Xue Junteng is a major individual shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle, China's large home-textile (bedding) maker, which is controlled by chairman Xue Weicheng. In March 2019 he agreed to sell 25.44 million shares (3.37%) to CA Fabric Investments and kept 58.78 million shares (7.79%). His exact family relationship to the Xue founders was not confirmed in the sources read.
interesting_fact: His 2019 stake sale went to CA Fabric Investments, bringing in an outside strategic investor at Luolai.
current_role: Shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle Technology (罗莱生活, SZSE: 002293); held 7.79% after a March 2019 share sale
research_notes: No biography found. Listed with Xue Weibin as wealth-sharer, but no source found linking the two. Appears to be a passive shareholder, not an executive. Route via Luolai's IR office if needed.

name: Ge Hang
profile: Ge Hang founded Hangzhou B-Soft (创业软件, later 创业慧康), a developer of hospital and healthcare information systems listed in Shenzhen. In November 2025 he agreed to transfer about 6.23% of B-Soft and delegate voting rights to Hangzhou Genghao, an investment platform of HK-listed IVD Medical, which would give the company an actual controller.
interesting_fact: In Nov 2025 Ge Hang, as B-Soft's largest shareholder, signed a share-transfer and voting-delegation deal with Hangzhou Genghao (set up by IVD Medical) at RMB5.18/share, a deal framed by media as a bet on 'AI + healthcare'.
deep_cut_fact: Crunchbase lists him as a 1984 bachelor's graduate of Zhejiang University's electrical engineering school; B-Soft was built around hospital information systems.
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder of B-Soft Co., Ltd. (创业慧康, SZ:300451), Hangzhou; previously chairman
research_notes: Facts from search-result summaries of B-Soft exchange filings (pdf.dfcfw.com) and Crunchbase snippet; Baidu Baike blocked. MarketScreener links a 'Hang Ge' to First-Trust Fund Management, which may be a different person; not used. Best route: B-Soft board secretary / IR via company filings.

name: Ji Chunlin
profile: Ji Chunlin (季春霖) is one of five PhD graduates of Duke and Oxford who founded Kuang-Chi in Shenzhen in 2010, a metamaterials and advanced-technology group led by Liu Ruopeng. He is listed as a vice chairman co-leading Kuang-Chi's state-level metamaterial electromagnetic modulation laboratory.
interesting_fact: Kuang-Chi was founded by five PhD students fresh from Duke and Oxford (Liu Ruopeng, Lin Luan, Ji Chunlin, Zhang Yangyang, Zhao Zhiya), and the founders remained its senior executives; it hosts China's first state key laboratory for metamaterial technology.
current_role: Co-founder and vice chairman, Kuang-Chi (光启) group (title per Wikipedia; current title not re-verified)
research_notes: Limited individual coverage found; best route is via Kuang-Chi corporate channels. Kuang-Chi Group was added to the US Entity List in Dec 2020 (context for a podcast host).

name: Luan Lin
profile: Duke-trained (PhD 2010) metamaterials scientist and one of the five Duke/Oxford PhDs who returned with Liu Ruopeng in 2010 to found the Kuang-Chi Institute of Advanced Technology in Shenzhen, forerunner of listed Kuang-Chi Technologies. He has been vice president of the institute since 2010, previously led KuangChi Science, and now runs Kuang-Chi Technologies as GM.
interesting_fact: He was part of the Duke student circle around Liu Ruopeng, whose team published the first broadband metamaterial 'invisibility cloak' paper in Science before returning to China to found Kuang-Chi.
deep_cut_fact: He served as a non-executive director of Martin Aircraft Company, the New Zealand jetpack maker backed by Kuang-Chi, and sits on the board of Kuang-Chi Martin Jetpack; his degrees are from Shandong University (2001), Peking University (2004) and Duke (2010).
current_role: General Manager & Director, Kuang-Chi Technologies Co., Ltd. (光启技术), since Dec 2022
research_notes: Low personal profile; route via Kuang-Chi Technologies (Shenzhen, A-share listed). Career dates from MarketScreener/Zonebourse insider profile, which has some inconsistencies.

name: Chen Yangnan
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2018-2021 with wealth from 'Huayu' (real estate). Searches did not find a source linking Chen Yangnan (陈阳南) to a specific Huayu company; several unrelated firms use the name, e.g. Chongqing developer Huayu.
research_notes: Identity not confirmed. Need the full Huayu company name or city to research further.

name: Zhao Zhiya
profile: Dr. Zhao Zhiya is one of five founders of Shenzhen-based Kuang-Chi, a metamaterials company whose founding team came out of a Duke University research lab before 2010. He served as president/general manager and director of the listed Kuang-Chi Technologies until November 2022, when he resigned to lead fundamental, frontier research at the controlling-shareholder group.
interesting_fact: In 2020 he said Kuang-Chi aimed to be 'the Qian Xuesen of the new era', projecting about RMB 1bn of metamaterial orders that year and capacity of 48 tons by year-end, insisting the company was 'not drawing pie in the sky'.
deep_cut_fact: Per the company's Nov 2022 SZSE filing, he stepped down as director and GM of Kuang-Chi Technologies not to leave but to take on 'foundational, pioneering research' at the controlling-shareholder group level.
current_role: Co-founder of Kuang-Chi (光启); since Nov 2022 responsible for fundamental/frontier research at the controlling-shareholder group level (left listed Kuang-Chi Technologies' board and GM post)
research_notes: Low public profile since 2022; no personal channels found. Route would be via Kuang-Chi (光启) corporate/IR channels (not verified in this pass). Founding team linked to Duke University metamaterials lab per The Paper.

name: Guo Yaosheng
profile: Guo Yaosheng — wealth from Yaosheng Group (China) Estimated net worth $470M (Hurun China, 2008).
research_notes: Listed on Hurun China 2008 via Yaosheng Group (tungsten, hotel, tourism). Two web searches (English/Chinese, 郭耀升) returned nothing identifying him or the group; no facts recorded.

name: Pan Xiong
profile: Listed on Hurun China (2007-2008) for Xin Haicheng Group (investments). No source found linking a Pan Xiong / 潘雄 to Xin Haicheng Group.
research_notes: Unidentified; last appeared on rich list in 2008. Search results only returned unrelated academics and directors with the same name.

name: Chen Chun-Lin
profile: Chen Chunlin (陈春麟) earned a pharmacy master's from China Pharmaceutical University (1986) and a PhD in pharmacology/toxicology from Oklahoma State University (1994), worked in US drug metabolism research, then returned to China in early 2004 to found Medicilon, a Shanghai preclinical CRO now listed on the STAR Market.
interesting_fact: Medicilon says it has served 2,000+ biotech/pharma clients and helped about 580 innovative-drug INDs get cleared for clinical trials in China, the US, Australia and the EU.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Medicilon he specialised in pharmacokinetics and metabolism for cardiovascular, anti-HIV and anticancer drugs; he also chairs the biomedicine branch of the Western Returned Scholars Association in Shanghai and won a Shanghai Zhangjiang 'most passionate Pharma Valley person' award (2013).
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Shanghai Medicilon Inc. (688202.SS)
public_contact: ir_email: IR@medicilon.com.cn | press_email: marketing@medicilon.com | official_website: https://www.medicilon.com
research_notes: marketing@ address is the business-inquiry mailbox, not a dedicated press desk; IR mailbox is best for a formal approach. A 2008 PharmAsia News interview with him exists (scrip.citeline.com SC066729).

name: Dai Yunjie
profile: Dai Yunjie (Kros Dai) co-founded P2P sharing site VeryCD with Huang Yimeng (Dash Huang) in 2003, then pivoted with him in 2010-11 into games, founding XD (Xindong). XD publishes and develops games and runs the TapTap game platform; Dai oversees daily operations, overseas business and product development.
interesting_fact: VeryCD, which Dai co-founded in 2003 and where he ran tech R&D and operations, ranked among the world's top 100 websites by traffic at its peak before pivoting in 2010 to found XD.
deep_cut_fact: At TapTap's TDW 2024 developer conference he said TapTap keeps ads to about 20% of homepage game exposure and that ~70% of the Android homepage is driven by user preferences; TapTap charges zero commission on mini-games.
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Director/President of XD Inc. (心动, HKEX: 2400); described as CEO of TapTap at TDW 2024
research_notes: English name Kros Dai. Contact is company investor-relations site only; no published personal/press email found.

name: Guo Yanhong
profile: Guo Yanhong — wealth from Puyang Iron and steel (China) Estimated net worth $470M (Hurun China, 2021).
research_notes: Searches (EN/CN, incl. 普阳钢铁 + 郭艳红) found no source linking a Guo Yanhong to Hebei Puyang Iron & Steel (Handan/Wu'an, Hebei); only an unrelated Dalian Univ. of Technology professor of the same name. Very low public profile; check corporate registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) before outreach.

name: Hua Guichao
profile: Hua Guichao (Dr. Gary Hua) is a power-electronics engineer (Zhejiang University BS/MS; Virginia Tech CPES PhD 1994) who founded Inventronics in 2007, now one of the largest makers of high-efficiency LED drivers; the company entered EV chargers in 2015. He also founded 4D Bios Corp.
interesting_fact: Before Inventronics he co-founded VPT Inc. (military/aerospace power) as VP of Engineering, and founded e-Power Co., later a wholly-owned affiliate of NASDAQ-listed Bel Fuse.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his PhD at Virginia Tech's Center for Power Electronics Systems (CPES) in 1994 and has published 60+ papers and received 80+ patents worldwide.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Inventronics (Hangzhou), Inc. (SZSE: 300582)
research_notes: Goes by 'Gary Hua' in English. Strong fit for energy/EV-charging angle. ISA profile notes a CCTV 2010 Economic Person of the Year nomination (https://isa-world.org/Index/show/catid/14/id/121.html). 2026 reports of share-sale plans unverified.

name: Li Jianbo
profile: Founder (1998) and chairman of Luoyang Jalon Micro-Nano New Materials, formerly Luoyang Jianlong Chemical, a maker of molecular-sieve adsorbents and catalysts for industrial gas separation, medical oxygen, energy/petrochemicals and environmental uses. He and Li Xiaohong are the company's actual controllers; in July 2026 he proposed a share buyback for employee incentives.
interesting_fact: Jalon makes molecular-sieve powders, molded and special sieves and activated alumina used in industrial gas separation, medical oxygen, energy/petrochemicals and renewable energy.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Jalon he spent over a decade (Nov 1987 to Jun 1998) as sales section chief at the Yanshi Donggu water-glass (sodium silicate) factory in Henan.
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller, Luoyang Jalon Micro-Nano New Materials Co. (SSE STAR: 688357)
research_notes: Company also romanized as Jianlong/Jianlon. For IR contact, consult the company's SSE annual report (board secretary). Molecular sieves for oxygen/gas separation could be an energy-adjacent angle. Company profile lists Li Yicheng as vice chairman/president.

name: Li Qian
profile: Li Qian (利虔) is chairman and largest shareholder (~38%) of Beijing Sun-Novo Pharmaceutical Research, a CRO providing preclinical and clinical drug R&D services, which he has chaired since 2009. He also chairs Beijing Baiao Pharmaceuticals and is founder/executive director of Jiangsu Langyan Life Technology. Sun-Novo reported 2025 revenue of about RMB 1.22bn.
interesting_fact: Sun-Novo describes itself as moving from a pure CRO 'service provider' toward an innovation-driven 'partner' with its own self-developed drugs; 2025 revenue rose 12.9% to RMB 1.218bn and net profit 10.5% to RMB 196m.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Sun-Novo, he founded Jiangsu Langyan Life Technology Holdings (exec director since Jan 2016) and has been a non-executive director of Eastenova (Chengdu) Biotechnology since 2025; he studied at Peking University Health Science Center.
current_role: Chairman, Beijing Sun-Novo Pharmaceutical Research Co., Ltd. (STAR Market: 688621)
research_notes: Personally hosts investor meetings (e.g. March 2026) alongside IR director Guo Xinchi (郭心驰) and board secretary Wei Liping (魏丽萍); IR route is via SSE E-Interaction / company IR hotline. Company site sun-novo.com was unreachable during research.

name: Liao Ronghua
profile: Born January 1976, he holds an engineering master's degree. He worked at ZTE, SIM Technology and SIMCom from 2001 to 2009, then founded Queclink in Shanghai in June 2009. The company makes wireless IoT terminals for vehicle, asset and personal tracking, sells largely overseas, and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2017. He held about 29% of the shares as of May 2026.
interesting_fact: Queclink sells its trackers to North and South America, Europe, Africa and elsewhere through a global network that includes foreign sales staff stationed abroad, which makes it unusually export-oriented for a Chinese IoT hardware maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Queclink he spent 2001-2009 at ZTE, SIM Technology (Shanghai) and SIMCom Wireless (Shanghai). His co-founder and vice GM, Peng Wei, followed the same SIM Technology/SIMCom path and joined Queclink at its founding in June 2009.
current_role: Chairman (and general manager per 2022 annual report), Shanghai Queclink Wireless Solutions Co., Ltd. (300590.SZ); controlling shareholder
research_notes: Also listed in English as Adam Liao or Rong Hua Liao. He chaired the April 2025 board meeting. IoT and telematics hardware angle. Low media profile, so the best route is the board secretary's office (stock@queclink.com).

name: Lin Changqing
profile: Lin Changqing (林长青) appears on the 2021 Hurun China list via Medicilon, a Shanghai preclinical CRO. Shareholder disclosures describe him as a relative by marriage of Medicilon co-controller Chen Jinzhang (nephew-in-law) and of shareholder Chen Guoxing (brother-in-law). No further public profile found.
interesting_fact: Medicilon's actual controllers are founder Chun-Lin Chen and Chen Jinzhang (acting-in-concert agreement); several other shareholders, including Lin, are their relatives but not acting-in-concert parties.
current_role: Shareholder (family-related) of Shanghai Medicilon Inc. (688202.SH)
research_notes: Very low public profile; relationship info from a search-result summary of Sohu shareholder disclosure (page could not be loaded directly). Contact is Medicilon's company marketing email, not personal.

name: Lin Zhibin
profile: Lin Zhibin is chairman of Xiamen-based Ruida Futures, a futures brokerage incorporated in 1993 and the first futures company listed on the Shenzhen market. Together with Lin Hongbin and Lin Lifang he controls the company as an acting-in-concert party through Ruida Holdings, per the 2024 annual report.
interesting_fact: Ruida Futures was the first listed futures brokerage on the Shenzhen market and the first Fujian futures firm to win a financial-futures brokerage licence.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 he was named 'Best Helmsman of a Chinese Futures Company' (中国期货公司最佳掌舵人) at the 10th China Best Futures Operating Institutions awards.
current_role: Chairman, Ruida Futures Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002961)
research_notes: No personal channels found; reach via company IR (SZSE 002961) website. Personal biography (age, education) not found in accessible sources.

name: Lu Hongping
profile: Lu Hongping (卢红萍, b. 1969) is a passive top-10 shareholder of GoodWe, the Suzhou maker of solar inverters and energy-storage systems founded in 2010. Her stake came largely from husband Tu Haiwen, one of GoodWe's five founding shareholders, who transferred his 8.76m shares to her in 2018. She also controls precision-electronics and investment firms in Kunshan and Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: GoodWe was set up in November 2010 by five individuals including chairman Huang Min and Tu Haiwen (who put in 4m yuan for 20%), and grew into one of China's leading PV inverter and home energy-storage brands, listing on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond GoodWe, GoodWe's IPO prospectus lists her as actual controller of Kunshan Tianyaze Precision Electronics, Shenzhen Tianyaze Precision Electronics and Anhui Deying Electrical Technology, plus investment vehicles Kunshan Hanzetai and Kunshan Handing.
current_role: Major individual shareholder (~2.35% at end-2025) of GoodWe Technologies (688390.SH); controller of Kunshan-based precision-electronics firms
research_notes: Not an executive or director of GoodWe; a passive investor with no public profile. GoodWe chairman/CEO Huang Min is the more relevant guest for an energy podcast. She has been reducing her GoodWe stake (sold ~3.6m shares in 2025). Only route found is GoodWe IR.

name: Lu Xiaojian
profile: Lu Xiaojian (b. 1970) is a co-founder of Jiecang Linear Motion, a Zhejiang maker of linear actuators for height-adjustable desks, medical beds and smart furniture listed in Shanghai in 2018. He has run the company as general manager since 2010 and holds about 66 million shares.
interesting_fact: He is one of the principal drafters of China's light-industry standard QB/T4288-2012.
deep_cut_fact: He studied applied mathematics at Nanjing University of Science and Technology and spent a decade (1990-2000) as R&D manager at Nanjing Sikai Electronics before joining Jiecang's predecessor, Xinchang Jiecang Medical Equipment, in 2000.
current_role: Director and General Manager (CEO), Zhejiang Jiecang Linear Motion Technology (603583.SH)
research_notes: A 2026 Jiecang robotics-actuator brochure lists him as 'Lu Xiaojian (Su Jie), President & CEO, co-founder'. Company is also moving into robot actuators.

name: Luo Aiping
profile: Luo Aiping (罗爱平) founded Fangyuan in Jiangmen, Guangdong in 2002. The company makes lithium-battery cathode precursors (NCA/NCM) plus nickel-battery materials and lithium salts, and was a major NCA precursor supplier to Panasonic. He holds roughly 19.8% of the listed company. He studied at Central South University.
interesting_fact: Fangyuan began bulk-supplying high-nickel NCA precursors to Panasonic in late 2017. In 2021, NCA precursors brought in 1.326bn yuan, about 64% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He completed his undergraduate (1987), master's (1989) and doctoral (1998) degrees at Central South University. Fangyuan later commercialised a lithium-extraction process it co-developed with that university.
current_role: Chairman and President, Guangdong Fangyuan New Materials Group (formerly Guangdong Fangyuan Environment; SSE STAR: 688148)
public_contact: official_website: https://www.fangyuan-group.com | office_email: fyhb@fangyuan-group.com (company general contact)
research_notes: Energy-relevant: battery materials. In Feb 2025 the company set up Guangdong Fangyuan Xincai to make high-purity electronic chemicals for chipmaking. The lithium-process detail is from the company homepage. Co-listed Wu Fang is a director and VP of the company.

name: Wu Fang
profile: Wu Fang (吴芳) is a director and major shareholder of Guangdong Fangyuan (688148), a Jiangmen-based battery-materials maker, and a concerted-action party of controlling shareholder and chairman Luo Aiping. Per the Q1 2026 report she held ~17.3m shares (3.40%).
interesting_fact: Company filings list Wu Fang as an acting-in-concert party with founder Luo Aiping, who was re-elected chairman of the 4th board in July 2025 while Wu Fang joined that board.
current_role: Director, Guangdong Fangyuan New Materials (芳源股份, formerly Fangyuan Environment; SSE STAR 688148)
research_notes: Low public profile; facts from search-result summaries of company filings. Route via company board office / IR (Fangyuan, 688148). Hurun list shares wealth with Luo Aiping.

name: Ma Yongtao
profile: Ma Yongtao (马永涛) is the controlling shareholder of Dongjian Technology, a Guangdong maker of automotive exterior parts, roof racks and vehicle protection systems that has expanded into outdoor gear and full-vehicle customization. 2023 filings show him holding ~25.3% directly plus stakes via Dongjian Huiying Investment.
interesting_fact: The company says its founder entered the car-modification industry in 1994, and in 2023 Ma bought more shares on market (823,500 shares).
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller of Guangdong Dongjian Technology (东箭科技, 300978.SZ); listed as chairman in 2023 filings
research_notes: Hurun lists wealth shared with Liu Shaorong. A July 2026 report names Luo Jun as Dongjian chairman (and racing driver), so Ma may no longer be chairman; verify. Facts on holdings from 2023 company announcements (dongjian.cc PDFs) via search snippets.

name: Liu Shaorong
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2021) with Ma Yongtao for WINBO-Dongjian (Guangdong Dongjian / 东箭科技, auto components, SZ:300978). Searches confirmed Ma Yongtao as Dongjian's chairman and controlling shareholder, but found no source naming Liu Shaorong (刘少容) or her role.
research_notes: Could not verify identity; company site dongjian.cc PDFs blocked by WAF. Ma Yongtao is chairman/actual controller of Dongjian per a 2023 company announcement (per search summary). Likely a family co-holder; route via company IR.

Nata has no controlling shareholder. She appears to be a passive investor rather than an executive.
interesting_fact: Nata, where she is the top shareholder, said its ArF photoresist was the first domestically made one to pass customer certification (tested on 50nm flash memory, 2020), challenging an import-dominated market.
current_role: Largest shareholder (about 8.75%, about 10.7% with concert party Beijing Hongyu Rongji VC) of Jiangsu Nata Opto-electronic Material Co. (南大光电, SZSE: 300346)
research_notes: Very private; no interviews or bio found. Exchange filings (June 2026, https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202606291826547570_1.pdf) confirm her as Nata's largest 5%+ shareholder. Common name, so be careful with other 'Shen Jie's. The company website lists a general inbox, natainfo@natachem.com, which is a company contact, not hers.

interesting_fact: He was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia list in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He serves as a deputy to the 8th and 9th Baoshan District People's Congress in Shanghai.
current_role: Founder, Chairman, Executive Director and CEO, Weimob Inc. (HKEX: 2013)
research_notes: Best route is Weimob investor relations (IR page lists the address for investors, analysts and media).

name: Zhu Guangping
profile: Zhu Guangping (朱广平) is a Shenzhen businessman-investor. Trina Solar's 2021 bond prospectus names him as actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, which held about 4.25% of Trina after its 2020 STAR listing. That stake explains his single 2021 Hurun listing. Filings also link him to duty-free retail, Guowei Electronics, microfinance and food-import firms.
interesting_fact: His Trina stake came through a private fund, not a solar company. Trina's prospectus lists more than 20 firms he controlled or helped run, from China Duty Free joint ventures in Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Urumqi to Comvita Food (China), the mainland arm of the New Zealand manuka-honey brand.
deep_cut_fact: For years he was listed as the legal representative of Shenzhen China Duty Free Merchandise Co. and Zhuhai China Duty Free Merchandise Co., joint ventures in which state-owned China International Travel Service (now China Tourism Group Duty Free) held 30-50%.
current_role: Private investor based in Shenzhen; actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, an early ~4.25% shareholder of Trina Solar (688599.SH)
research_notes: Resolved via cninfo filings. Not a Trina executive; a financial investor whose fund had held over 5% within the year before the 2021 prospectus. Focus Media 2025-26 deal documents show him as an indirect LP via Shenzhen Guangliwei Investment. Hurun 2021: 朱广平 | 天合光能 | RMB 3.0bn (residence given as Changzhou). Private; no contact published.

name: Luo Jianqiang
profile: Luo Jianqiang (骆建强, b. 1965) is a Hangzhou chemicals entrepreneur and investor. He held 61.3% of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (上海辰祥投资中心), which took 300 million shares (11.89%) in the 2014 court-led rescue of bankrupt Shanghai Chaori Solar. Chaori was relaunched under GCL as GCL System Integration (002506.SZ), which explains Hurun's 2015 solar listing.
interesting_fact: His vehicle was the second-biggest investor, after GCL, in the nine-member consortium that rescued Shanghai Chaori Solar. Chaori's March 2014 missed coupon was China's first onshore corporate bond default.
deep_cut_fact: His day job is chemicals, not solar: GCL System's 2015 filing lists him since 2012 as chairman and general manager of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical Co. and chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical Co. in Shandong.
current_role: Chairman & GM of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical; chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical; majority LP of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (per 2015 filing)
research_notes: Resolved via cninfo: Hurun's 'Chenxiang' is 上海辰祥投资中心 (not 晨祥). Chaori default background: https://thediplomat.com/2014/03/its-official-chinas-chaori-defaulted. Other filings show a 骆建强 as a 2011 Joyson Electronics (600699) asset vendor and a shareholder of Haixing (603115); not confirmed as the same man. Private; no published contact.
