name: Wen Kaifu
profile: Wen Kaifu built Holitech, a Shandong-based maker of touch screens, LCD modules and other display components for smartphones. In 2018 he handed control (via a voting-rights proxy and share transfers) to the state-owned Fujian Electronics & Information Group, which now controls the company.
interesting_fact: Holitech grew into one of China's larger suppliers of touch-display modules for smartphone brands before Fujian Electronics & Information Group took control around 2018.
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Holitech Technology (合力泰, SZSE: 002217); no current executive role found
research_notes: Not a good outreach target: in June 2026 Holitech disclosed a regulator's preliminary penalty notice naming the company and Wen Kaifu over 2017-2021 financial misreporting, and reports say he faces a lifetime securities-market ban and his shares are judicially frozen (news.10jqka.com.cn/20260901/c679501996.shtml). No personal public channels found.

name: Chai Huijing
profile: Chai Huijing (柴慧京) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2008 to 2018 with real-estate wealth tied to a company listed as 'Guodu' (国都). I could not find any public profile, company page or press coverage to confirm her role or what she is doing now.
research_notes: Very low public footprint; searches for the exact Chinese name returned nothing relevant. Not the Taiwanese general Chai Hui-chen (柴惠珍). Verify via Chinese corporate registries (Qichacha/Tianyancha) before outreach.

name: Zhang Xinming
profile: Zhang Xinming was chairman of Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group and was described as Shanxi's richest energy tycoon, appearing on Hurun China from 2005 to 2010. Reports since 2010 concern legal matters rather than business activity.
current_role: Formerly chairman, Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group (山西金业煤焦化集团); no verified current role
research_notes: Do not approach. Chinese media reported in Oct 2010 that he fled and was wanted by police (https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2010-10-26/400513.html); later reports cite organised-crime allegations. Off rich lists since 2010; current status unverified.

name: Zhang Tongsheng
profile: Wenzhou entrepreneur who co-founded the Wenzhou Bearing Factory in 1991 with three partners; it became C&U Group, China's largest bearing maker, plus the Renben (人本) supermarket and Shizu retail chains. He controls ~60.8% of the votes of C&U Co., which re-filed for a Shanghai main-board IPO in late 2025.
interesting_fact: C&U has ranked No.1 in China by bearing output and sales every year since 2013 and is described as the only Chinese company in the global top 10 bearing makers; it employs ~19,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: He started the bearing business at age 24 with a junior-middle-school education; the Wenzhou Bearing Factory was registered in July 1991 with RMB 4 million of capital, and he has led it as chairman ever since.
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, C&U Co., Ltd. (人本股份) and controlling shareholder of C&U Group (人本集团), Wenzhou
public_contact: office_email: cuchina@cugroup.com (C&U corporate general contact) | official_website: https://www.cugroup.com/ | contact_form: https://www.cubearing.com/contact/ (C&U Americas subsidiary)
research_notes: Low public profile; little personal press. Route via C&U corporate office or the IPO sponsor/IR once listed. Bearings for wind turbines/EVs could be an energy angle.

name: Sun Guomin
profile: Listed by Hurun alongside Sun Deliang, founder and chairman of Hangzhou-based Netsun (China Chemical Network / 生意宝), a B2B e-commerce pioneer listed in Shenzhen in 2006. Exchange filings show a pre-IPO 5%+ holder named 孙国明 (Sun Guoming), possibly the same person as Hurun's 孙国民, who held 9.25% and sold down to 4.83% by 2014.
interesting_fact: Netsun says it was the first Chinese company to build and run an industry-specific B2B website (ChemNet / China Chemical Network); it listed in Shenzhen in late 2006.
current_role: Early shareholder of Zhejiang Netsun Co. (生意宝, 002095.SZ); no executive role found
research_notes: Identity unclear: Hurun's 孙国民 may be a rendering of filings' 孙国明, a passive pre-IPO holder (9.25%, cut to 4.83% by 2014). Their link to Sun Deliang is unconfirmed. The public face of the business is founder-chairman Sun Deliang. Not a good outreach target.

name: Zhou Jianhe
profile: Hong Kong-based businessman (also styled Zhou Chu Jian He) behind Junefield Group, whose interests span Beijing property, hospitality and trade. Was chairman of HKEX-listed Junefield Department Store Group (stock 758), based at Beijing Junefield Plaza on Xuanwumen Wai Street. Appeared on Hurun China lists 2003-2005.
interesting_fact: His group developed Beijing Junefield Plaza on Xuanwumen Wai Street, the PRC base of his HK-listed department-store company in the mid-2000s.
current_role: President, Junefield (Holdings) Ltd (Hong Kong); chairman, Prime Century Investments Ltd (per MarketScreener, undated)
research_notes: Low public profile; most info from 2005 HKEX filings and aggregator data. No official Junefield website or contacts found. Verify current role via HK Companies Registry.

name: Hong Jiangyou
profile: Born 1964 in Puning, Guangdong; pharmacy graduate (Guangdong College of Pharmacy, 1988) who left a state pharmacist job in Shenzhen to found Hainan-based Honz Pharmaceutical, a children's-medicine maker listed on ChiNext. He controls ~20% of the company and was re-elected chairman for a three-year term in December 2025.
interesting_fact: He has pitched Honz around a single mission, 'children's great health' (儿童大健康), and has said he won't retire until it is complete; the firm specialises in paediatric drugs.
deep_cut_fact: A keen Go player since university, he chairs the Hainan Provincial Go Culture Promotion Association and says Go's opening stage shapes how he makes business decisions; Honz sponsored a children's Go training camp in Guangzhou.
current_role: Chairman and President, Honz Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (康芝药业, SZSE: 300086), re-elected Dec 2025
research_notes: Also chairs the International Teochew (Chaozhou) Business Federation 21st council and the Hainan overseas-Chinese business federation. Company has been loss-making in 2024-25. Best route: the board secretary (Lin Dexin) through the IR email.

name: Li Shiyong
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for wealth from Ensign, a citric-acid and alcohol producer. Shandong Ensign Industry (named Weifang Ensign until 2020) is reported to be the world's largest citric-acid producer, with ~600,000 t/a capacity and an upgrade planned to 700,000 t/a. Recent annual reports list Li Jian as company head; Li Shiyong's current role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Shandong Ensign has been described as the world's largest citric acid producer, planning to lift capacity from 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes a year.
current_role: Associated with Shandong Ensign Industry (formerly Weifang Ensign), Changle, Weifang; current title not confirmed
interesting_fact_source: https://www.cnchemicals.com/Press/91863-Shandong Ensign: Citric acid capacity expansion proposal and refined citric acid project completion.html
research_notes: Very low public profile; no biography found in English or Chinese web search, and Baidu Baike was not accessible. A 'Shiyong Li' appears as an inventor on Weifang Ensign patents (goodip.io). No published contact or company website found.

name: Luo Weidong
sec_insider_companies: Aurora Mobile Ltd (JG) - Chief Executive Officer
profile: Luo Weidong (Chris Luo) co-founded Shenzhen-based Aurora Mobile (JPush / Jiguang) in 2011 and has been chairman and CEO since May 2012. The mobile developer-services and big-data company, backed by IDG, Fidelity and Goldman Sachs, listed on Nasdaq in 2018; his stake (~30%) is the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: PolyU says Aurora Mobile was the first company of its kind to list on Nasdaq (2018); Luo holds an MPhil in computing from PolyU and won its Outstanding Alumni Award for entrepreneurial achievement in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: During COVID-19, Luo led a research team behind a data platform that PolyU credits with supporting epidemic-containment work in 334 Chinese cities. Before Aurora he was GM of Shenzhen Zhiwo Information Technology (2007-2010).
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Aurora Mobile Ltd (Nasdaq: JG), Shenzhen
public_contact: ir_email: ir@jiguang.cn | pr_agency: Christensen Advisory - Xiaoyan Su, Xiaoyan.Su@christensencomms.com (IR agency named in Aurora Mobile press releases) | official_website: https://ir.aurora-mobile.com
research_notes: Goes by Chris Luo. Some IR pages list ir@aurora-mobile.com instead of ir@jiguang.cn (company rebranding of IR domain). Named 2025 Greater Bay Area Strategic Emerging Industry Youth Leader (Feb 2026 release).

name: Yang Zhen
profile: Yang Zhen (杨振, b. 1962, Ningxiang, Hunan) founded Jiajia soy sauce in 1996 and took it public in 2012 as China's first listed soy-sauce maker, earning the nickname 'soy sauce king'. He later stepped back from management to focus on outside investments; a cousin, Yang Xudong, now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: In 2003 he spent RMB 48m, nearly all of Jiajia's profits from its first seven years, to win CCTV's prime-time 'ad king' slot for two months; revenue hit a record RMB 500m in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he trained at Yiyang Normal College and worked as a Chinese-language teacher. He is credited with inventing the built-in pull-ring soy-sauce bottle cap, and he founded Jiajia in 1996 after Hunan factories turned down his offer to sell the patent for RMB 500k.
current_role: Founder and (per 2024 reports) actual controller of Jiajia Food Group (加加食品, SZSE: 002650); no longer chairman
research_notes: Sensitive. Since 2022, Yang and his holding company have repeatedly been listed as debt defaulters, and Jiajia has been ST-flagged over guarantees he arranged. Approach with care, if at all. No personal or office contact published. Go through the Jiajia Food board secretary listed in SZSE filings.

name: Chen Wenli
profile: Chen Wenli was one of the founders of Hainan-based HNA Group in 1993, alongside Chen Feng, Wang Jian and Adam Tan. He held an individual HNA stake (Hurun rich list 2017-2019) and sat on the board. He left the board in March 2020 when a Hainan government working group took control. HNA later went through court-led restructuring in 2021, which wiped out the founders' equity.
interesting_fact: He co-founded HNA, which grew from a provincial airline into a global conglomerate that held stakes in Hilton, Deutsche Bank and Swissport during a record overseas buying spree that ended in 2017.
current_role: Former director and co-founder of HNA Group (left the board in March 2020); no current public role found
research_notes: Very low profile and likely not a viable guest. His wealth was tied to HNA equity that was largely erased in the 2021 bankruptcy restructuring, and other HNA founders were detained in 2021. Source for his 2020 board exit: https://www.mingtiandi.com/?p=43164. No personal channels found.

name: Ye Jiahao
profile: Ye Jiahao (叶家豪) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2016-2020 with wealth attributed to 'Qixin Construction' (construction sector). Web searches in Chinese and English found no public coverage linking him to a specific company, so identity and current role could not be confirmed.
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2016-2020) as founder/owner of Qixin Construction; current role not verified
research_notes: Very low public profile; company name 'Qixin' may be a romanisation of 祺鑫/启鑫/奇信 etc. Verify via Chinese business registry (e.g. Qichacha) before outreach.

name: Chen Qiming
profile: Chen Qiming is one of nine SF Express-linked individuals on the 2020 Hurun Global/China Rich List, with an estimated RMB 3.1bn (rank 1,705). The listing implies an early or indirect stake in SF Holding, the delivery giant founded by Wang Wei. I found no published biography or SF board or management role.
interesting_fact: He was one of nine SF-linked people on the 2020 Hurun list, a year in which SF's rising share price added five new SF billionaires-by-yuan.
current_role: Shareholder associated with SF Express / SF Holding (002352.SZ); no executive title found
research_notes: He is not among SF Holding's directors, supervisors or senior management in the filings I checked. He is probably an early partner or indirect shareholder. Identity details are thin. The only route is via SF Holding IR, which may not forward.

profile: Listed on the 2008 Hurun China Rich List with Jinsheng Group (copper). No reliable online source found linking the name 王景连 to a specific Jinsheng group or role, so identity could not be confirmed.
research_notes: Could not verify. A copper business called Shandong Jinsheng Nonferrous Group (Linyi) went through a court-supervised restructuring/settlement in 2022-23 (https://www.zhonglun.com/news/trade/15361.html), but no source names Wang Jinglian in connection with it. Treat as unverified; low priority.

name: He Qiqiang
profile: Co-founded Chant Group (长青集团) in Zhongshan in 1985 as a gas and heating appliance maker, listed it in Shenzhen in 2011, and from 2004 steered it into biomass combined heat-and-power and industrial-park district heating, where it ranks among China's largest operators. Still chairman; fortune shared with wife Guo Miaobo.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from gas stoves and heaters to burning crop and forestry residues instead of coal, and its installed biomass CHP capacity ranks among the largest of China's peers.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting his business in 1985 he was a factory workshop director earning about 100 yuan a month, and his early goal was simply to save 1 million yuan, since its ~5% interest would yield 4,000+ yuan a month (told at a 2023 Yabuli entrepreneurs' forum).
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Chant Group (Changqing Group, 002616.SZ), Zhongshan
research_notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (biomass CHP). Active in the Yabuli China Entrepreneurs Forum, which may be a warm route. IR email is the board secretary's office.

name: Guo Miaobo
profile: Guo Miaobo (郭妙波) is the spouse of Chant Group chairman He Qiqiang and one of the parties acting in concert with the company's actual controllers (He Qiqiang and Mai Zhenghui), per the 2025 annual report. Chant, based in Zhongshan, Guangdong, started in gas appliances and has expanded into biomass and waste-to-energy power generation and industrial-park heat supply.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from making gas stoves and water heaters into environmental energy, operating agricultural-biomass power plants and waste-to-energy and heat-supply projects in China, a possible angle for an energy podcast.
current_role: Shareholder and acting-in-concert party of the controlling group of Guangdong Chant Group (SZSE: 002616); holds no position at the company
research_notes: Private, non-executive; the 2025 annual report states she holds no post at Chant. Better interview target would be chairman He Qiqiang; route via the board secretary office (dmof@chantgroup.cn).

name: Xu Xizhong
profile: Xu Xizhong (许锡忠) controlled Shanghai-listed float-glass maker Sanxia New Materials (三峡新材), together with his vehicle Hainan Zong Xuan Da Industrial Investment (海南宗宣达实业), and chaired its board; the company also owned mobile-phone distributor Shenzhen Hengbo. By 2025 the company was controlled by Dangyang City Investment and chaired by Xie Pule.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he chaired Sanxia New Materials while also chairing Shenzhen Weikangde Investment Group, Jiangxi Chaosheng Mining and Hainan Zong Xuan Da Industrial Investment, per the company's 2019 annual report.
deep_cut_fact: His career began as a department manager at a garment factory in Laowu township, Chaoyang county, Guangdong; he later ran a restaurant (Haomen Yeda Jiulou) in Puning as general manager before becoming chairman of Shenzhen Xinzhen Co.
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Hubei Sanxia New Building Materials (600293.SH); current post unknown
research_notes: Hurun listing only 2017. He has since lost control of Sanxia New Materials (now state-controlled) and his shares were frozen in 2019 litigation; a Dec 2025 SSE regulatory warning named him as former chairman. Likely no longer UHNW and not a good outreach target; no published contact found.

name: Zhang Chunhua
profile: Hurun China (2016-17) lists 张春华 of 'Brilliant' in logistics. profile: Xu Mingbo (徐明波, b. 1964) is a genetic-engineering scientist who co-founded Beijing SL Pharmaceutical, has run it as general manager since December 1994 and later became chairman. The Shenzhen-listed company makes biotech and chemical drugs (recombinant proteins, peptides, generics); his wealth comes from his controlling stake. He still chaired the board through 2025-26.
interesting_fact: Before going into business he was a research group leader at the Academy of Military Medical Sciences, led four national high-tech research projects, published 40+ papers and won a National Science and Technology Progress Award (2nd class).
deep_cut_fact: He earned his PhD at China's Academy of Military Medical Sciences and was described as one of the first young experts in 'mid- and downstream' genetic-engineering process technology trained entirely in China; he also serves on the council of the Chinese Society of Biotechnology.
current_role: Chairman & general manager, Beijing SL Pharmaceutical Co. (双鹭药业, SZSE: 002038)
public_contact: ir_email: lsj@slpharm.com.cn (board secretary Liang Shujie); securities rep yitingjing@slpharm.com.cn; IR tel +86 10-88627635 | official_website: http://www.slpharm.com/
research_notes: Low public profile, Chinese-language only. In May 2026 the SZSE publicly reprimanded the company and Xu over unrecovered trust investments (company blamed alleged embezzlement by a former finance employee) - context to be aware of, sensitive. Best route: board secretary's office.

name: Xu Zhiming
profile: Xu Zhiming (许智明), born 1964 in Gaozhou, Guangdong, moved to Hong Kong in the late 1980s and built Jiahao Group in property, finance and trade, then became an oil tycoon via Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical ('Sunpec'), which bought overseas oilfields. In 2009 he bought five coal mines for HK$3.66B, steering it toward coal and chemicals.
interesting_fact: A major poverty-relief donor (over HK$300M per his profile), he was honoured by China Post with a 7-envelope commemorative cover set, 'Xu Zhiming and China's Guangcai poverty relief', and received Hong Kong's Gold Bauhinia Star.
deep_cut_fact: He single-handedly financed the development of Fangji Island (放鸡岛), dubbed the 'Pearl of the South China Sea' off Guangdong, and was awarded an honorary doctorate and the Lomonosov Medal by the Russian Academy of Sciences.
current_role: Chairman, Hong Kong Jiahao (Ka Ho) Group; former chairman and controlling shareholder of Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical (HKEX 346, later Sino Union Energy Investment) (last reported)
research_notes: 'Sunpec' appears to be the abbreviation of Sino Union Petroleum & Chemical (中联石化). Little news after ~2010; last on Hurun list 2021. No published contacts found. Former CPPCC national committee member and Hong Kong JP.

name: Shao Jianming
profile: Shao Jianming (邵建明) founded Guangzhou's Highsun (海印) group in 1991, growing it from a leasing business into theme malls, wholesale markets, shopping centres and urban complexes, with a later push into finance (payments, a rural-bank stake, Huacheng Bank). He is a co-controller with Shao Jianjia (president) and Shao Jiancong.
interesting_fact: Highsun was one of the few privately controlled commercial-property companies listed in Guangzhou (Shenzhen listing 2008) and pioneered themed specialist malls in the city; it also helped found Huacheng Bank (花城银行).
deep_cut_fact: He served as a non-executive director of Guangzhou Rural Commercial Bank from 2009 to 2019.
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Highsun Group Co., Ltd. (海印股份; reappointed March 2025)
public_contact: ir_email: IR000861@126.com (company investor relations) | official_website: http://www.000861.com
research_notes: Company now trades on the NEEQ delisted-securities board ('海印5') and faces regulatory/financial issues; avoid financial topics. Deep-cut fact comes from an aggregator (MarketScreener), so verify it. Not a natural fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Gao Tianle
profile: Founder-chairman of Tengen (天正电气), founded 1999 in Yueqing, Zhejiang, which makes low-voltage electrical products and industrial control solutions; company listed in Shanghai in 2020.
interesting_fact: Tengen's low-voltage switchgear and power-distribution products sit directly in the power infrastructure chain relevant to energy and data-center build-outs.
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Zhejiang Tengen Electrics Co., Ltd. (SHSE: 605066)
research_notes: Chinese name 高天乐 inferred from romanization. No public personal channels found; route via company IR/board secretary.

name: Li Yuping
profile: Li Yuping — wealth from Nature (China) Estimated net worth $430M (Hurun China, 2017).
research_notes: Hurun China 2009-2017 (real estate, 'Nature'). Could not identify the company or any public record of 厉育平; web-search budget ran out. No facts or contacts recorded.

name: Wang Dafu
profile: Wang Dafu (王大富) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List for over a decade (2009-2021), most recently at about $430M, with wealth attributed to the property group 'Visun'. No accessible English or Chinese source could confirm the company's full name, location or his current role.
current_role: Listed as owner of Visun, a real-estate group, on the Hurun China list (2009-2021). Current role not verified.
research_notes: Unverifiable from this environment (Baidu Baike blocked, no Wikipedia page). Long Hurun tenure suggests an established regional developer, but treat identity as unconfirmed. Real estate is not a strong podcast fit.

name: Lin Kaiwen
profile: Lin Kaiwen (林凯文) founded Shanghai Kaiquan Pump in the mid-1990s; it was registered in July 1996 and is headquartered in Jiading, Shanghai. It grew into one of China's largest private pump groups, designing and making pumps, water-supply equipment and pump control systems. He has been on Hurun's China rich list every year since 2006 and still leads the group.
interesting_fact: Kaiquan sells through its own direct-sales model and has been recognised as a 'National Enterprise Technology Centre', claiming more than 700 technology patents. Large pumps like its products run municipal water, power plants and cooling systems.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (legal representative), Shanghai Kaiquan Pump (Group) Co., Ltd.
research_notes: Very low media profile; I found no interviews. The company site (kaiquan.com.cn) did not load from here. Note that kaiquan.com is a different, unrelated pump company. Pumps for power plants and cooling are a possible energy/data-centre angle. Data aggregators disagree on the founding year (1995 vs 1996).

name: Wang Chunming
profile: Wang Chunming built Chengdu-based Sichuan Guodong Construction Group and was legal representative and chairman of its listed arm, Sichuan Guodong Construction Co., which IPO'd in Shanghai in 2001. In 2016 Guodong Group agreed to sell control (about RMB 2.5bn at RMB 7/share) to Zhengyuan Real Estate (Fu Yanbin). Guodong Group and an affiliate still held ~22.9% in 2023 as second-largest holder.
interesting_fact: Guodong Construction's March 2001 Shanghai IPO sold 70m shares at RMB 12.28 each (about 28x earnings), lifting its share capital from 105.2m to 175.2m shares.
current_role: Founder/controller of Sichuan Guodong Construction Group (Chengdu); former chairman of Guodong Construction (SSE: 600321, now Zhengyuan Co.)
research_notes: Very low public profile and little personal coverage; no published personal or office contact found. Control sale source: https://stock.stockstar.com/SS2016101100001192.shtml; 2023 stake: https://paper.cnstock.com/html/2023-04/10/content_1746133.htm. Not an obvious podcast fit.

name: Dai Wei
education: High School Affiliated to Renmin University of China; Peking University
profile: Peking University graduate who co-founded ofo in 2014 with fellow PKU cycling-club members; it pioneered dockless smartphone bike-sharing, raised money from Didi, Xiaomi, Alibaba and DST and became a $1bn+ unicorn by 2017 before collapsing in 2018-19. He has since split time between China and the US, launching a power-bank rental startup in Seattle and the About Time Coffee chain in New York.
interesting_fact: The name 'ofo' was chosen because the word visually resembles a cyclist riding a bicycle; ofo grew from 2,000 bikes on the PKU campus in 2015 to a global unicorn in under two years.
deep_cut_fact: He spent a year as a volunteer teacher in Qinghai Province during his postgraduate studies; the 'ofo' name was reportedly born on 15 Feb 2014 while he was still teaching there. He met co-founders through a PKU Cycling Association outdoor trip.
current_role: Founder, ofo (defunct Beijing dockless bike-sharing company); since COVID has run small US ventures (Seattle power-bank rental; About Time Coffee, New York)
research_notes: Sensitive history: ofo's collapse left large unrefunded user deposits and he was placed on China's debtor ('laolai') list; avoid in outreach. No published personal contact; US coffee venture largely wound down per 2023 reports. Was a WEF Young Global Leader-type profile; best route likely via mutual tech/VC contacts.

name: Mo Jianrong
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for Boee, i.e. Boee Group (保亿集团), a Hangzhou-based private developer founded on 16 Sept 1991 as Huarong home-appliance trading company in Taizhou that moved into real estate in the late 1990s. The group now spans property development, property management, trading and industrial investment. A third-party profile names a Mo Jianrong as chairman of its property-service arm.
interesting_fact: Boee began in 1991 as Zhejiang Huarong, a home-appliance trading firm, and switched to property; its first project, Boee Mingzhu in Taizhou (2001), made its name. Its property arm sent butlers to train in Europe for a 'platinum butler' service.
current_role: Linked by Hurun to Boee Group (保亿集团), Hangzhou property developer; exact current title not confirmed
research_notes: Chairman's name on Boee's site is shown only as an image; a third-party site (altss.com) names founder Mo Jianhua as group chairman and Mo Jianrong as chairman of Zhejiang Boee Property Service - unverified. Group HQ: Boee Center, Qianjiang Century City, Hangzhou. Very private; Chinese-language media is the likely route.

name: Chen Yunqin
profile: Founder, controlling shareholder and one of the actual controllers of Ningbo David Medical Device (founded 1992). The company announced he died of illness on 20 September 2024, aged 82; he held about 21.12% of the company at the time.
current_role: Deceased (founder of Ningbo David Medical Device Co., SZSE: 300314)
research_notes: Died 20 Sept 2024 per company announcement filed with Shenzhen Stock Exchange: https://disc.static.szse.cn/download/disc/disk03/finalpage/2024-09-23/15a7f1c9-2396-4e01-b537-99518cc845e2.PDF . Company is now led by Chen Zaihong (legal representative/chairman).

name: Liao Dinghai
profile: Liao Dinghai (b. 1963), a naval hydrographic surveyor turned entrepreneur, founded Hi-Target (中海达), a Guangzhou maker of GNSS/BeiDou surveying, mapping and marine-survey equipment that listed on ChiNext in 2011. He has chaired it since 2009 and was re-elected for a three-year term in May 2024; son Liao Wen is a director and VP.
interesting_fact: He graduated from the Dalian Naval Academy's marine surveying department and spent nearly 20 years in the PLA Navy as a unit leader and senior engineer doing marine surveying before running Hi-Target.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2015 he and Hi-Target's executives have funded a RMB10m 'Hi-Target Love Fund' (中海达爱心基金) that supports employees and their families facing serious illness or accidents.
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Guangzhou Hi-Target Navigation Tech Co. (SZSE 300177)
research_notes: Hurun co-listee Liao Wen is his son. Relevant to podcast via BeiDou/GNSS positioning tech. Contact via board secretary office.

name: Liao Wen
profile: Liao Wen appears on the Hurun list jointly with Liao Dinghai, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Guangzhou-based Hi-Target, a maker of high-precision GNSS receivers, CORS stations, total stations, 3D laser scanners and drones. Liao Wen was named as a shareholder in Hi-Target's 2011 IPO lock-up undertakings; the exact relationship to Liao Dinghai is not stated in the filings found.
interesting_fact: Hi-Target, founded in Guangzhou in 1999, is one of China's main makers of BeiDou/GNSS high-precision surveying equipment.
current_role: Pre-IPO shareholder of Hi-Target Navigation Tech (中海达, SZSE: 300177); no executive role found
public_contact: official_website: https://www.hi-target.com.cn/ (company; general sales email sales@hi-target.com.cn)
research_notes: Low public profile; the wealth figure is shared with Liao Dinghai, the public face of the company. Any outreach is better aimed at Liao Dinghai via Hi-Target's board secretary/IR. Relationship between Liao Wen and Liao Dinghai not confirmed.

name: Qian Yunbao
profile: Qian Yunbao (钱云宝) was the controlling shareholder of Hengbao Co. (恒宝股份, SZSE 002104), a smart-card maker in Danyang, Jiangsu, and chairman of Jiangsu Hengshen (carbon fibre). A June 2017 Shenzhen Stock Exchange disclosure records his death on 12 April 2017 and the transfer of his shareholdings by inheritance.
current_role: Deceased (died 12 April 2017)
research_notes: Deceased. Source: Hengbao equity-change report filed with the SZSE, 23 June 2017 (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2017-06-23/2d9ddce9-51ba-4b87-b463-e675958b7fe0.PDF). Not an outreach candidate.

name: Shen Jieyong
profile: Shen Jieyong (沈洁泳) shares the Hurun-listed fortune (2014-2021) with Shen Jinhao, founder of Hangzhou-based CNP / Nanfang Pump, a maker of stainless-steel multistage centrifugal pumps listed in Shenzhen (300145). Control was later sold to state-linked owners; Wuxi Municipal Public Utilities is now controlling shareholder. In 2025 the company dropped the name 中金环境 and returned to 南方泵业.
interesting_fact: The listed company was renamed back from 'Zhongjin Environment' to 'Nanfang Pump' (南方泵业) in 2025, keeping stock code 300145; Shen Jieyong still held about 40.97 million shares (2.13%) as of December 2025.
current_role: Shareholder (~2.1%) of Nanfang Pump / CNP (SZ300145), acting in concert with Shen Jinhao
research_notes: Passive shareholder with no public profile; the active figure is Shen Jinhao (founder). info@cnppump.com is a general/sales inbox, not personal. Very private.

name: Shen Jinhao
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur behind CNP (Nanfang Pump), founded 1991 and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in December 2010; it grew into one of China's leading stainless-steel multistage centrifugal pump makers and was renamed Nanfang Zhongjin Environment in 2016 as it expanded into environmental services. He chaired the listed company until 2019; family member Shen Jieyong shares the Hurun listing.
interesting_fact: CNP was among the first batch of companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext-era growth listings (listed 9 Dec 2010, code 300145) and later bought Texas pump maker Tigerflow Systems (2016).
current_role: Founder and former chairman (2005-2019) of Nanfang Pump / Nanfang Zhongjin Environment (SZSE: 300145); reported as chairman of Hangzhou Nanfang Haoyuan Pump Industry
public_contact: office_email: info@cnppump.com (CNP company general inbox) | official_website: https://www.cnppump.com
research_notes: Very little personal coverage; current role after 2019 control change not confirmed from primary filings. Alive status not confirmed (no reports of death found). CNP is now run by a different CEO (Shen Haijun).

name: Huang Zongmin
profile: Hurun China listed Huang Zongmin (黄宗敏) from 2014 to 2021 with wealth from 'Sanhe', an auto repair and retail business. Searches in English and Chinese found no reliable public profile linking him to a specific Sanhe entity.
current_role: Listed by Hurun as founder/owner of 'Sanhe' (auto repair & retail); could not verify the current role
research_notes: Could not identify which 'Sanhe' (三和) company this is; Baidu Baike was blocked. Needs Chinese company-registry research (e.g. Qichacha) to pin down. No contacts found.

name: Hu Dong
profile: Born 1973; founded Hangzhou-based Ebang, which started out making communications network access equipment and around 2014 pivoted into bitcoin-mining ASIC machines, listing on Nasdaq in 2020. Holds most of the voting power; Ebang has since expanded into crypto exchange, payments and mining businesses.
interesting_fact: Ebang began as a telecom network-equipment maker and only moved into blockchain/bitcoin-mining hardware around 2014, becoming one of China's big three miner makers.
deep_cut_fact: Before and while building Ebang he was a lecturer at Zhejiang University of Technology's College of Computer Science and Technology (where he earned an industrial automation degree in 1998); he also holds a Zhejiang University MBA and Tsinghua EMBA.
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and CFO, Ebang International Holdings (Nasdaq: EBON), Hangzhou
public_contact: ir_email: ir@ebang.com | pr_agency: Ascent Investor Relations (Tina Xiao), tina.xiao@ascent-ir.com | official_website: https://ebanginternational.gcs-web.com (IR site)
research_notes: Strong fit for data-center/energy angle (bitcoin-mining hardware, mining operations). Company was subject of a 2020 Hindenburg short report. IR contacts from 2023 releases; confirm on latest release.

name: Yao Hong
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur (born c.1980) who founded Weidai in 2010, a P2P lender that pivoted to car-collateral loans in 2012 and listed on the NYSE in 2018. The platform exited online lending in 2020 and came under a Hangzhou police illegal-deposit-taking investigation; Weidai reported repaying all outstanding investor principal by mid-2021. No recent public information on him.
interesting_fact: He started his first business in 2001 at 21 with three friends and 5,000 yuan; he says he struggled to borrow 500 yuan for inventory and a classmate lent it on the 20th call. He framed Weidai as a lender for small entrepreneurs like his younger self.
current_role: Founder of Weidai (微贷网), Hangzhou; current role/status unclear since the platform wound down in 2020-21
research_notes: Sensitive: Weidai has been under police investigation since July 2020 (https://m.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_17363197). Status unknown; Hurun listings ended 2019. Not a good outreach target; no public contacts found.

name: Ding Mingshan
profile: Appears on the Hurun China Rich List (2015-2019) with real-estate wealth attributed to a company rendered 'Wallink'. Could not identify the company's Chinese name or confirm his current role from public web sources.
current_role: Unknown (listed by Hurun China 2015-2019 as real-estate entrepreneur, company 'Wallink')
research_notes: Searches in English and Chinese (丁明山) returned no matching biography; Baidu Baike blocked. Identity unconfirmed - needs a Chinese registry check (e.g. 国家企业信用信息公示系统) to locate 'Wallink'.

name: Shen Haiyin
profile: Shen Haiyin (沈海寅) is an internet executive turned EV entrepreneur: a former VP at Kingsoft and Qihoo 360 and angel investor, he founded Zhiche Youxing in Oct 2014 to build smart EVs under the Singulato (奇点) brand, which raised at least seven rounds through 2020 and made him a Hurun unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: He decided to build cars after driving a Tesla in 2014: 'After experiencing a Tesla, I felt the auto industry was bound to change' (体验过特斯拉的车后，我就感觉汽车行业一定会变天).
deep_cut_fact: Not a total auto outsider: his first job after university was at Shanghai Delphi Automotive Air Conditioning, making car A/C components; in 2000 he moved to Japan and founded three companies there before ~15 years in China's internet industry.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zhiche Youxing Technology (智车优行, brand Singulato / 奇点汽车), Shanghai/Beijing; current status unclear
research_notes: Singulato faced funding/wage-arrears problems and was reported heading toward bankruptcy around 2023 - avoid as a hook. No recent (2024-26) public activity found; no published contact.

name: Huang Jinlan
profile: Hurun China (2017-2021) linked Huang Jinlan (黄金兰) to Zuoyou (左右), the Shenzhen sofa and furniture maker. Public sources name Huang Huakun (黄华坤) as Zuoyou's founder and chairman, and no source found describes Huang Jinlan's role.
research_notes: Could not confirm this person's identity or role. The company's public face is founder/chairman Huang Huakun (https://house.huanqiu.com/article/45vap4zG0ww); outreach about Zuoyou should probably go through the company. Checking Chinese business registries for the shareholder list was outside the allowed tools.

name: Huang Tengxin
profile: Hurun China lists Huang Tengxin (黄腾新) as the wealth holder behind Zuoyou, a furniture business. Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture (左右家私) is a sofa maker with about 4,000 staff and parks in Shenzhen, Huizhou, Anhui and Sichuan. Public sources name Huang Huakun (黄华坤) as its founder, who started making sofas in Shenzhen in 1986. No source found that links the name Huang Tengxin to the company.
interesting_fact: Zuoyou registered its brand in 1995 and opened China's first 'scenario-style' living-room furniture stores. In 2005 it signed former China women's volleyball head coach Chen Zhonghe as brand ambassador.
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun against Zuoyou (Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture / 左右沙发)
research_notes: Identity unresolved. Hurun's 'Huang Tengxin' may be a transliteration or listing error, or a relative or partner of founder Huang Huakun. Verify against Hurun's Chinese list before any outreach. Baidu and Sogou blocked automated lookups.

name: Shi Weixue
profile: Shi Weixue (史维学) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2016-2021 with wealth attributed to 'Guowei' in real estate and investments. Chinese and English web searches returned no coverage linking him to an identifiable company, so identity and current role are unconfirmed.
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2016-2021) as owner of 'Guowei' (real estate, investments); current role not verified
research_notes: Very low public profile; Baidu Baike blocked from this environment. Verify company (国伟?) via Chinese business registry before outreach.

name: Li Lei
profile: Li Lei co-founded Qutoutiao, the Shanghai 'pay-to-read' news-aggregator app, with Eric Tan Sixiao. He served as CEO from August 2018, when it listed on Nasdaq, until May 2019, and then as vice chairman. He held about 7.6% of the company (15.6% of the votes) in 2022, before Qutoutiao was delisted in 2023.
interesting_fact: He led Qutoutiao through its September 2018 Nasdaq IPO, which came about two years after launch. The app grew fast by paying users in coins to read and share articles, aimed at lower-tier cities.
deep_cut_fact: He studied while building the business, earning an associate degree in law (2014) and a bachelor's in law (2017) from the Open University of China. Earlier he was director of advertising solutions at Shanda's ad subsidiary, Shanghai Shengyue (2010-13).
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO (2018-19) and vice chairman of Qutoutiao Inc.; no current public role found
research_notes: Qutoutiao was delisted from Nasdaq in 2023, and I found no current company or personal contact. He is low-profile since stepping down as CEO in 2019. Don't confuse him with other people named Li Lei (e.g. former ByteDance AI Lab head Lei Li).

name: Wang Yanzhi
profile: Chinese mobile-game publisher. After stints at Kunlun and other game firms he founded Lemeng Interactive in 2012, sold it to Zhongqing Longtu (Locojoy) in 2013 and built its publishing arm as COO. He then founded Gaea, a game publisher focused on overseas markets, in which he controls about 77%.
interesting_fact: As Longtu's COO he signed the hit mobile game 'Dota Legends' (刀塔传奇), which pushed Longtu into China's top-10 game publishers.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Lemeng Interactive (乐檬互动, founded 2012), was fully acquired by Zhongqing Longtu within about a year (May 2013), and its team became the core of Longtu's mobile publishing division.
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Gaea Mobile / 盖娅互娱 (Beijing/Shenzhen game publisher); latest-role sources are older
research_notes: Gaea Mobile (盖娅互娱) is listed on China's NEEQ/BSE as 430181; company filings are the best source for an official contact. No personal social accounts found. Current status (2024+) not verified.

name: Xing Jiaxing
profile: Born 1972 in Pucheng, Fujian, he moved to Shanghai in 1994, began as a clothing sales agent and launched the La Chapelle womenswear brand, aiming to build a 'Chinese Zara'; it became the only Chinese apparel company dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong (A+H). He stepped down as chairman in 2020 and no longer controls the company.
interesting_fact: During the 2003 SARS outbreak he bet against the downturn and ramped up production; when shoppers returned, deep discounting made La Chapelle a nationally known brand.
deep_cut_fact: He learned his trade at a clothing-design training school for just six months, then worked at a Fuzhou garment firm sewing clothes, staffing the counter and delivering goods by bicycle before becoming a business supervisor. He later built a 1,000-mu cherry-orchard leisure farm (樱园) in his home village of Yangdun, Xianyang town.
current_role: Founder and former chairman of La Chapelle (拉夏贝尔); no current executive role found (resigned Feb 2020)
research_notes: Sensitive: lost control of La Chapelle in 2020 after his shares were judicially auctioned, and the company later faced bankruptcy proceedings. Avoid these topics. No current public contact route found; hometown agritourism project may be his current focus.

name: Sun Feng
profile: Sun Feng (孙丰, b. 1978) founded Secote in Suzhou in June 2007 and still runs it as chairman and GM. Secote makes automated assembly and inspection equipment for consumer electronics makers and has expanded into semiconductor wafer inspection equipment. He and co-controller Zeng Hui are the company's actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Unusually for a listed-company chairman, Sun Feng also personally serves as Secote's board secretary, the officer responsible for investor relations and disclosure.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Secote he started out as a test engineer at Kunshan KONE Elevator (昆山通力电梯), then ran a small automation equipment factory in Suzhou's Wuzhong development zone.
current_role: Founder, Chairman, General Manager and Board Secretary, Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic Co. (SSE: 603283)
research_notes: Since he is also board secretary, the securities office email (zqb@secote.com) reaches his own office. Low English-language profile.

name: Zeng Hui
profile: Zeng Hui (曾慧, b. 1977) co-founded Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic in 2007 with Sun Feng; the Shanghai-listed company makes automated/intelligent manufacturing and inspection equipment for consumer-electronics makers. She served as general manager from 2015 and remains a top shareholder, directly holding 18.85% as of Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Secote's 36Kr company profile lists her as founder and general manager with a junior-college (dazhuan) education, building the company from a 2007 startup into a listed automation-equipment maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Secote she did sales work at Shanghai Liangrui Electronics (1999-2002) and then was deputy general manager of Yanling Automation Equipment Factory in Suzhou's Wuzhong Economic Development Zone (2002-2007).
current_role: Co-founder and ~18.85% shareholder (one of the controlling shareholders) of Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic (603283.SH)
research_notes: Feb 2026 SSE filing confirms her 18.85% stake (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-02-28/1224987773.PDF); an Aug 2025 company notice mentions her separately from directors/officers, so she may no longer hold an executive post. No published personal contact; route via Secote board office.

name: Wang Shouchun
profile: Wang Shouchun (b. June 1962) founded Shandong Xiantan in Yantai in June 2001, building it into a listed integrated broiler-chicken producer; he and his wife Qu Lirong are the actual controllers. He still chairs the company, with filings in 2024-25 showing him chairing board meetings and proposing dividends.
interesting_fact: He and his wife together held 83.68% of Xiantan before its Shenzhen IPO, per the 2013 prospectus.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Xiantan in 2001 he ran a sole-proprietor business and contract farming; a Shandong Agricultural University economics-management graduate, he was named a 'Shandong Rural Star' and an outstanding figure of Muping district's 30 years of reform.
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shandong Xiantan Co. (仙坛股份, SZSE: 002746)
research_notes: IR email is from the 2013 IPO prospectus; check the latest annual report for the current one. Also vice-chair of the China Animal Agriculture Association's presidium (as of 2013).

name: Qu Lirong
profile: Qu Lirong is one of the actual controllers of Shandong Xiantan Group, a Yantai-based white-feather broiler company spanning feed, breeding, hatching, farming, slaughter and chicken processing. She holds about 21.34% (183.6m shares) and acts in concert with her husband, controlling shareholder Wang Shouchun; Xiantan reported H1 2026 revenue of RMB 2.99bn.
interesting_fact: Xiantan says it has more than twenty years of experience in white-feather broiler farming and slaughter, running an integrated chain from feed mills to chicken processing.
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (21.34%), Shandong Xiantan Group (SZSE: 002746); no executive post found
research_notes: Hurun lists the company as 'Xian Tan'. Shareholder only, no public profile found; approach via husband/chairman Wang Shouchun or the board-secretary office email.

name: Hu Liping
profile: Hu Liping (b. 1970, Mongolian ethnicity) is a finance executive who spent his career at dairy giant Yili, serving as executive director and board secretary from 2005 and also chairing Yili Finance Co. His wealth comes from roughly 79 million Yili shares built up via the 2006 share reform, equity incentives and stock dividends. He resigned as board secretary in December 2018.
interesting_fact: At end-2017 he held 79.3 million Yili shares (about 1.31%, the 8th-largest holder), worth nearly RMB 2bn at the time he resigned in Dec 2018.
deep_cut_fact: A finance specialist by training, he started out as finance supervisor at a Yili mineral-water subsidiary, then ran the group's settlement centre and was assistant to the president before becoming board secretary.
current_role: Former director, vice president and board secretary of Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group (600887); current role not confirmed
research_notes: Has kept a low profile since leaving Yili's board-secretary post in 2018; no public contacts found.

name: Yuan Meng
profile: Listed on the 2020 Hurun China Rich List with RMB 2.9bn (rank 1,883) as one of nine people whose wealth comes from SF Holding (顺丰), the express-delivery group founded by Wang Wei. Role at SF not found.
interesting_fact: One of nine SF-linked people on the 2020 Hurun list, alongside founder Wang Wei.
research_notes: Low profile. No source found for Yuan Meng's role at SF (possibly an early partner/shareholder; unverified). SF's filings searched did not name this person.

name: Guo Xiangwen
profile: Guo Xiangwen (郭向文) built Shanxi Kangwei Group from Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke, set up in 2000 with him as legal representative. In 2012 Yongtai Energy paid RMB 2.895bn for 65% of Kangwei (a RMB 1.5bn capital injection plus RMB 1.395bn for 31% from Guo and employee share funds). He then held Yongtai shares (about 70m in 2014), and still appeared in its top-10 holders in 2020.
interesting_fact: Kangwei was a rural collective turned private company. Until 2012 three employee share-fund associations, one with about 420 worker members, owned about 36% of the group alongside Guo.
deep_cut_fact: Kangwei began as the Nanshan coal mine in Baizi town, Qinyuan County. It was restructured in 2000 into Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke with registered capital of only RMB 820,000. Twelve years later Yongtai valued the group at billions.
current_role: Founder and former chairman/Party secretary of Shanxi Kangwei Group (Qinyuan County coal and coke); 65% sold to Yongtai Energy (600157.SH) in 2012; current role unverified
research_notes: Identity confirmed via Yongtai Energy filings on cninfo (2012 acquisition report; 2015 notice that Guo personally paid the 2014 profit-guarantee shortfall: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2015-06-24/1201186581.PDF). That payment is neutral but avoid it in outreach. Very local, low-profile Shanxi coal owner; no published contact. Kangwei is now a Yongtai subsidiary.

name: Tao Yishan
profile: Hunan-born (Ningxiang, b. 1955) agribusiness executive who rose from grain-station worker to director of the Zhuzhou municipal feed factory, then chaired Xiangda Group before becoming chairman of Tangrenshen in 2000. Tangrenshen is a Zhuzhou-based feed, hog-farming and meat-products group listed in Shenzhen; he still chaired its board meetings in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: He was a deputy to China's 10th National People's Congress and has served as executive vice president of the China Feed Industry Association and vice president of the China Meat Association.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1972 at the Hetang district grain station in Zhuzhou, followed by a decade at the Zhuzhou municipal rice mill, before he ran the city feed factory (1985-1993).
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Tangrenshen Group (唐人神, 002567.SZ)
research_notes: Current chairmanship confirmed by Aug 2026 board notice (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202608281828640649_1.pdf). Biographical details come from a user-uploaded profile on maigoo.com; treat as secondary. Route via Tangrenshen board secretary / IR.

name: Victor Cha Mao Ching
profile: Hong Kong property executive and son of Dr. Cha Chi Ming. He joined HKR International's board in 1989, became managing director (2001), deputy chairman (2007) and chairman (2020); his background spans property development and textile manufacturing. He is also a non-executive director of Mingly Corporation.
interesting_fact: He chairs the Hong Kong Arts Festival and has chaired the HKTDC's Hong Kong-Japan Business Co-operation Committee.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Sloan Fellow at Stanford University (MBA) and was named a University Fellow of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University in 2010.
current_role: Executive Chairman and Managing Director, HKR International Ltd (board effective 9 Oct 2026)
research_notes: Current title confirmed via report of HKRI board structure effective 9 Oct 2026: https://www.itiger.com/news/1130580564 . HKRI website (hkri.com) blocked automated access, so no published press/IR email captured; best route is HKRI corporate communications or the Hong Kong Arts Festival.

name: Guo Chenghui
profile: Listed on Hurun China (2020-2021) with wealth from 'Cathay' (biomedicine). Possibly linked to Cathay Biotech (凯赛生物, SSE STAR 688065, listed 2020), but no source read in this task connects 郭成辉 to that company; Cathay Biotech is described as founded by Dr. Xiucai Liu.
research_notes: Identity not confirmed; do not use without verifying via Cathay Biotech prospectus/shareholder list.

name: Kwok Siu Ming
profile: Dr Simon Kwok Siu Ming co-founded Sa Sa with his wife Eleanor Kwok in 1978, starting from a 40 sq ft cosmetics counter in Causeway Bay. He built it into a major Asian beauty retail chain, listed in Hong Kong in 1997, and remains chairman and CEO per the 2025/26 annual report.
interesting_fact: He was named Business Person of the Year at the DHL/SCMP Hong Kong Business Awards 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Sa Sa he worked as a parking meter repairman; the first shop was a basement unit in President Shopping Centre on Jaffe Road, Causeway Bay.
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Sa Sa International Holdings (HKEX:178)
research_notes: Also known as a racehorse owner (Royal Ascot owner profile exists). Wife Eleanor Kwok is vice-chairman.

name: Hou Bo-yi
profile: Hou Bo-yi (侯博義) is a grandson of Tainan Group elder Hou Yu-li, whose family fortune is tied to Tainan Spinning and the wider Tainan Group. He took over management of Universal Cement in 2008, a company founded in 1959 by Wu San-lien and Hou Yu-li, and has run it with his sons, who are credited with turning it from losses to profits.
interesting_fact: Universal Cement, which he chairs, was founded in 1959 by Wu San-lien and his grandfather Hou Yu-li, and holds Taiwan's top market share in gypsum board.
deep_cut_fact: The Hou family motto handed down from his grandfather Hou Yu-li is '一分實力做一分事' ('do only as much as your real strength allows'). He is described as reserved and rarely gives long media interviews.
current_role: Chairman, Universal Cement Corp. (環球水泥, TWSE: 1104), Taiwan
interesting_fact_source: https://www.tatlerasia.com/the-scene/people-parties/家族企業的背後那份世代傳承的侯式精神縱橫談環球水泥集團侯智元侯博義侯智升專訪
deep_cut_fact_source: https://www.tatlerasia.com/the-scene/people-parties/家族企業的背後那份世代傳承的侯式精神縱橫談環球水泥集團侯智元侯博義侯智升專訪
research_notes: Taiwanese, though Hurun lists him under China. His brother Hou Bo-ming (侯博明) ran Tainan Spinning (businesstoday.com.tw 2007). Company spokesperson per cnyes: 楊宗仁. ucc@ucctw.com is the company's general email, not a personal one. He is very private.

name: Hu Jidan
profile: Hu Jidan (胡继丹) appears in Yealink's 2024 annual report as one of the company's ten largest shareholders, holding unrestricted shares as a domestic individual. Yealink is a Xiamen-based maker of enterprise video-conferencing and VoIP communications equipment. No biography or management role was found.
current_role: Individual shareholder (domestic natural person) among the top 10 shareholders of Xiamen Yealink Network Technology (SZSE: 300628); no executive role found
research_notes: Very low public profile; not listed as director or executive. Shareholding confirmed in Yealink 2024 annual report (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-04-21/1223154940.PDF) and Q1 2025 report. Only route is via the company. Website is the company's, not his.

name: Hu Zhirong
profile: Born 1962, Hu Zhirong controls Warom Technology, a Shanghai-based maker of explosion-proof electrical equipment that also has professional-lighting and new-energy businesses. The group traces its origins to 1987, and the listed company went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in May 2017. Hu holds about 34% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Warom is led by its explosion-proof equipment business, which is used in hazardous oil, gas, chemical and mining settings, and it now also does professional lighting and new energy.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Warom, Hu is listed as executive director of Shanghai Zunrong Yacht Club (上海尊荣游艇俱乐部) and vice-chairman of Fuji Elevator (Sichuan), according to Warom's 2025 annual report.
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and legal representative of Warom Technology (华荣科技, SSE: 603855); chairman of Warom Group
public_contact: ir_email: hrzhd@warom.com | office_email: warom@warom.com | official_website: https://www.warom.com
research_notes: Low media profile. Best route is the board secretary's office (Song Zongbin, hrzhd@warom.com). Relevant to the energy theme (explosion-proof gear for oil and gas, plus new energy).

name: Hua Nan
profile: Hua Nan co-founded the marketing-strategy firm Huayuhua (华与华) with his brother Hua Shan, which in 2006 invested to set up Dook Media, a book planning and distribution house. As chairman he built hits such as the Tibet Code (藏地密码) series; Dook listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2021. He held about 41% directly as of Q3 2025; a planned control change was called off in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: He has said his entry into publishing was 'very accidental'; after his first promoted title took off, the 2008 Tibet Code (藏地密码) series became a milestone, selling about 5.8 million copies by end-2020.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dook's IPO he was named China's Publisher of the Year (中国年度出版人) in 2009, credited with planning bestsellers including Tibet Code and The Godfather trilogy edition.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Dook Media Group (读客文化, SZ:301025), Shanghai
research_notes: Dook Media is listed (301025.SZ); IR/board-secretary contact is in its exchange filings (not verified here). Brother Hua Shan is the better-known public figure (Huayuhua).

name: Huang Ping
profile: Huang Ping (黄平) is vice chairman and general manager of Shenghe Resources, a Chinese rare-earth group, and a major individual shareholder (about 5.49% per a 2024 pledge announcement). He acted as chairman between July and September 2024 after the previous chairman left, before Xie Bing was elected. In 2026 he presented the company's overseas project plans.
interesting_fact: He temporarily performed the chairman's duties of Shenghe Resources from July 2024 until a new chairman was elected in September 2024.
current_role: Vice Chairman and General Manager, Shenghe Resources Holding (盛和资源, 600392.SH)
research_notes: Common name; identity tied via Shenghe Resources role. Current role per 2026 reports (https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20260905/c679622411.shtml). No personal bio found. Rare earths relevant to energy/data-center supply chain angle.

name: Jia Haibo
profile: Jia Haibo (贾海波) is a co-founder-era executive and major shareholder (~3-5%) of Yangling Metron New Material, a Shaanxi maker of electroplated diamond wire used to slice silicon wafers for solar and semiconductors. He served as the company's CEO from 2015 to 2021 before moving to chief technology officer.
interesting_fact: Metron's diamond wire is a key consumable for cutting photovoltaic silicon, tying his fortune directly to China's solar manufacturing boom.
current_role: CTO & non-independent director, Yangling Metron New Material Co. (300861.SZ)
research_notes: Roles per Yahoo Finance / MarketScreener insider profile (https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/HAI-BO-JIA-A258UD/experience/). Chairman is Liu Haiying (elected Nov 2024). A share-transfer agreement involving Zhang Yingjiu and Jia Haibo was reported; stake may have changed. Route via company board secretary.

name: Kuai Jiaqi
appears_on: Hurun China (2020-2021); Hurun China U40 (2020-2021); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2020)
profile: MIT-trained logistics engineer who founded Dada in July 2014 with Sequoia backing. It is a crowdsourced same-city instant-delivery platform that merged with JD to Home in 2016 and listed on Nasdaq (DADA) in June 2020. He stepped down as chairman and CEO in August 2022. Reports said he might turn to investing and mentoring founders.
interesting_fact: Within about a year of launch, Dada reportedly had over 100,000 delivery couriers on its crowdsourced platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dada he co-founded online ad platform AdChina (易传媒) and then joined property-listing site Anjuke, both later acquired. He decided that staying independent meant picking industries where both supply and demand are fragmented, citing Uber.
current_role: Founder and former chairman & CEO of Dada Group (stepped down 31 Aug 2022); no current public role found
research_notes: On leaving he said: 'The past eight years have been a very exciting journey' (https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_19573756). No personal public contact found. Dada IR is the institutional route, but it is now under JD.

name: Li Chunrong
profile: Li Chunrong chairs Jinling Sports, a Zhangjiagang (Jiangsu)-based, A-share-listed maker of high-end sports equipment that also does venue construction, public fitness and event services. He and his family (as joint actual controllers) held about 52% of the company as of Dec 2025, the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: Jinling Sports' shares hit the 20% daily limit-up in June 2025, riding enthusiasm for Jiangsu's 'Su Chao' city football league.
current_role: Chairman (董事长) and legal representative, Jiangsu Jinling Sports Equipment Co. (金陵体育, SZSE: 300651)
research_notes: Chairman role confirmed in the company's April 2025 board announcement (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-04-22/1223186970.PDF). Interesting fact from a search summary of the yzwb page (not fetched directly). Very low English-language profile; route via company board secretary/IR. No published personal contacts found.

name: Liang Chen
profile: Liang Chen (梁晨, b. 1962) founded Hichain Logistics in Wujiang, Suzhou in Aug 2011 and is its controlling shareholder; it listed on Shenzhen ChiNext in 2020 and provides supply-chain logistics, logistics equipment and warehouse automation for consumer-electronics, EV, semiconductor and other manufacturers. She signs the 2024 ESG report as chairman.
interesting_fact: Her career started in finance, not logistics: she was an accountant at Guangdong Weiguo Machinery Factory (1980-89) and worked at China Construction Bank Wujiang branch (1989-99) before running trading and logistics firms.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Hichain she was general manager of Haichen Trading (1999-2003) and then of Hengtong Haichen (2003-2011), the predecessor logistics business, per the IPO prospectus.
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Hichain Logistics Co., Ltd. (Hichain, 300873.SZ)
research_notes: Female founder (prospectus: 梁晨女士). Hurun co-listing Yang Xi is a fellow Hichain director/vice GM. IR email is the securities department contact published in the 2024 ESG report.

name: Yang Xi
profile: Yang Xi is the former name of Liang Zhirui, who with his mother, chairman and GM Liang Chen, is co-actual controller of Hichain Logistics, a Suzhou/Shenzhen-based provider of integrated logistics for global technology manufacturers that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in August 2020. Third-party profiles list Liang Zhirui as a director and deputy GM.
interesting_fact: Hichain's 2025 interim report notes that Liang Zhirui 'formerly named Yang Xi' (曾用名杨曦) is a joint actual controller alongside controlling shareholder Liang Chen.
current_role: Co-actual controller of Jiangsu Hichain Logistics Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300873); now known as Liang Zhirui (梁智睿)
research_notes: Search under 'Liang Zhirui' rather than Yang Xi. Hichain's 2024 ESG report also lists irm@hichain.com (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-04-19/1223150714.PDF). Director/deputy GM title from Simply Wall St via search snippet only, not opened.

name: Liao Tengjia
profile: Liao Tengjia (廖腾佳) is a Guangzhou property developer with nearly 30 years in Chinese real estate. He chaired HK-listed Zhuguang Holdings (2009-13), was its CEO (2015-17) and has been deputy chairman since March 2017. A 2022 HKEX filing says he beneficially owns 36% of controlling shareholder Rong De.
interesting_fact: He is one of the ultimate owners of Rong De Investment, controlling shareholder of Zhuguang Holdings; a 2022 HKEX filing put his stake in Rong De at 36%.
current_role: Deputy Chairman and Executive Director, Zhuguang Holdings Group (1176.HK)
research_notes: Officer history per webb-site.com (officers.asp?p=4922) and HKEX filings. Couldn't load the company website (zhuguang.com.hk) for an IR contact. Low public profile.

name: Lin Xiaofa
profile: Lin Xiaofa (b. 1973, Fujian) is co-founder and chairman of Jomoo, a Xiamen-headquartered kitchen and bathroom fixtures maker founded in 1990 that grew from a family workshop into one of Asia's largest sanitary-ware bases, selling in 120+ countries. He is pushing global expansion and smart manufacturing.
interesting_fact: In 2009, when Jomoo's annual sales had just passed 2 billion yuan, he set the goal of a '10-billion-yuan, 100-year Jomoo'; in 2023 he said Jomoo should become the sanitary-ware industry's first brand with a 100-billion-yuan market value.
deep_cut_fact: He started out making dust-suppression spray systems for coal-cutting machines before applying spray tech to bathrooms; after a 1995 trip to Europe he led the team that made China's first handheld shower (花洒), and earlier China's first quick-open faucet.
current_role: Party Secretary and Chairman, Jomoo Group (九牧集团); member of 14th CPPCC National Committee
research_notes: Company site jomoo.com; no published press/IR email found (Jomoo is private). Also held roles as Fujian Federation of Industry & Commerce vice chairman; named a National Model Worker.

name: Liu Zhixin
profile: Founder-chairman of Ficont, which started selling suspended work platforms overseas and around 2008 pivoted to high-altitude safety equipment (tower lifts, ladders, fall protection) for wind turbines under the '3S Lift' brand. Listed on the Shanghai main board in May 2021.
interesting_fact: Ficont's wind-turbine work-at-height safety equipment held about two-thirds of the China market in 2019, per a Shanghai Securities News interview with Liu at the 2021 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: The company's '3S Lift' brand stands for Safe, Simple, Specialized.
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Ficont (中际联合), Shanghai-listed - largest shareholder (~39.5% per 36Kr)
research_notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (wind-power O&M equipment). Shares Hurun listing with Yu Haiyan. 36Kr source: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678253559985159

name: Yu Haiyan
profile: Yu Haiyan is the wife of chairman/president Liu Zhixin and, with him, the actual controller of Ficont (中际联合, brand 3S), which makes wind-turbine tower lifts, climb-assist devices and other high-altitude safety equipment. She was a director 2016-2023 and is now a vice president; the company listed in Shanghai in May 2021.
interesting_fact: Ficont's 3S-branded tower lifts ride inside wind-turbine towers; the company has subsidiaries in the US (3S Americas), India, Hong Kong and the Middle East and is pushing into Europe and Brazil.
current_role: Vice President and co-actual controller, China Ficont / 3S Industry (中际联合, SSE: 605305), Beijing
research_notes: Per 2025 annual report she holds no shares directly or indirectly; husband Liu Zhixin holds ~28%. Directly relevant to the wind-energy angle; Liu Zhixin is the public face.

name: Pan Huarong
profile: Pan Huarong (潘华荣) built Focus Lightings from a small plant in Suzhou Industrial Park (founded 2010, ChiNext IPO 2017) into a leading LED epitaxial-wafer and chip maker, expanding counter-cyclically through three downturns. He is steering it toward a compound-semiconductor platform: Mini/Micro LED, auto lighting, AR, optical interconnect and space PV.
interesting_fact: Focus Lightings has taped out prototype Micro LED CPO (co-packaged optics) array chips with a strategic customer; Pan says AI data-center expansion will accelerate commercial optical interconnects.
deep_cut_fact: Known for a low-key, almost obsessive 'product-first' style, he told Shanghai Securities News in 2026: 'We don't chase being No. 1 in scale, but we pursue leadership in profitability' (我们不追求规模上的第一，但追求盈利能力上的领先).
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Focus Lightings Technology (聚灿光电, SZSE: 300708), Suzhou
research_notes: Good data-center angle (CPO/optical interconnect Micro LED chips; joint lab with CAS Suzhou Nano institute on optical interconnect and space PV). Company email is a general corporate address; IR materials at stocknotice.asp. Chinese-language approach advised.

name: Pan Yanqing
profile: Co-founder (2007) and chairman of SK Automation (先惠技术), a Shanghai maker of intelligent automation equipment for automotive production; he and GM Wang Yinglin jointly control the company. Originally serving carmakers such as VW and BMW, it has since 2019 grown on lithium-battery module/PACK lines for CATL and other battery makers.
interesting_fact: SK Automation pivoted from automaker assembly lines into EV battery equipment, winning orders from CATL from 2019; its customers have included BMW Brilliance, SAIC-VW, VW Germany, CATL and Farasis.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding the company he held senior roles at Shanghai Volkswagen and Bosch Rexroth; per Shanghai Securities News he turned down a company-sponsored PhD opportunity at Bosch to start a business making domestic substitutes for imported (mostly German) auto equipment.
current_role: Chairman (and CTO per 2023 report), Shanghai SK Automation Technology / 先惠技术 (SSE STAR: 688155)
research_notes: Battery/EV manufacturing equipment angle relevant to energy. IR contact available via company's SSE filings (board secretary). Deep-cut PhD detail read via search snippet of the cnstock article (page fetch failed).

name: Peng You
profile: Peng You is chairman and, with his wife Wang Lingli, co-actual controller of Anhui Coreach Technology (Xinruida), a Hefei company founded in 2012 that makes display backlight modules, quantum-dot and Mini LED display modules, automotive displays and healthy smart lighting systems; it is listed in Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: In a 2022 China Securities Journal interview Peng said Coreach was pushing into semiconductor packaging, in-car displays and smart sensing, had IATF16949 automotive certification and had already sent Mini LED display samples to local carmakers.
deep_cut_fact: Peng told China Securities Journal (May 2022) that Coreach was developing 570nm-plus wavelength light sources paired with sensors to shine into skin tissue, so they could serve as heart-rate modules in smart wearables.
current_role: Chairman, Anhui Coreach Technology Co., Ltd. (002983.SZ), Hefei
research_notes: Peng You and Wang Lingli are husband and wife and joint actual controllers per the IPO prospectus (SZSE disclosure). A third-party data source has listed him as CEO with a ~55% stake. Best route is the company board office.

name: Wang Lingli
profile: Wang Lingli (王玲丽) and her husband Peng You (chairman and general manager) are the actual controllers of Anhui Coreach Technology, a Hefei-based maker of display optoelectronic (backlight) systems and smart lighting, listed in Shenzhen. Per the 2020 annual report, the couple controlled about 71% of the company, hers held via two partnerships she runs.
interesting_fact: Coreach's ownership is a husband-wife structure: Peng You held 55.76% directly while Wang Lingli, as executive partner of Xinhui Investment and Xinzhi Consulting, controlled another 15.38%.
deep_cut_fact: She is executive partner of Xinzhi Consulting, Coreach's employee share-ownership partnership (she contributed 45.79% of its capital), and of Anhui Xinhui Investment, set up in March 2016.
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and administrative manager (as of 2020 annual report), Anhui Coreach Technology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002983)
research_notes: Low public profile; husband Peng You is the public face. Role info from the 2020 annual report (Mar 2021); may have changed. IR email is the company securities department.

name: Shi Weili
profile: A materials scientist born in October 1978 with a PhD from SUNY Buffalo (2006). He worked at several US materials companies before returning to lead DK Electronic Materials, a Yixing-based maker of conductive silver pastes for solar cell metallization (PERC, TOPCon, HJT, TBC). DK has since expanded into semiconductor packaging pastes and, through its Jiangsu Jingkai acquisition, memory chips (LPDDR/DDR4).
interesting_fact: DK has led mass-production use of high-copper pastes for TOPCon cells and is developing pure-copper metallization, aimed at cutting the solar industry's dependence on costly silver. It now aims to be a global high-performance electronic materials and memory technology company.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking over DK in 2013 he worked in the US as senior chemist at Evident Technologies (2006-08), project manager at Nano Dynamics (2008-09), researcher/consultant at Henkel (2009-10), and R&D scientist at Ferro Corporation (2010-12).
current_role: Chairman & General Manager (since Apr 2013), Wuxi DK Electronic Materials Co., Ltd. (300842.SZ); one of its actual controllers
research_notes: Strong fit for the energy angle (solar PV materials) and the AI/memory angle. He was US-trained and likely comfortable in English. Best route is IR at ir@dkem.cn.

name: Sui Guodong
profile: Sui Guodong (隋国栋) founded SMZDM ('What's Worth Buying'), China's shopping-recommendation and consumer-content platform, in 2010 and took it public in Shenzhen; post-IPO he controlled about 50.8% of the shares. As chairman he focuses on strategy, and in May 2024 launched an 'all-in AI' strategy to rebuild the core app as AI-native and expand overseas.
interesting_fact: In May 2024 he announced a full AI strategy for Zhidemai, planning to turn its core apps into AI-native products and push overseas.
deep_cut_fact: smzdm.com launched on 30 June 2010 as Sui's personal 'geek' blog of product finds and reviews; early on the site would crash if ~300 people visited at once - five years later it drew tens of millions of daily visits.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Zhidemai Technology (值得买科技, SMZDM, 300785.SZ)
research_notes: Company insists on platform neutrality ('我们绝不站队' - won't take investment from any e-commerce platform; ifanr 2015). Reported as first president of the Fengtai District International Chamber of Commerce (search summary, unverified).

name: Wang Yinglin
profile: Wang Yinglin has been general manager and a director of Shanghai SK Automation (先惠技术) since its founding in 2007, and holds roughly a fifth of its shares per data aggregators. The Shanghai company makes intelligent manufacturing equipment such as EV battery-module/pack lines and chassis and engine assembly lines.
interesting_fact: A MarketScreener headline reports SK Automation landing a '106 Million' deal with battery giant CATL.
current_role: General Manager and Director, Shanghai SK Automation Technology Co., Ltd. (SSE STAR: 688155)
research_notes: Aggregators disagree on gender/age; no personal biography found. Chairman/CTO is Pan Yanqing. Best route is via company investor relations (688155).

name: Wang Zengduo
profile: Wang Zengduo (b. 1963) founded Guanglian Aviation, a Harbin maker of aviation tooling, aerospace parts and drones, and is its controlling shareholder (about 23.6%). A BUAA computer-science graduate, he built a string of Harbin electronics and precision-machinery firms before setting up the aviation composites tooling business in 2011.
interesting_fact: He began his career in 1987 as a computer-centre technician at Harbin Aircraft Manufacturing Corp. He later built his own aviation-tooling supplier.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics in computer science and engineering. In 1992-96 he chaired the Hafei Group computer company before founding Harbin Guanglian Electronics.
current_role: Chairman and Party Secretary, Guanglian Aviation Industry Co. (300900.SZ), Harbin
research_notes: Since 2024 he has also chaired Jingdezhen Hangsheng Aviation Machinery.

name: Pan Dongxiao
profile: Wei Dongxiao (魏东晓) has chaired and run Zhongfu Information, a Jinan-based cybersecurity and data-security firm, since 2013. Founded in 2002 and listed on ChiNext in 2017, Zhongfu sells classified-information protection, data-security and electromagnetic-security products, mainly to government bodies and state enterprises. Simply Wall St puts his direct stake at about 22%.
interesting_fact: Zhongfu says it launched China's first practical security/secrecy-inspection tool in 2004. In 2019 it won what it describes as China's largest Xinchuang (domestic IT substitution) security project.
deep_cut_fact: Zhongfu says that in 2018, at the 2nd National Secrecy Exhibition, it first proposed the concepts of 'smart secrecy' and 'digital government secrecy governance'. Its motto, 至诚于中 业成于孚, plays on the company name.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhongfu Information Inc. (中孚信息, SZSE ChiNext: 300659), Jinan
research_notes: The romanised name in the input ('Pan Dongxiao') does not match the Chinese name 魏东晓, which is Wei Dongxiao. That is the Zhongfu chairman (MarketScreener: 'Dong Xiao Wei', age 57).
