name: Huang Qinghe
profile: Huang Qinghe (黄庆和, born 1961) is a landscape engineer and designer who co-founded Guangzhou PB Landscape (普邦园林) with Tu Shanzhong and Huang Jianping. He was its chief designer and later vice-chairman. The company listed in Shenzhen in 2012 as a major landscaping, design and ecological-engineering firm. He remains a top-10 shareholder and honorary vice-chairman.
interesting_fact: He personally led award-winning landscape designs, including the Phase II grounds of Guangzhou's Chimelong Hotel (2010 grand gold award, Chinese Society of Landscape Architecture) and residential projects that won China's Zhan Tianyou civil-engineering prize.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding PB he was head of the horticulture section at Guangzhou's Yuexiu Park, the city's largest historic urban park.
current_role: Co-founder, major shareholder and Honorary Vice-Chairman, PB Landscape (普邦股份, SZSE 002663), Guangzhou
research_notes: Not the controlling shareholder (that is Tu Shanzhong). Bio is from the 2013 annual report; current honorary vice-chairman title and IR email are from the 2025 annual report. Designer, not a dealmaker, so a design or landscape angle may land better.

interesting_fact: Golden Dragon says it is the only copper-tube maker to win a National Science and Technology Progress Award (second class); its tubes also go into computer heat dissipation and solar applications.
current_role: Former head/major owner of Golden Dragon Precise Copper Tube Group (金龙精密铜管集团); current role unknown

name: Cao Hongguang
profile: Born 1962; a medical doctor turned medical-imaging entrepreneur who co-founded Shanghai-based iRay, a maker of digital X-ray flat-panel detectors, high-voltage generators and X-ray tubes for medical, industrial inspection and security uses, now also making silicon microdisplay backplanes for AR/VR. Chaired iRay 2012-2019 and remains a director and major indirect shareholder.
interesting_fact: iRay broke foreign dominance of digital X-ray flat-panel detectors, becoming China's No.1 and the world's No.3 supplier, and has moved into silicon-based OLED microdisplay backplanes for AI glasses and VR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: Before turning to imaging tech he was a neurosurgeon, attending then associate chief physician and deputy director of the neurosurgery institute at the Lanzhou Railway Bureau Central Hospital; he later chaired Beijing Heng Rui Mei Lian and was chief scientist at TCL Medical Radiology.
current_role: Director and core technical staff, iRay Technology Group (STAR: 688301), Shanghai; chairman 2012-2019
research_notes: Director term runs to Nov 2026 per 2025 annual report; check re-election. Holds stake via Hainan Heyi (where he is executive director) and Shanghai partnerships. Controller/chairman of iRay is Tieer Gu.

name: Cao Qidong
profile: Hong Kong industrialist and son of Ningbo-born tycoon Cao Kuang-piu (Novel Enterprises), whose 1997 investment created Yongxin Optics. He became chairman in 2007 and took it public in Shanghai in 2018. Yongxin makes high-end microscopes and precision optics. In 2026, aged 75, he became honorary chairman.
interesting_fact: Yongxin built China's first space microscope, installed on the Tianhe core module. It was used in the February 2022 'Tiangong classroom' broadcast to show beating heart-muscle cells in orbit. Yongxin also made camera lenses for the Chang'e-2, -3 and -4 lunar missions.
deep_cut_fact: The company name honours his father's Hong Kong group, Novel (永新). In Chinese it means 'forever innovating', and the English word deliberately evokes a long, legendary story. From 2005 Cao spent about two years acting as the bridge that completed Yongxin's acquisition of Nanjing Jiangnan Yongxin.
current_role: Honorary Chairman, Ningbo Yongxin Optics Co. (603297.SH); stepped down as chairman in 2026 after 19 years
research_notes: Recently retired to an honorary role (Securities Times, stcn.com/article/detail/4058883.html). He announced the succession in a letter to all shareholders on Yongxin's official WeChat account. Formal route: the Yongxin Optics board secretary office.

research_notes: Very low profile. She has a high-school education and is described as having worked in printing and dyeing all her career. Fu Shuangli is the public face. name: Shen Wanqiu

In 2001 he founded Highlander, which started with ship voyage-data recorders and grew into smart-ship and ocean-observation systems. It is now best known for building China's first commercial underwater data centre, with a version powered by offshore wind.
interesting_fact: Highlander completed China's first commercial underwater data centre off Hainan in 2022, cooled by seawater at a PUE of 1.15 or lower. It then launched a 'subsea data centre plus offshore wind' design in Shanghai Lingang, claiming 95% direct wind-power supply; the Hainan pods host a 675 PFlops AI compute cluster.
deep_cut_fact: He was named one of Tsinghua MBA's '20 People in 20 Years', and his company's systems served China's first aircraft carrier. Highlander's subsea data centre also won the UN Industrial Development Organization's first carbon-neutral technology leading-project award in 2022.
current_role: Founder, director and General Manager, Beijing Highlander Digital Technology (SZSE: 300065); chairman until October 2025
public_contact: office_email: hlx@highlander.com.cn | press_email: udc@highlander.com.cn (underwater data centre business) | official_website: http://www.highlander.com.cn
research_notes: Top fit for the podcast: underwater data centres powered by offshore wind. The Tsinghua MBA honour and the aircraft-carrier detail come from his Sina Finance resume and the company's founder statement (http://www.highlander.com.cn/speech.html). Lu Yaozu replaced him as chairman in October 2025, but he remains GM and a director. Web search quota ran out mid-lane; all facts come from the company site and filings.

research_notes: He is a passive investor with no executive role, and filings classify him as an overseas natural person. He is reducing his stake. No personal biography or contact is public. Company IR is a weak route.

name: Yao Chengzhi
profile: Born 1974, he heads and controls Ningbo Menovo Pharmaceutical, founded in 2004 and Shanghai-listed. It makes active pharmaceutical ingredients, intermediates and finished drugs, largely for export to regulated markets. He was re-elected to the board in May 2024.
interesting_fact: Menovo is an export-oriented API maker that partners with multinational generic and originator drugmakers for regulated markets in Europe and elsewhere.
deep_cut_fact: Before pharmaceuticals he worked at Ningbo United Group (宁波联合集团) and its import-export arm, a trading background that shaped Menovo's export-led model.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Ningbo Menovo Pharmaceutical (美诺华, SH: 603538); controlling shareholder via Ningbo Menovo Holdings
research_notes: IR email is the board-secretary contact in the 2024 annual report. Low media profile.

name: Zhou Lingen
profile: Hangzhou investor listed by Hurun (2020) for his stake in Hundsun Technologies, China's leading maker of trading and core-system software for brokerages, funds and banks (controlled since 2014 by Jack Ma's Zhejiang Rongxin). Filings show him holding ~1.77% (c. 34m shares), one of the largest individual holders.
interesting_fact: Hundsun, which began as Hangzhou Hundsun Software in the 1990s, is the back-office software backbone of much of China's securities industry; in 2014 Jack Ma's personal vehicle paid 3.3bn yuan for its parent, Hundsun Group.
current_role: Individual top-10 shareholder (~1.8%) of Hundsun Technologies (600570.SH), Hangzhou; no current executive role found
research_notes: Shareholding per Hundsun filings (shareholder table, 2022-2024). Likely part of Hundsun's founding/early team but not verified from a public source. Very low profile; only corporate IR route found.

name: Zhuo Chuguang
profile: Zhuo Chuguang (卓楚光, b. 1973) founded Guangzhou Songle Electronics in 2002, the predecessor of Guangdong DP (Jiuliang), which built the 'DP' brand of portable LED lights and torches sold mainly in emerging markets, and listed on ChiNext in 2019. He and his wife Guo Shaoyan sold their controlling stake in 2023-26 to a Shiyan (Hubei) state-linked investor; he remains a director.
interesting_fact: DP built its brand largely through overseas distribution networks in emerging markets for portable and rechargeable LED lighting, before a Hubei state-backed investor took control and renamed it Hubei Jiuliang.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business and served as vice-president of both the Guangdong Lighting Appliance Association and the Guangdong Chaoshan (Teochew) Chamber of Commerce.
current_role: Director (former chairman and GM), Hubei Jiuliang Co. (formerly Guangdong DP Co., 'DP 久量' LED lighting; SZSE ChiNext: 300808)
research_notes: Hurun 'DP' = Guangdong DP Co. (久量股份). Has largely exited after selling control; company IR is now run under new owners, so it's a weak route. Hurun listing shared with wife Guo Shaoyan.

name: Guo Shaoyan
profile: Guo Shaoyan (郭少燕) was, with Zhuo Chuguang and family members acting in concert, controlling shareholder of Guangdong DP (久量股份), a Shenzhen-listed (300808) maker of LED lighting products. In 2024 they sold stakes and waived voting rights so that Shiyan state-owned vehicle Zhongda Huixiang became controlling shareholder, with Shiyan SASAC as actual controller.
interesting_fact: The 2024 deal transferred control of the LED company from its founding family to the Shiyan (Hubei) municipal SASAC, with the first transfer of 11.42% registered on 2 July 2024.
current_role: Former co-controlling shareholder (with Zhuo Chuguang) of Guangdong DP Co. / Jiuliang (久量股份, 300808.SZ); control passed to Shiyan SASAC vehicle in 2024
research_notes: Hurun listing only 2020. After the 2024 deal she waived voting rights on her remaining ~11.18% stake. No personal profile found; low-value outreach target.

name: Padam chand Gupta
profile: Padam Chand Gupta co-founded PC Jeweller, the Delhi jewellery retailer named after him, with his brother Balram Garg. He sat on the board from the company's inception and was its chairman and a promoter. PC Jeweller announced his sudden death on 28 January 2019.
interesting_fact: PC Jeweller was a first-generation business started by two brothers, Padam Chand Gupta and Balram Garg, and named after Gupta, the elder brother.
current_role: Deceased (28 Jan 2019); was Chairman and non-executive director of PC Jeweller Ltd
research_notes: DECEASED: PC Jeweller's stock-exchange filing announced the death of chairman Shri Padam Chand Gupta on 28 Jan 2019 (https://bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/2b0c1313-f315-4e6d-9b84-f6c54662eab1.pdf). Do not contact. Surviving co-founder: Balram Garg.

name: Jia Tingliang
profile: Jia Tingliang (贾廷亮, b. Dec 1956) opened the Datuhe coal mine in his home village in 1985 and built Datuhe into an integrated mining, washing, coking, power, magnesium-alloy and coal-chemical group. With his wife Wang Suolan he was Shanxi's richest person on Hurun's 2006 list. Since Shanxi forced its 2.4 Mt/yr coking capacity to close, he has refocused on coal mining and the schools he founded.
interesting_fact: He built a complete private school system in Lüliang: Tingliang Kindergarten, Tingliang Primary, Tingliang Middle School and Fengshan Senior High, on a campus of 400+ mu covering preschool through high school.
deep_cut_fact: At 18 he was a labourer on the Wucheng reservoir project earning work points. He was then elected production-team leader of Datuhe village. Datuhe started with traditional 'earth' coking, hauling coal by donkey cart and walking tractor.
current_role: Founder and chairman of Shanxi Datuhe Coking Group (山西大土河焦化集团); legal representative of Shanxi Datuhe Energy Technology, Lishi, Lüliang, Shanxi
research_notes: Hurun 'Dutuhe' = 大土河 (Datuhe). CAUTION: he was arrested in 2015 in a unit-bribery case linked to a Lüliang official (The Paper, Dec 2015). He is now active again (school and company news in 2025-26), but avoid the topic. Energy angle: in Feb 2026 Datuhe joined other Shanxi coal firms (Xinmin, Meijin) in a RMB 240m heating JV (https://www.sohu.com/a/987195198_395101). Unlisted; no published contact.

name: Wang Suolan
profile: Wang Suolan (王锁兰) is the wife and business partner of Datuhe founder Jia Tingliang. The couple own Shanxi Datuhe Coking (Jia 82.5%, Wang 17.5%), a Lüliang coal, coke, power and coal-chemical group. They topped Shanxi on Hurun's 2006 list (RMB 4.2bn) and ranked 3rd in Shanxi in 2009 (RMB 6.8bn). She also holds directorships in group coal and trading companies.
interesting_fact: She ranked 34th on Hurun's 2006 list of China's richest women, one of the few women on the list whose fortune came from coal and coking.
current_role: Co-owner (17.5%) and former legal representative of Shanxi Datuhe Coking (山西大土河焦化); director of Shanxi Datuhe Energy Technology; legal representative of Taiyuan Jinyu Microcredit
research_notes: Hurun 'Dutuhe' = 大土河 (Datuhe). The shareholding split is from a Nov 2025 profile ('晋才晋商') and from registries (aiqicha/qizhidao). No interviews or personal profile found. Low public profile; any approach would go through Datuhe Group in Lishi. Note her husband's 2015 detention in a bribery case; avoid the topic.

name: Guo Jindong
profile: Guo Jindong (郭金东, b. 1965/66), a Nanjing native and senior economist, built Gpro Group (金浦集团) into a Nanjing conglomerate spanning petrochemicals and chemical materials (incl. titanium-dioxide maker Gpro Titanium and the Nanjing Jinling plastics/Jiangsu Zhongshan chemical JVs), plus real estate, hotels, aviation and agriculture. He was on the Hurun China list 2006-2019.
interesting_fact: In 2013 his group took over the shell of 1993-listed Jilin Pharmaceutical and turned it into Gpro Titanium, a titanium-dioxide pigment producer, with Guo chairing it until 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond chemicals, his filings list him as director of a winery (Gpro 'Dibboli' estate, 金浦帝博利酒庄), a Spanish food-industry company, Jiangsu Gpro Aviation and eco-farming/livestock ventures in Nanjing.
current_role: Chairman, Gpro Investment Holding Group (金浦投资控股集团, Nanjing) per latest public filings; chaired listed Gpro Titanium (SZSE 000545) 2013-2021
research_notes: Low public profile; not on Hurun since 2019. IR email belongs to Gpro Titanium, which he no longer chairs, so it is an indirect route. Current group status not verified (search quota ran out). Better fit for chemicals/real estate than data centers.

name: Li Heiji
profile: Li Heiji (李黑记, b. 1958, Baoji) built Dongling Group from a village collective into a Shaanxi conglomerate spanning steel, coal, chemicals and nonferrous metals, later trade supply chain and property, with 2022 revenue of about RMB 126B. He was a deputy to the 11th National People's Congress (2008). Dongling was put into bankruptcy restructuring in July 2024.
interesting_fact: He was named among the '100 Outstanding Private Entrepreneurs of 40 Years of Reform and Opening-Up' and served on the standing committee of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce.
deep_cut_fact: Dongling began in 1979 when villagers of Dongling village, Baoji, acting as a production team, built 16 street-front shop units and opened the 'Jintai District Lianmeng General Services Department' - the seed of what became a RMB 100B+ group.
current_role: Founder, chairman and Party secretary of Dongling Group, Baoji, Shaanxi (group entered bankruptcy proceedings in 2024)
research_notes: Sensitive: Dongling Group is in bankruptcy restructuring (2024), and older press covers a 2009 lead-poisoning protest at a group smelter. Current status of Li unclear; no published contacts (group site chinadljt.com appears defunct). Not recommended for outreach.

name: Xue Dingmin
profile: Xue Dingmin (薛靛民, b. Jan 1959, Beifangping village, Hejin), the 'Coke King of Shanxi', founded Sunshine Group in 1992. It is now a coal, coke, tar, carbon-black, fine-chemicals and carbon-materials group with its own power plant and rail line (2024 revenue RMB 15.8bn). He and his son control ~82%. Since 2023 Sunshine has been pursuing a Shanghai IPO to raise RMB 4bn.
interesting_fact: In 2006 Sunshine was China's second-largest private-sector taxpayer, and in 2007 the largest. In 2023 Shanxi named it 'chain leader' for the province's carbon-based new-materials industry.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sunshine he worked at Hejin's Laoyaotou coal mine and a glass factory. At 20, in 1979, he quit to start a trucking business. In 1986 he pooled funds to open the Xitie Trading Qingjian coal-washing plant, Sunshine's forerunner.
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and co-controlling shareholder (with son Xue Guofei) of Shanxi Sunshine Coking Group (山西阳光焦化集团), Hejin, Yuncheng, Shanxi
research_notes: Hurun 'Sunshine Group' = 山西阳光焦化集团 (not Jiangsu Sunshine). Energy angle: the IPO proceeds target a 3.69 Mt/yr coking project and a coke-oven-gas-to-LNG and ammonia plant. Once the SSE prospectus is public, its board-office contact would be the official route. I could not open SSE PDFs here (bot challenge). He was vice chairman of the Yuncheng CPPCC from 2006. Avoid the safety-incident coverage.

profile: Yan Jiying (闫吉英/阎吉英), from Jiexiu, Shanxi, founded Sanjia Group, a coal-chemical (coking) business that also developed the Mianshan mountain scenic area, Hurun's 'coal, tourism'. He died of illness in June 2015. Per The Beijing News (2017), his death left the group without a settled successor.
current_role: Deceased (died of illness in June 2015). Was founder and chairman of Shanxi Sanjia Coal Chemical Group (三佳煤化集团), Jiexiu, Jinzhong, Shanxi
research_notes: DECEASED: per The Beijing News (via Toutiao, July 2017) he died of illness two years earlier, i.e. 2015 (https://toutiao.com/group/6445420466404638990/). Another post dates it to June 2015. Not a podcast candidate. Hurun 'Sanjia' = 三佳 (Jiexiu).

profile: Wen Zhanghua (闻掌华), a postgraduate-educated economist, built Meidu Holdings in Deqing, Zhejiang from property into energy. As Meidu Energy, it bought US oil and gas fields in Texas and later expanded into lithium-battery materials and graphene. The listed company was delisted in May 2020 when its shares fell below par.
interesting_fact: A rare Chinese private buyer of US shale-era oil: in 2013 Meidu paid US$135m for Woodbine Acquisition LLC (Eagle Ford area, Texas), then added the Devon and Manti blocks in 2014-15. All three were held by Meidu America Energy (MDAE).
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Meidu Group (美都集团), Deqing, Zhejiang; formerly chairman and controller of Meidu Energy (SSE: 600175, delisted 2020)
research_notes: Hurun 'Meidu' = 美都 (Zhejiang). profile: Yang Jin (杨劲) co-founded Beijing-based Dongyi Risheng with Chen Hui in 1997; it became the first home-renovation company listed on China's A-share market (2014) and grew into a national interior-design and fit-out group. Hurun listed the pair 2014-2021. The company's chairman is now Zhang Jianhua, and neither founder appears among its 2026 directors or officers.
interesting_fact: Dongyi Risheng, founded in 1997, was the first Chinese home-decoration (家装) company to list on the A-share market, in 2014.
current_role: Co-founder of Dongyi Risheng Home Decoration Group (东易日盛, SZSE: 002713); not on the current (2026) board or management list
research_notes: Appears to have exited management (control/leadership change by 2025-26; not independently confirmed because web-search budget ran out). Company board office dyrs@dyrs.com.cn would not reach her directly. Very private.

name: Li Xinzhou
profile: Li Xinzhou (李新洲) founded Pioneer Pharma in Haikou in 1996, building a marketing and promotion platform for imported pharmaceuticals and medical devices in China; it listed on the HKEX main board in 2013. Renamed Shanghai Pioneer Holdings in 2021, it has since added environmental, eye-care, dental-implant and beauty divisions; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: The group has diversified well beyond drug distribution: it bought Hunan Tiantong Environmental in 2021, Q3 Medical's mainland China rights in 2023, and launched new units (电火时代 in 2024, beauty in 2025, dental implants in 2026).
deep_cut_fact: Before pharma he was an English teacher at the Jianghan Oilfield school (1981-84), then an English translator for CNOOC's South China Sea West company (1984-88), and later worked at Sumitomo's Hainan office.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Executive Director, China Pioneer Pharma Holdings / Shanghai Pioneer Holdings (1345.HK)
public_contact: office_email: info@pioneer-pharma.com (group general inbox) | contact_form: http://www.pioneer-pharma.com/contact.php
research_notes: Hurun pairs him with Wu Qian, who joined the board as a non-executive director in March 2026. The oil-industry early career offers a good hook for an energy podcast. Former Hainan CPPCC member.

name: Wu Qian
profile: Co-controlling shareholder of Pioneer Pharma, a Shanghai-based marketer and distributor of imported pharmaceuticals and medical devices in China, together with chairman Li Xinzhou; controls about 845 million shares directly and indirectly; appointed non-executive director in March 2026.
current_role: Non-Executive Director, Shanghai Pioneer Holding Ltd (formerly China Pioneer Pharma Holdings, HKEX: 1345)
research_notes: Board appointment reported by secondary source (itiger); check HKEX filing. Route via company secretary / HKEX-listed company IR.

name: Bao Shijin
profile: Bao Shijin (b. 1959), a senior economist, founded Jiangyin Jixin Machinery in 2003, which became Jiangsu Jixin Wind Energy (SINOJIT), a maker of large castings for wind turbines, listed in Shanghai. He chaired it from 2008 to April 2021 and then served as a director until late 2023.
interesting_fact: He was named an Excellent National Entrepreneur of the foundry industry (2010) and was a vice-chairman of the Jiangsu Renewable Energy Industry Association.
deep_cut_fact: He was a standing director of the China Foundry Association and in 2009 received the national 'Outstanding Entrepreneur of the Machinery Industry' award for 2007-08.
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Jiangsu SINOJIT Wind Energy Technology (SH:601218); no board seat listed after Dec 2023
research_notes: Hurun labels industry 'solar equipment' but the company makes wind-turbine castings. Strong fit for energy podcast. Current status after leaving the board not confirmed.

name: Qu Quanda
profile: Qu Quanda (屈全大), from Qujiagou village in Liulin county, is counted among Liulin's best-known coal bosses. He founded Hongsheng Energy (est. 2006), a private coal and coking group whose assets include the Liulin Hongsheng Jude coal mine, formed in 2009 Shanxi coal consolidation by merging nine smaller mines. Hurun listed him 2013-2016 under 'Hongsheng'.
interesting_fact: In July 2021 Hongsheng gave RMB 10m to Henan flood relief, the largest gift in a RMB 24m batch from Shanxi private firms. That October it gave RMB 5m more to flood-hit Xiaoyi in Shanxi.
deep_cut_fact: The group's Jude mine (柳林宏盛聚德煤业) was created under Shanxi's 2009 coal-mine consolidation order (晋煤重组办发[2009]33号) by merging the former Liulin Jucai coal mine and eight others, with Hongsheng as the lead company.
current_role: Chairman of Shanxi Hongsheng Energy Development & Investment Group (山西宏盛能源开发投资集团), Liulin county, Lüliang, Shanxi (registries: chairman, with controlling stakes via Shanxi Fulin Investment and Lüliang Hongsheng Coal & Coke)
research_notes: Hurun 'Hongsheng' = 山西宏盛能源 (Liulin), not Jincheng's Hongsheng construction (宏圣). The legal representative of the group is now Yang Guobing, with Qu listed as chairman. Registry data show consumption-restriction and court flags on the group; financial stress is possible. Unlisted; no published contact (the mine site hsjdmy.cn was unreachable from here).

name: Shu Cecheng
profile: Shu Cecheng (舒策城) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2012 to 2015 with about $330M from Wuzhou International, a Hong Kong-listed developer of specialised wholesale and commercial complexes in Chinese cities. His current role and the company's status were not verified in this session.
current_role: Listed as owner of Wuzhou International (commercial real estate) on the Hurun China list (2012-2015), presumably founder/chairman of Wuzhou International Holdings (HKEX: 1369), a Wuxi-based wholesale-market developer. Current role not verified.
research_notes: Off Hurun since 2015, and the company's current status is unknown. Verify via HKEXnews before outreach. Web-search budget was exhausted. Real estate, so a weak podcast fit.

name: Wang Zhiqin
profile: Wang Zhiqin (王致勤), born 1964, worked at Nanjing No. 2 Steel Plant and then traded on his own before founding Nanjing Jincao Garment Factory in 1996. Its upmarket womenswear brand V.GRASS became Vgrass Fashion, which listed in Shanghai in 2014 and was renamed Jinhong Fashion Group in 2019. He has been chairman and GM since 2010, re-elected in September 2025; Hurun co-lists Song Yanjun, the long-time design director.
interesting_fact: He started out as a steelworker: he spent 1986 to 1992 at Nanjing No. 2 Steel Plant before switching to fashion and building one of China's listed premium womenswear groups.
deep_cut_fact: V.GRASS was co-built with Song Yanjun, who left her job at the Nanjing Electric Power Instrument Factory (1980 to 1994) to become the design director of their small Jincao garment factory in 1996, a role she held through the IPO.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jinhong Fashion Group Co., Ltd. (formerly V.GRASS / Vgrass Fashion; SSE: 603518), Nanjing
research_notes: Web search quota ran out mid-lane; data comes from Sina Finance filings. The group also owns other brands (I could not verify the details here). Weak fit for the energy theme; the steel-plant-to-fashion founder story is the hook.

name: Song Yanjun
profile: Song Yanjun co-founded Nanjing Jincao Fashion in 2003 with Wang Zhiqin (chairman and GM), and it became the V·GRASS women's-wear group. Listed in Shanghai in Nov 2014 (37m shares at RMB 20.02), it was renamed Jinhong Fashion and now also owns Teenie Weenie and a Yunjin brocade line. She and Wang are joint actual controllers.
interesting_fact: The group grew from a single women's-wear label into an owner of the Teenie Weenie men's, women's and kids' brand plus Nanjing Yunjin brocade products.
deep_cut_fact: When the predecessor company was set up on 14 March 2003 with RMB 2m registered capital, she contributed RMB 570,000 (28.5%) alongside Wang Zhiqin's RMB 1.2m.
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (about 15.35%) of Jinhong Fashion Group (SSE: 603518, formerly V·GRASS / Weigenasi), Nanjing
research_notes: Not a listed executive in current filings; Wang Zhiqin (a former Nanjing No.2 Steel Works employee) is the public face. Route via the board secretary's office. Not a natural energy/data-centre fit.

name: Ji Defa
profile: Born 1951, automation engineer (Shandong University of Technology postgraduate, PKU EMBA). Founded Step Electric in Shanghai in 1995; it grew from elevator control systems into servo drives, inverters and industrial robots and listed in Shenzhen in Dec 2010. In 2025 the family transferred shares and delegated voting rights to Haier's Kaos Industrial Intelligence, which became controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Step Electric became a national robot-standards body member and vice-chair of the China Robot Industry Alliance, evolving from elevator controllers into one of China's domestic industrial-robot makers.
deep_cut_fact: From 1968 to 1992 he worked at the Yancheng Power Machinery Plant, a Lianyungang chemical-mining design institute and a Shanghai housing-equipment factory, then ran Pudong Shida Elevator Control's development department (1992-95) before founding Step. He was named a Shanghai Model Worker in 2007.
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Shanghai Step Electric (新时达, 002527.SZ); founding family remains a large shareholder after selling control to Haier's Kaos Industrial Intelligence in 2025
research_notes: Alive as of Feb 2025 when he signed the share-transfer agreement with Haier Kaos (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-06-26/1223981724.PDF). Company is now Haier-controlled, so IR is an indirect route. Robotics/automation angle is relevant.

name: Zhou Judong
profile: Zhou Judong built Xinjiang Haoyuan Natural Gas, a natural-gas distribution and CNG business in Xinjiang that listed in Shenzhen in 2012, and appeared on the Hurun China Rich List (2014-2018) together with Di Rong. He served as a director and was named the company's responsible person in its 2019 annual report.
current_role: Founder/controlling shareholder of Xinjiang Haoyuan Natural Gas (Shenzhen-listed); listed as head of the company in its 2019 annual report; current role unclear
research_notes: 2024 company disclosures (cninfo) report regulatory action over controlling-shareholder fund use and that his shares were auctioned by creditors; he is likely no longer a major holder. Low priority / not recommended for outreach.

name: Di Rong
profile: Di Rong (狄蓉) is the wife of Zhou Judong, founder and chairman of Xinjiang Haoyuan Natural Gas, an Aksu (Xinjiang) city-gas and CNG distributor listed in Shenzhen in 2012. She held 14.99% of Shengwei Industrial, the family vehicle that, with Zhou, controlled the company. current_role: Founder and actual controller of Hunan Corun New Energy (科力远, SSE: 600478); former chairman

It spans coal mining and trading in Tumed Right Banner and solar/silicon manufacturing through Baotou Shansheng New Energy, plus solar ventures in Shanghai, Hohhot and Golmud (Qinghai). current_role: Chairman, legal representative and ~90% owner of Inner Mongolia Shanlu Energy Group (内蒙古山路能源集团), Tumed Right Banner, Baotou (per business registries)
research_notes: Hurun 'Shanlu' = 内蒙古山路能源集团 (Baotou). Identity rests on business-registry data (aiqicha/qixin); no press profile, interview or official website found in Chinese/English searches. No published contact.

current_role: Co-owner (with husband Wang Xueqing 王学清, chairman) of Shandong Shouguang Luqing Petrochemical (山东寿光鲁清石化), Shouguang, Shandong

Business-registry aggregators also show her as a Luqing shareholder. Her own role is low-profile; no published personal contact. Approach via Luqing's corporate office in Shouguang. name: Cao Baohua
profile: Cao Baohua (曹宝华, born April 1955, from Jizhou, Hebei) is the entrepreneur behind Chunfeng Industrial Group, a privately held Hebei equipment-manufacturing group. He chairs it and serves as president. He has also been a long-serving deputy to China's National People's Congress for Hebei.
interesting_fact: He was elected a Hebei deputy to five consecutive National People's Congresses (the 9th through the 13th), which is unusually long for a private entrepreneur.

current_role: Chairman of the Board and President, Chunfeng Industrial Group (春风实业集团), Hebei

name: Fu Sheng

Led Qihoo 360's 360 Safeguard team (2005-08), founded Conew Image in 2009, and in 2010 merged it with Kingsoft Security (backed by Lei Jun) to form what became Cheetah Mobile, listed in New York in 2014. Since 2016 he has pivoted to AI via OrionStar, which builds service robots and LLMs and became a Cheetah subsidiary in December 2023.
interesting_fact: Before Cheetah he was the product lead behind 360 Safeguard (360安全卫士), the free security app that made Qihoo 360 one of China's biggest internet companies; he left in 2008 over differences with Zhou Hongyi, and the two publicly reconciled in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: His first brush with the internet was in 1999 as head of the e-commerce department at Xiamen computer maker Xoceco (厦华电脑), followed by enterprise full-text search work at Guoxin Base and a director role at 3721 (later bought by Yahoo China).
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Cheetah Mobile (NYSE: CMCM); Chairman, OrionStar (猎户星空) AI & robotics
public_contact: ir_email: IR@cmcm.com | press_email: cmpr@cmcm.com | official_website: https://www.cmcm.com/en/
research_notes: Highly public and media-friendly (frequent speaker and short-video creator on AI). Strong fit for an AI/compute angle via OrionStar. Name sometimes rendered 'Sheng Fu'.

Liu Ce has been chairman since October 2025.

current_role: Founder and co-actual controller (~14%) of Shanghai Lonyer Data Co. (formerly Shanghai Lonyer Fuels); no longer chairman

He controls two listed companies and founded the Zhongtian Love Charity Foundation.
interesting_fact: He was named one of China's Top Ten Charity Role Models and received the Guangcai Medal; his foundation backed a 'maternal and infant safety' programme for pregnant migrant workers.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Dongyang No. 2 Construction Company as a clerk in 1979. In 1987 he was sent to Shanghai to open up its market there, and reportedly turned that operation from loss to profit within a year.
current_role: Chairman and Manager, Zhongtian Holding Group (中天控股集团), Hangzhou/Dongyang, Zhejiang; actual controller of Zhongtian Services (SZSE: 002188) and Huarong Holdings (SSE: 600421)

name: Li Mantie
profile: Li Mantie (李漫铁, born 1968) is a radio engineer and senior engineer who founded Shenzhen Ledman Optoelectronic, an LED display maker now focused on COB-packaged Micro LED ultra-fine-pitch screens. He remains chairman and president and holds civic roles, including Guangdong CPPCC member, Nanshan District People's Congress deputy and SUSTech industry professor.
interesting_fact: He serves as a distinguished industry professor at Southern University of Science and Technology (SUSTech) and as vice-chairman of the display-application branch of the China Optics and Optoelectronics Manufacturers Association.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in radio technology at South China University of Technology's radio engineering department. His first job was as a clerk on the Huizhou municipal government's Radio Management Committee, before he ran Huizhou Yuexin Communications Development and later founded Ledman.
current_role: Chairman and President, Shenzhen Ledman Optoelectronic Co. (雷曼光电, SZSE: 300162)
public_contact: ir_email: ledman@ledman.cn (board secretary / securities office) | official_website: http://www.ledman.com
research_notes: An active founder-chairman, with Micro LED display tech as the hook. The best route is Ledman's board secretary office. Web search budget was exhausted, so the profile comes from the FY2025 annual report.

name: Liu Pingshan
profile: Liu Pingshan (刘平山, b. June 1955) is a former Fujian provincial official turned businessman who controls Pingtan Development, a Shenzhen-listed forestry, timber-products and trading group tied to the Pingtan Comprehensive Experimental Zone facing Taiwan. A Xiamen University graduate, he ran Fujian state import-export companies before taking control of the listed group, which he still chairs.
interesting_fact: Pingtan Development is a provincial-level 'leading enterprise' in Fujian agriculture and forestry, with ~30 subsidiaries spanning afforestation, timber processing, trade and development projects in the Pingtan zone opposite Taiwan.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a deputy division head in the general office of the Fujian Provincial People's Congress and then vice-mayor of Shishi city, before heading Fujian Zhongfu and Fujian Huamin import-export companies.
current_role: Chairman, Zhongfu Straits (Pingtan) Development Co. (平潭发展, SZSE: 000592); also chairman of Fujian Shantian Industrial Development and Fujian Huamin Import & Export
public_contact: ir_email: zhongfu@000592.com (board office; tel +86 591-87871990) | official_website: http://www.000592.com
research_notes: Ex-official with very low media profile; Chinese-language approach via board secretary's office. Forestry/carbon-sink angle could fit an energy show loosely.

name: Chen Dekang
profile: Chen Dekang (陈德康) founded Pinghu, Zhejiang-based Shapuaisi Pharmaceutical, best known for its bendazac-lysine eye drops, and took it public in Shanghai in 2014. He later ceded control to Lin Hongyuan/Lin Hongli (Shanghai Yanghe), who now run it as chairman, but he still holds about 10.8%.
interesting_fact: Even after giving up control, he remains the company's second-largest shareholder (10.81% as of Q3 2026), behind the new owners' Shanghai Yanghe Industrial (21.01%).
current_role: Founder and second-largest shareholder (10.81%) of Zhejiang Shapuaisi Pharmaceutical (莎普爱思, 603168.SH); not on current management
public_contact: ir_email: zjspas@zjspas.com (company IR; he is no longer management)
research_notes: Low priority for an energy podcast. Product-efficacy controversy around the eye drops (2017) should be avoided. Limited research because the web search budget was exhausted.

name: Bu Fansheng
profile: Major early shareholder of Guangzhou Hangxin Aviation Technology, an aviation maintenance (MRO) and airborne equipment company founded 1994. Sold stakes to Guangzhou Hengmao Venture Capital in 2021-22 and later reduced below 5%.
current_role: Shareholder (formerly 5%+ holder), Guangzhou Hangxin Aviation Technology Co., Ltd. (航新科技, SZSE: 300424)
research_notes: No current executive role found; may no longer be closely tied to the company.

name: Ke Zonggui
profile: Ke Zonggui (b. 1969), a Shenzhen University electronic-engineering graduate (1992), co-led Guangzhou-based cybersecurity firm Bluedon as vice chairman and president from 2009 to 2021. Bluedon has since been delisted.
interesting_fact: He authored the textbook 'Practical Computer Network Security Technology' and won a Ministry of Public Security science & technology award.
deep_cut_fact: He was a guest professor at Guangzhou City Construction College and earlier worked at Bank of China's Hong Kong computer software development centre in Shenzhen.
current_role: Co-founder and former vice chairman/president, Bluedon Information Security Technologies (formerly SZ:300297, now delisted); current role unknown
research_notes: Company delisted (蓝盾退); old board email no longer a reliable route. No current public channels found.

name: Ke Zongqing
profile: Ke Zongqing (柯宗庆) built Bluedon (蓝盾股份), a Guangzhou-based Chinese information-security company (firewalls, security management software), and listed it on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2012. He appeared on Hurun's China list in 2015-2017. Filings identify him and Ke Zonggui as controlling shareholders. The company left the exchange in 2023.
interesting_fact: Bluedon was one of the early domestic cybersecurity vendors on ChiNext, part of China's push for home-grown network-security products.
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Bluedon / Blue Shield Technology (蓝盾股份, ex-SZSE: 300297), a Guangzhou cybersecurity software company delisted in 2023
research_notes: The company was delisted in 2023 and SZSE filings describe court-ordered sales of the controlling shareholders' shares. Avoid this topic, and the profile may now be outdated. No published contact found. Web-search budget was exhausted before his current activity could be checked.

name: Liu Dehong
profile: Liu Dehong (刘德宏), born 1965, spent the 1990s at Liaoning Radio & TV Audio-Video Publishing House, rising from distribution manager to deputy president. He then chaired Beijing Baina Culture before running Hualu Baina from its 2002 founding. The TV-drama and variety producer listed on ChiNext in 2012; he was GM until 2019 and then chairman, before control passed to new owners (now Baination Pictures).
interesting_fact: He came to TV production from home-video publishing. As a distribution executive at a provincial audio-video publisher in the 1990s, he learned the content-distribution side before co-founding Hualu Baina, one of the first TV-drama producers to list on ChiNext.
deep_cut_fact: From 1990 to 2000 he worked at the Liaoning Radio & Television Audio-Video Publishing House (辽宁广播电视音像出版社), going from head of distribution to deputy president, before moving to Beijing to start the Baina business.
current_role: Co-founder and former Chairman/GM of Beijing Hualu Baina Film & TV (now Beijing Baination Pictures, SZSE: 300291); no longer on the board, and current role not public
research_notes: He no longer has a board role at Baination Pictures (chairs since 2023: Fang Gang, then Zhu Youyi), so company IR (bainqcdsh@infore.com) is not a route to him. I found no personal channels. Web search quota ran out mid-lane.

name: Ye Yingtao
profile: Ye Yingtao was a founding shareholder (12.75%) and, from 2008, general manager/CEO of Beijing mobile-game developer Ourpalm, which listed on ChiNext in May 2012 as an early 'mobile games stock'. He sold down (about RMB 230m in 2016) and left management around then; he is now listed as founder of the Xindong Jinding sports investment fund.
interesting_fact: Ourpalm's early revenue leaned heavily on China Mobile's handset game platforms: 44-61% of revenue in 2008-H1 2011 came via China Mobile's Baibaoxiang and G+ channels.
deep_cut_fact: Before games he earned a finance and accounting diploma through Renmin University's self-study exam programme, then worked in the overseas division of the China Aviation Settlement Center and as a systems engineer and wireless executive (incl. SK China).
current_role: Founder of Xindong Jinding sports fund (新动金鼎体育基金); former co-founder and CEO of Ourpalm (SZSE: 300315)
research_notes: No longer at Ourpalm (now no controlling shareholder). Share-sale coverage: https://finance.sina.cn/stock/ssgs/2016-08-04/detail-ifxutfpf1172689.d.html. No published contact for him or the sports fund found.

name: Tai Zhengbiao
profile: Born Oct 1964; Nanjing University MBA and Tsinghua EMBA. Founded Taier in Ma'anshan in 2001; it makes couplings and intelligent equipment for steel mills, plus laser, surface-engineering and powder-materials businesses, and listed in Shenzhen in Jan 2010 (he held 65% pre-IPO). He has stepped back to honorary chairman; a family member now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: Taier says its metallurgical equipment and services reach over a thousand steel production lines, and it has expanded laser technology into new-energy and semiconductor applications.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as a salesman at Dangtu County No.2 Machinery Manufacturing Co., then was deputy director of Ma'anshan Donghua Metallurgical Plant and GM of Hongda Metallurgical Machinery before founding Taier; he was named a Ma'anshan Model Worker in 2009.
current_role: Controlling shareholder and honorary chairman, Taier Heavy Industry (泰尔股份, 002347.SZ), Ma'anshan, Anhui
research_notes: Sensitive: placed under supervisory detention by Jianli city supervision commission in Apr 2025; measures eased in June 2025 and lifted per a June 2026 company announcement (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-06-09/1225356988.PDF). Not an ideal outreach target; do not reference.

Du Haili's exact role or shareholding could not be confirmed from sources found.

current_role: Reported major shareholder of TDG Holding / Tiantong (天通控股, SSE: 600330), Haining, Zhejiang (unconfirmed)

name: Huang Peijin
profile: Huang Peijin (黄培劲, b. 1963), a hybrid-rice seed-production expert and former Hunan seed-company executive, founded Hainan Shennong Dafeng (Grand Agriseeds) in 2000, contributing his hybrid-rice seed-production patent as capital, and took it public on ChiNext in 2011. He no longer appears among the company's directors or major shareholders.
interesting_fact: His 1992 invention, a method for ultra-high-yield hybrid rice seed production, won a WIPO Outstanding Young Inventor gold medal - the only WIPO top award in hybrid rice besides Yuan Longping's.
deep_cut_fact: He won the first-ever Yuan Longping Agricultural Science & Technology Award in 1998, proposed a Seed Law bill to the National People's Congress, and made a TV teaching series on high-yield hybrid seed production.
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controller of Hainan Shennong Dafeng Seed (now 神农种业, SZSE 300189); current role not found
public_contact: ir_email: sndf2010@126.com (company board office; he is no longer involved)
research_notes: Appears to have exited Shennong (company now controlled by others); no current contact route found. Web search budget exhausted, so current status/whereabouts not checked.

name: Peng Peng
profile: Peng Peng (彭朋, born around 1949) is a senior economist who took control of Guilin Guanglu Digital Measurement, a maker of digital measuring instruments. As chairman he turned it into Oriental Times Media, adding digital-TV operation and internet services. He held about 15% in 2015. In 2020–21 he tried to transfer control to Shandong Xingtan, then cancelled the deal and kept a 7.68% stake.
interesting_fact: Under him a precision-measuring-instrument maker (calipers, gauges) became a digital-TV network operator, with ventures in regional cable-TV operations and a Silk Road broadcasting affiliate.
current_role: Former chairman and controlling shareholder, Oriental Times Media (东方时代网络传媒, SZSE 002175; formerly Guilin Guanglu Digital Measurement); still a 7.68% shareholder as of 2021
research_notes: Shareholding and bio are from the company's 2015 annual report and Peng's April 2021 equity-change report (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2021-04-01/1209566174.PDF). The listed company is now distressed (*ST), and he no longer appears to hold a management role. He would be in his late 70s. Low priority; no public contact route found.

name: Zhao Kang
profile: Zhao Kang (赵康) co-founded Jinlihua Electric in Jinhua, Zhejiang in 2003 with Zhao Jian and 20 others; it makes toughened-glass disc suspension insulators for 10kV-1000kV AC/DC transmission lines and listed on ChiNext in 2010. Control later passed to Shanxi-based investors (chairman Han Chang'an since 2022), and Zhao Kang no longer appears among the top-10 shareholders in the 2025 report.
interesting_fact: Jinlihua's glass insulators are used on high-voltage up to 1000kV ultra-high-voltage lines and are sold mainly through State Grid and China Southern Grid tenders - relevant to the grid-buildout side of energy.
current_role: Former co-founder and major shareholder of Jinlihua Electric / 金利华电 (SZ300069); no longer a top-10 shareholder; current role unknown
research_notes: Appears to have exited; the company's published IR email (info@jlhdq.com) now represents the new owners, not him. No personal public presence found. Low-priority target.

name: Sun Yizheng
profile: Co-founded Sichuan Yimikang Refrigeration in 2002 with Zhang Wan (the Hurun entry's 'Zhang Yuan' is 张菀); they jointly control 20.7% of what is now Yimikang Technology Group, listed on ChiNext in 2011. The company makes precision cooling and thermal-management equipment for data centres and now sells full-lifecycle 'green digital infrastructure' and zero-carbon data-centre solutions.
interesting_fact: Yimikang bills itself as the first A-share-listed company in China's precision-environment/data-centre cooling industry, and now positions itself around zero-carbon data centres.
current_role: Co-founder and joint actual controller (with Zhang Wan) of Yimikang Technology Group (依米康, SZSE: 300249), Chengdu; ~5.3% direct holder
public_contact: ir_email: yimikang@ymk.com.cn (company / board-secretary contact) | official_website: http://www.ymk.com.cn
research_notes: STRONG podcast fit (data-centre cooling / green digital infrastructure). Co-founder Zhang Wan is the current chairman and the more visible face of the company - she may be the better guest. Sun no longer holds a listed management title per current disclosures.

current_role: Listed by Hurun (2017), with Wang Jianqing, as owners of Shenzhen Annil (安奈儿, 002875.SZ, children's apparel); current role not verified

name: Wang Jianqing
profile: Shenzhen entrepreneur who co-founded the Annil children's clothing shop in 1996 with her husband Cao Zhang and built it into a national mid-to-high-end kidswear brand; Annil listed in 2017 as the A-share market's first kidswear stock. She left the vice-chair/deputy GM roles in 2023 and in 2025 the couple sold control to Shenzhen Xinchuangyuan (actual controller Huang Tao).
interesting_fact: Annil, which she co-founded as a single shop in 1996, became the first children's-clothing company listed on China's A-share market (2017).
current_role: Co-founder, Shenzhen Annil Co. (SZSE: 002875); former vice chairman (to Jan 2023); no longer a controlling shareholder since Aug 2025
public_contact: ir_email: dongmiban@annil.com (Annil board office; note she no longer controls the company)
research_notes: Control change details in Annil 2025 annual report. Company route is now weak since she exited control; no personal channels found. Fit for consumer-brand entrepreneurship angle rather than energy.

name: Chen Qifeng
profile: Born December 1960; entered the tungsten-products trade in 1982 and set up Chaozhou Xianglu Tungsten in 1997, chairing it since 2001. Xianglu, listed in 2017, is integrated from mining through APT, tungsten oxide and powders to carbide and precision cemented-carbide parts. He chairs the presidium of the China Tungsten Industry Association.
interesting_fact: Xianglu covers the full tungsten chain, from ammonium paratungstate and tungsten oxide to tungsten and tungsten-carbide powders and hard-alloy parts. Tungsten is a strategic metal China dominates.
deep_cut_fact: He has worked in tungsten products since 1982, 15 years before founding Xianglu, and has received provincial and city science-and-technology awards. Chaozhou's government has honoured him as a 'philanthropist' and 'love ambassador'.
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Xianglu Tungsten Co., Ltd. (翔鹭钨业, SZSE: 002842), Chaozhou
research_notes: Good fit for a critical-minerals angle. Board secretary: Yang Feng. Family members sit on the board (not detailed here).

name: Chen Yuemeng
profile: Chen Yuemeng founded and chairs Zheshang Venture Capital, one of Zhejiang's leading private equity/VC managers, which has invested in about 100 projects with nearly 30 listed or acquired. He holds senior roles in Zhejiang's business community, including Standing Committee member of the Zhejiang CPPCC and first executive chairman of the Zhejiang Private Equity Association.
interesting_fact: Named one of Hurun China's Top 50 Best Venture Capitalists (2016) and Forbes China's Top 100 venture capital figures (2018); ZSVC has taken nearly 30 of ~100 portfolio companies to listing or M&A exit.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a VC, he graduated from Zhejiang University's Chinese language and literature department before taking an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.
current_role: Chairman and Founding Partner, Zheshang Venture Capital (ZSVC, 浙商创投, NEEQ 834089), Hangzhou
research_notes: invest@ is the published project-submission mailbox (only email on the site); company also runs a WeChat official account. Active in Zhejiang chambers of commerce - possible intro route.

name: Lai Chunlin
profile: Lai Chunlin (赖春临, b. 1977, Hubei) entered internet-cafe software in 2000 and in 2006 co-founded Shengtian (Century) Network, launching the 'Yiyou' (易游) internet-cafe management platform. She took it public on ChiNext in Dec 2015 - Hubei's first listed internet company - and has since expanded into game publishing and IP operations (Tianxi Huyu acquisitions 2019/2021). She owns ~24%.
interesting_fact: Shengtian was the first internet company from Hubei province to list (ChiNext, 2015); Lai was named one of the 'Optics Valley 30 innovators in 30 years'.
deep_cut_fact: Her company's roots are in China's internet cafes: in 2006 she launched 'Yiyou' (易游), a management platform for internet cafes; in 2023 she proposed esports hotels as offline entry points to the metaverse at a Wuhan developer summit.
current_role: Chairwoman and General Manager, Hubei Century Network Technology (盛天网络, SZSE: 300494), Wuhan; vice chair, Hubei Federation of Industry and Commerce
research_notes: Hurun's 'Shanda' refers to Shengtian Network (盛天网络), not Chen Tianqiao's Shanda. Active in Hubei business associations; donated RMB1m to Hubei Red Cross in 2020. Formal route via company board office.

name: Zhang Shaohuai
profile: Hurun China (2017) linked Zhang Shaohuai (张少怀), jointly with Wang Dan, to Luxin, a packaging-materials business. No verifiable public information about the person or the company was found with the tools available.
research_notes: Not researched in depth: the lane's web-search budget ran out. Needs manual follow-up; the company's Chinese name is unconfirmed.

name: Hu Xin
profile: Hu Xin (胡欣) appears on Hurun China 2017 jointly with Xu Na (徐纳) as holders of Hangzhou XZB Tech ('New Coordinate'). Founded in Hangzhou in 2002, XZB makes engine valve-train parts and cold-forged auto components (valve cotters, spring seats, hydraulic lash adjusters, roller rocker arms) and listed on the Shanghai main board on 9 Feb 2017. SSE records list Xu Na as the company's legal representative.
interesting_fact: XZB is a niche precision-parts maker: its catalogue centres on small valve-train components such as valve cotters and hydraulic lash adjusters, and it went from founding to an SSE main-board listing in 15 years.
current_role: Founding-family shareholder of Hangzhou XZB Tech (新坐标, SSE: 603040); exact current title not verified
research_notes: Low-profile auto-parts founder family. His current board role was not confirmed (search budget exhausted). The company website appears compromised by spam links, so use the SSE-registered IR email (stock@xzbco.com) instead.

name: Yang Xiaoming
profile: Yang Xiaoming (杨小明), from Guanlin in Yixing, Jiangsu (a major Chinese cable-making cluster), was chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller of Yuancheng Cable when it listed in Shenzhen around 2012. He later handed the chair to Yu Guoping, lost part of his stake through a court-ordered execution in 2020 and sold down further in 2021-22.
interesting_fact: Yuancheng Cable is based in Guanlin town, Yixing, one of China's densest wire-and-cable manufacturing clusters.
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Yuancheng Cable (远程电缆 / 远程股份, SZSE: 002692), Yixing, Jiangsu; now a reduced minority shareholder (approx. 6% in 2022)
research_notes: No longer runs the company, which has carried an ST (risk-warning) tag; stake reductions involved judicial enforcement. Low suitability for outreach; current activities unknown. Common name - identity tied via SZSE filings.

name: Li Wenming
profile: Hurun China 2019 listed Li Wenming (李文明) with about $330m from 'Zhongneng Haolong', a real estate, manufacturing and investment group. I couldn't find any sourced information on this company or its chairman. The name is very common: there is an unrelated Southeast University energy professor named Li Wenming, and it doesn't match Zhongneng Holdings (0228.HK).
current_role: Unknown. Listed by Hurun China (2019 only) with 'Zhongneng Haolong' (real estate, manufacturing, investment)
research_notes: Identity unresolved and the name is very common. Don't conflate him with Professor Li Wenming (Southeast University energy school) or with Zhongneng Holdings (HK 0228). He appeared on Hurun only once (2019).

name: Song Xuesong
profile: Co-founder of C Media Limited, which he chaired 2012-2018 before it reverse-merged into Luokung. He became Luokung's chairman and CEO in August 2018, building it into a spatial-temporal big-data firm offering location-based services, HD maps for autonomous driving (via the 2021 eMapgo acquisition) and satellite remote-sensing data.
interesting_fact: Luokung raised US$120m in early 2021 and bought eMapgo, one of China's licensed HD-map makers for self-driving cars. Song pitched it as China's 'most powerful remote sensing data engine'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Luokung he co-founded C Media Limited and served as its chairman and CEO from 2012 until it merged into Luokung in 2018.
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Luokung Technology Corp. (Nasdaq: LKCO, Beijing) per latest available filings (2021-2023); current status not verified
research_notes: Data/geospatial and smart-transport angle fits a data-center podcast. Luokung's market value and listing status have declined since 2022; check current SEC/Nasdaq status before outreach. Contact via the company's IR listed in its SEC 20-F.

profile: Appears once on the Hurun China Rich List (2016) with an IT-sector fortune attributed to a company romanised as 'Paixin'. Chinese and English searches found no company or public record matching 孙秀荣 and Paixin, so identity and current role could not be verified.
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China (2016) with wealth from 'Paixin' (IT)

name: Lin Rujie
profile: Lin Rujie (林汝捷, b. 1968) founded Changle Snowman Refrigeration Equipment in Fujian in March 2000; it is now Snowman Group, listed in Shenzhen. It makes ice-making systems and industrial refrigeration compressors and has expanded into industrial heat pumps, LNG/oil-and-gas services and hydrogen-energy equipment, including fuel-cell compressors via a Japanese hydrogen-power affiliate.
interesting_fact: Snowman's compressors and ice systems span cold-chain, concrete cooling for dams, mine cooling, energy-storage peak shaving, ice-sports venues and hydrogen equipment, and it runs a dedicated hydrogen unit (Fujian Snowman Hydrogen Technology).
deep_cut_fact: After starting a trading company straight out of high school in 1988, he spent most of the 1990s in Japan, studying at a Tokyo language school and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries' refrigeration-technology institute (1993), then working as a refrigeration engineer at Takagi Sangyo (1994-97) before returning to found Snowman.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Fujian Snowman Group (雪人集团, SZSE: 002639); Vice President, Fujian Refrigeration Society
research_notes: Strong energy angle (hydrogen compressors, heat pumps, LNG services). Probably speaks Japanese. Route via the Snowman board office email.

name: Xiang Bin
profile: Xiang Bin (向彬, b. 1969, Hong Kong resident) has chaired Guangzhou Well Lead Medical since 2011 and is its actual controller via controlling shareholder Gaobo Investment. The Panyu, Guangzhou-based company makes medical consumables, including anaesthesia-related devices, and has been recognised as a manufacturing 'single champion' product enterprise.
interesting_fact: Well Lead has been named a national manufacturing 'single champion' product enterprise and a 'hidden champion', per its company profile.
deep_cut_fact: Before building a medical-device business he studied mathematics, earning his bachelor's degree from Lanzhou University; he later took an EMBA at CEIBS.
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Guangzhou Well Lead Medical Co. (维力医疗, 603309.SH)
public_contact: ir_email: chenmeiling@welllead.com.cn (company contact email as listed) | official_website: http://www.welllead.com.cn

profile: Xiao Zhihong (b. 1954) entered book distribution in 1983, set up Hunan Tianhong Investment in 2002 and in 2003 founded Hunan Tianzhou Science & Education Culture, now Tangel Culture, an educational publishing and culture company listed in 2010. He returned as chairman in 2024, re-elected in 2026.
interesting_fact: He founded Tangel in 2003 and returned as chairman in March 2024 after stepping back in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He holds the professional title 'senior book distributor' (高级发行员), having started in book distribution in 1983, two decades before founding Tangel.
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Tangel Culture Co., Ltd. (SZ:300148), Changsha; chairman of Hunan Jiachuang and Mingyuan Investment
research_notes: Publishing veteran; route via board secretary email.

name: Luo Yun
profile: Luo Yun (罗云) co-founded Biostime in Guangzhou in 1999 with Luo Fei, who is H&H's chairman and CEO. The company began with children's probiotics, then grew into infant formula and nutrition, and listed in Hong Kong in 2010. After buying 83% of Australia's Swisse Wellness in 2015 for A$1.45B it renamed itself H&H in 2017. Today it is a global nutrition group with brands including Swisse, Biostime and Good Goût.
interesting_fact: The 2015 Swisse purchase (A$1.45B for 83%) turned a Guangzhou infant-probiotics firm into the owner of one of Australia's best-known vitamin brands. It was among the largest Chinese takeovers of an Australian consumer brand.
deep_cut_fact: In 2013 Biostime took a 20% stake in Isigny Sainte Mère, a historic French Normandy dairy producer, to secure infant-formula supply. This was years before the Swisse deal.
current_role: Co-founder of Health and Happiness (H&H) International Holdings (HKEX: 1112), formerly Biostime. His current board role is not verified.
public_contact: office_email: info.group@hh.global (H&H group enquiries; the form routes investor/media enquiries) | contact_form: https://www.hh.global/contact-us | official_website: https://www.hh.global/
research_notes: Co-founder Luo Fei is the public face of H&H; Luo Yun keeps a low profile. Healthcare/consumer, so a weak fit for an energy podcast but a good entrepreneurship story. Web-search budget ran out, so his current status was not re-verified.

name: Liu Chenglin
profile: Hurun's China list gives Liu Chenglin (刘丞霖, b. 1964, Liaoning, based in Hong Kong) under 蒙古能源 (MEC), with coal and air-charter interests. Mongolia Energy Corp (HKEX:276) is controlled by chairman Lo Lin Shing through Golden Infinity, and Liu does not appear among its directors or substantial shareholders. His actual business is unidentified.
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2011-2021) against 'MEC' (蒙古能源 / Mongolia Energy Corp, Hong Kong; coal, air charter); not found in that company's filings
research_notes: Checked MEC's 2019 annual report (https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2019/0712/ltn20190712519_c.pdf) and its 2025 filings: no 劉丞霖. Searches for 刘丞霖 董事长 and English variants found nothing. Hurun may have mislabelled the company. Do not assume he is linked to MEC. Low priority.

name: Cao Yonggui
profile: Cao Yonggui founded Chenzhou, Hunan-based Jingui Silver, a silver smelter and refiner that listed in Shenzhen and made him a Hurun list member (2014-2019). The company ran into a debt crisis and the Chenzhou court put it through restructuring in Nov-Dec 2020. Control passed to a Chenzhou state investment vehicle, his stake was diluted, and the company was renamed Hunan Silver.
interesting_fact: After the 2020 court-led restructuring, the Chenzhou municipal state investment group's industrial arm replaced him as controlling shareholder and the company was renamed Hunan Silver.
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Jingui Silver Industry (SZSE: 002716, now Hunan Silver Co.); no longer in control since the 2020 restructuring
research_notes: Not recommended for outreach. The CSRC opened an information-disclosure investigation into the company and him in July 2020 and closed the case in Dec 2021 (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202112231536200486_1.pdf). Wealth figure is likely obsolete; no current public role found.

name: Xu Li
profile: Spouse of Jingui Silver founder Cao Yonggui and a pre-IPO shareholder (~3.2%) of Jingui, the Chenzhou, Hunan silver smelter that listed in Shenzhen in Jan 2014 as 'China's first silver stock'. The family wealth was tied to Jingui; after its financial difficulties and a 2024 restructuring, Hunan Mineral Resources Group became controlling shareholder and the company was renamed Hunan Silver.
interesting_fact: Jingui Silver was the only A-share company with silver as its core business, with about 2,000 tonnes/year of silver capacity, making Chenzhou one of China's main silver production and export bases.
current_role: Former co-owner (with husband Cao Yonggui) of Chenzhou Jingui Silver Industry (002716.SZ); company now state-owned 'Hunan Silver' after 2024 restructuring - no current role found
research_notes: Identity per Jingui's 2014 prospectus, which names Xu Li as Cao Yonggui's spouse and a 36-month lock-up shareholder (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2014-01-16/63490107.PDF). Sensitive: Jingui later had controlling-shareholder fund-occupation problems and was restructured; family no longer involved. Not a recommended target; no contact.

name: Ren Huaican
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2006-2015) for 'NorthStar', a diversified group spanning real estate, restaurants and manufacturing. The group's Chinese name and his current role could not be confirmed during this run.
current_role: Linked by Hurun to NorthStar (real estate, restaurants, manufacturing); not verified

name: Wu Qianghua
profile: Wu Qianghua, a GIS and surveying engineer, joined Beijing eGOVA in 2003 (two years after its founding), served as chairman and president, and remains chairman. eGOVA, listed on ChiNext in 2010, sells smart-city software for urban operations management, 'urban lifeline' infrastructure monitoring and municipal surveys, and says it serves 31 provinces and 500+ cities.
interesting_fact: eGOVA led development of Beijing's Dongcheng District grid-based urban management information system, the model for China's 'grid management' approach to running cities.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Beijing Forestry University in 1994 (postgraduate), is a professor-level senior engineer in GIS and surveying, and spent 1994-2002 as an R&D engineer and then technical department manager at Beijing Construction Electronic Information Engineering Co. before joining eGOVA.
current_role: Chairman, Beijing eGOVA Co., Ltd. (数字政通, SZSE: 300075)
public_contact: office_email: egova@egova.com.cn (company general email) | contact_form: https://www.egova.com.cn/about/contact | official_website: https://www.egova.com.cn (company)
research_notes: Board secretary is Qiu Luming (per company site); investor Q&A via cninfo IR platform for 300075. Smart-city / urban infrastructure angle fits data-center/energy podcast.

name: Xie Haiyu
profile: Hurun China (2014-2015) listed Xie Haiyu (谢海榆) under 'Isea', real estate. Exchange filings name a Xie Haiyu alongside Guangdong Lihai Group (广东利海集团), a Guangzhou property developer, in a 2013 loan agreement, suggesting he is linked to Lihai; the 'Isea' link is unconfirmed.
research_notes: Identity only partly established (possible Lihai Group link, via Yuexiu Financial 2016 annual report, http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2017-03-23/1203186579.PDF, which concerns a loan dispute - do not use in outreach). Web-search budget exhausted; needs a fresh check.

name: Yang Jianzhong
profile: Born 1965, Yang Jianzhong has run the family rigging business in Xushui, Hebei since 1992, building Juli Group and its SZSE-listed unit Juli Sling (wire-rope slings, rigging and hoisting gear, incl. for energy projects). He chaired Juli Sling for its first six board terms; brother Yang Jianguo has chaired it since ~2022. Hurun listed the family wealth jointly.
interesting_fact: He served as a deputy to China's 11th and 12th National People's Congress and has been named a National Model Worker and Hebei Outstanding Entrepreneur.
deep_cut_fact: His official honours include serving as a 'Baoding Image Ambassador' (保定形象大使) for his home city, alongside the 5th Hebei Province Entrepreneur award; he holds a master's degree and the professional title of senior business manager (高级经营师).
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and director-level family principal of Juli Sling Co. (巨力索具, SZSE: 002342) / Juli Group, Xushui, Baoding, Hebei; chaired the listed company through its 1st-6th boards (to ~2022)
research_notes: IR email is the board secretary's as published in Dec 2019; may be stale, check latest cninfo filings. Per mid-2026 press, Juli Sling disclosed a CSRC investigation (May 2026) and Juli Group had management changes; tread carefully and confirm his current title. Hurun pairs him with 'Yang Xiang'.

Sinovel's pre-IPO shareholders included many investment vehicles (Tianhua Zhongtai, Xizang Xinmeng, Xinneng Huaqi, Fudingshun, Ruihua Fengneng and others). current_role: Listed by Hurun (2011-2015) as a Sinovel Wind Group (华锐风电) shareholder; holding vehicle and current role unverified
research_notes: Checked the Sinovel IPO prospectus summary (https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2010-12/24/A21/AGG0211224C.pdf); he is not named. Searches for 程志山+华锐风电/风电/投资 also found nothing. SSE filings are bot-blocked from here. Sinovel had no actual controller; Dalian state assets took control in 2024. Low priority.

name: Lyu Xiaoyi
profile: Lyu Xiaoyi (吕晓义) co-founded Shenzhen Hifuture Electric in July 1999. It made power transmission, distribution and control equipment and listed in Shenzhen in 2007. He chaired the company until January 2013 and was a controlling shareholder until June 2015, after which he sold down. Control later passed to other investors and, from 2021, to a Chongqing state-owned entity.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Hifuture branched from switchgear into advanced materials and energy storage, with subsidiaries working on polyimide, nanofibre battery separators and supercapacitors for energy storage and EVs.
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman, Shenzhen Hifuture Electric (深圳惠程, SZSE 002168); no current role found
research_notes: 'Hifuture' = Shenzhen Hifuture (惠程), not Qingdao Hifuture/Hyunion (海立美达). Founding and control history is from Hifuture's 2021 annual report (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2022-04-30/1213257917.PDF). He has had no role at the company since 2015, so its contacts are not a route to him. Low public profile; search budget ran out before I could check his current status.

name: He Ping
profile: He Ping (何平, b. 1965) holds about 41% of Hangzhou Weiguang Electronic, which he built from the Hangzhou Weiguang Electronic Equipment Factory into a Shenzhen-listed maker of refrigeration motors and fans and servo motors. Its EC fans are used in HVAC, heat pumps, energy storage and data centres; he also runs its venture arm and Thai subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Weiguang's refrigeration motors and fans are sold into energy storage and data-centre cooling, and the company has set up a manufacturing subsidiary in Thailand - a direct link to the podcast's energy/data-centre theme.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he was vice principal of the Zhejiang Electronics Industry School, starting work in 1986, then became director of the Hangzhou Weiguang Electronic Equipment Factory; several of the company's founding team were colleagues from that school.
current_role: Chairman, Hangzhou Weiguang Electronic / 微光股份 (SZ002801)
research_notes: Good fit for the data-centre angle (EC fans for DC cooling). Also a Linping District people's congress deputy. Route via the board secretary's office.

interesting_fact: SPG Land listed on the HKEX main board in October 2006 with her as president, before Greenland bought control for HK$2.996bn in 2013.
current_role: Former president, SPG Land (Holdings) (HKEX: 0337, now Greenland Hong Kong); current role not found

name: Wu Changjiang
profile: Founder of NVC Lighting (雷士照明), established in late 1998 and listed in Hong Kong in 2010, once among China's largest lighting makers. After boardroom fights with investors he was voted off the board in August 2014 and was detained by Huizhou police in late 2014/early 2015 on suspected misappropriation of company funds. NVC sold 70% of its China business to KKR in 2019.
interesting_fact: NVC Lighting, founded in late 1998, sold 70% of its China lighting business to a KKR fund in 2019 for RMB 5.56bn.
current_role: None known; former founder/chairman/CEO of NVC Lighting (removed from board 2014)
research_notes: Not a suitable outreach target: arrested 2014-15 on misappropriation charges (https://www.ledinside.com/news/2015/1/police_file_for_former_nvc_lighting_chairman_detainment); widely reported later conviction not verified here. No current role or public contact found.

name: Yang Peng
profile: Yang Peng (杨鹏) founded Rundong, a Xuzhou-origin auto dealership group that sold luxury and mass-market brands (Ferrari, Maserati, BMW, Land Rover, Audi and others) across Jiangsu, Shandong, Zhejiang and Shanghai. It listed in Hong Kong, at one point as China Greenland Rundong Auto Group. From 2019-2020 the group shrank sharply as it closed dealerships.
interesting_fact: His dealership network included supercar franchises such as Ferrari and Maserati, and the group was renamed from 'China Greenland Rundong Auto' to China Rundong Auto Group.

name: Zhao Yuanhong
profile: Hurun China 2011 listed Zhao Yuanhong (赵元鸿) as holding wealth from NavInfo, the Beijing digital-map and navigation-data company that listed on the Shenzhen exchange on 18 May 2010. He has not been listed since, and no source retrieved here confirms his role. He may have been a pre-IPO shareholder.
interesting_fact: NavInfo, which listed in Shenzhen in May 2010, is one of China's main licensed digital-map and navigation-data providers. Its map data has gained importance for autonomous driving.
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China 2011 against NavInfo (四维图新, SZSE: 002405)
