name: Ren Shuliang
profile: Ren Shuliang (任书良), known internationally as Dr. Sherman Jen, founded the first Maple Leaf International School in Dalian in 1995, pioneering a dual-diploma model that pairs the British Columbia (Canada) curriculum with Chinese education. Maple Leaf grew into a large network of bilingual K-12 schools and preschools in China and Southeast Asia and listed in Hong Kong in 2014; he remains chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Maple Leaf schools teach the British Columbia provincial curriculum, so graduates earn a BC Dogwood diploma alongside Chinese credentials; by October 2020 the group operated 114 schools.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 he personally gave C$5 million to Thompson Rivers University in Kamloops, BC, the largest private donation in its history, funding a high-fidelity simulation centre, an instrumentation lab, a research innovation fund and scholarships.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, China Maple Leaf Educational Systems (HKEX: 1317) (per Aug 2025 board list)
public_contact: ir_email: ir@mapleleaf.net.cn | office_email: info@mapleleafschools.com | official_website: https://www.mapleleafschools.com
research_notes: Goes by 'Sherman Jen' in English (Shu Liang Sherman Jen in HKEX filings); strong Canadian (BC) ties - Canadian universities (TRU, Royal Roads) are a warm angle. IR email from 2019 annual report, may be dated; info@ is the schools' general inbox.

name: Zhu Fengxue
profile: Zhu Fengxue is, with chairman Li Chundi, a controlling shareholder of ZPEC, a Shanghai private oil and gas group founded in 2003 and backed early by Sequoia. ZPEC grew from drilling contractor and rig maker into upstream production, working in Iraq, Pakistan and its own Tenge oilfield in Kazakhstan. He has been selling down shares since late 2025.
interesting_fact: ZPEC, a private Chinese driller, won a $526.6M Iraqi government contract to drill 66 production wells at the giant West Qurna 2 oilfield, and in 2019 entered Kazakhstan to develop its own Tenge oilfield.
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder, ZPEC - Zhongman Petroleum and Natural Gas Group (603619.SH), Shanghai
public_contact: office_email: office@zpec.com (ZPEC administration dept.) | official_website: https://www.zpec.com
research_notes: Almost no personal public profile: no interviews or bio found, appears only in shareholder filings (e.g. https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2024-08-16/1220882095.PDF). Chairman Li Chundi is the company's public face. Company contact is the only route.

name: Yin Hongwei
profile: Yin Hongwei (born 1965) built Lingnan Landscape, later Lingnan Eco & Culture-Tourism, from a Dongguan landscaping business into a Shenzhen-listed group spanning ecological construction, water management and cultural tourism. He chaired the company and the Dongguan Private Investment Group. Control has since passed to a Dongguan/Zhongshan state-backed holder, and in 2026 court auctions cut his stake below 5%.
interesting_fact: He was one of Dongguan's best-known private entrepreneurs, serving as chairman of Dongguan Private Investment Group and as second president of the World Federation of Dongguan Merchants (世界莞商联合会).
deep_cut_fact: He is a certified senior environmental artist (高级环境艺术师) by profession. He graduated from Huizhou University and later completed an EMBA in economics at Peking University, which reflects the design roots of a landscaping firm that grew into eco-tourism.
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Lingnan Eco & Culture-Tourism (*ST岭南, 002717.SZ), Dongguan; now a sub-5% shareholder
research_notes: Sensitive. In June 2026 the CSRC Guangdong bureau issued a pre-penalty notice to him (a reported RMB 14m fine and 10-year market ban) over fund-occupation disclosures. His shares were court-auctioned in 2026, and the company got a 2025 audit disclaimer. Not a good outreach candidate now. I listed no company contact because he no longer controls the company.

name: Chen Qinzhong
profile: Born 1977, he has run Acetron since its start as Fuzhou Acetron Optoelectronic Materials in 2002. It makes PVD thin-film coating materials (sputtering targets and evaporation materials) for flat-panel displays, optics and semiconductors. He took it public on ChiNext in 2017 and is a co-controlling shareholder (about 31.6% direct).
interesting_fact: Acetron makes sputtering targets, the high-purity metal and ceramic sources used to deposit thin films in display panels and chips, a niche long dominated by Japanese and US suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: He became executive director and general manager of Fuzhou Acetron Optoelectronic Materials in October 2002, aged about 25. The group also has a Taiwan arm (台湾阿石创新材料), which he chairs.
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Fujian Acetron New Materials (阿石创, SZ: 300706), Fuzhou
research_notes: Hurun 'membrane material' means thin-film/PVD coating materials. Semiconductor/display materials supply chain fits a tech podcast. Wealth shared with Chen Xiumei (co-controller). IR email is the securities-affairs contact from the 2025 annual report.

name: Chen Xiumei
profile: Together with her husband Chen Qinzhong (chairman/GM), she is a controlling shareholder of Fujian Acetron New Materials, a ChiNext-listed (2017) maker of PVD sputtering targets and evaporation materials used to coat flat-panel displays, glass, optics and solar cells. She held about 11.5m shares as of Q1 2026; the founders sold part of their stake to a private fund in 2026.
interesting_fact: Acetron makes the sputtering targets used to deposit nanometre-thin films on display panels and solar cells, a niche long dominated by Japanese and US suppliers; it exports to Japan, the US, Germany and Korea.
current_role: Co-actual controller and shareholder of Fujian Acetron New Materials (阿石创, 300706.SZ), Fuzhou
research_notes: Hurun spells co-owner 'Chen Qinzhong'; filings use 陈钦忠. Public face is Chen Qinzhong. Solar/display coatings link to the energy theme. Route via securities-affairs IR email.

name: Wang Huiwu
profile: Wang Huiwu (汪辉武, b. ~1973) built Hope Education, one of China's largest private higher-education groups (vocational colleges and universities, mainly in Sichuan), listed in Hong Kong in 2018 and renamed XJ International Holdings in 2024. He controls it via Maysunshine and Hope Education Investment (~45%). He was also actual controller of Shenzhen-listed Jifeng Technology until a 2025 control transfer.
interesting_fact: He began as an educator: from 1999 to 2007 he was principal of Chengdu Mayflower Computer Science Professional College, and he chairs the council of Sichuan Hope Automotive Technical College.
deep_cut_fact: Already a college group CEO, he completed a bachelor's in education at Sichuan Normal University in 2013 and then a master's in teaching and educational theory from Vitebsk State University in Belarus in 2022.
current_role: Executive Director, CEO and President, XJ International Holdings (formerly Hope Education Group, HKEX: 1765)
research_notes: Sensitive: XJ International has had going-concern audit issues and an undersubscribed 2025 rights issue, so avoid finances in outreach. Linked to the Tequ group (Tequ Education is a connected party). Route via ir@hopeedu.com, which the annual report gives for shareholder communications with the board.

name: Fan Min
profile: Fan Min (范敏) co-founded Ctrip (now Trip.com Group) in 1999 with James Liang, Neil Shen and Ji Qi, and served over the years as its executive vice president, CEO and later president and director. He resigned as director and president effective 25 February 2026. He has also been chairman and CEO of cruise operator Skysea (天海邮轮).
interesting_fact: He is one of the four 1999 co-founders of Ctrip, China's largest online travel company, and stayed in senior management for about 27 years until early 2026.
deep_cut_fact: A Shanghai Jiao Tong University graduate, he came from the hotel business: he was an assistant in the general manager's office at Shanghai New Asia Group and then deputy GM of Shanghai New Asia (Group) Hotel Management Co. before co-founding Ctrip.
current_role: Co-founder of Trip.com Group (Ctrip); stepped down as director and president effective 25 Feb 2026; current role not found
research_notes: Recently left Trip.com board (Feb 2026), so company IR is an indirect route. Skysea title is from an undated profile and may be outdated. IR email seen in 2026 press-release contact blocks via search (site blocks direct fetch).

name: Shao Xue
profile: Shao Xue is the controlling shareholder and actual controller of Thunisoft, a Beijing software firm known for court and legal-sector IT, e-government and education systems, which he previously led as chairman and general manager. Guo Ying has chaired the company since May 2022; Thunisoft's Q1 2026 report still lists Shao as controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Thunisoft, which he controls, is a major supplier of digital systems to China's courts and procuratorates, and has built AI tools for legal work.
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Beijing Thunisoft (华宇软件, SZSE: 300271); no longer chairman
research_notes: Caution: Thunisoft's 2024 annual report notes a 2023 court judgment against the company and Shao Xue, after which he no longer holds the chair. Treat as sensitive; low outreach suitability.

name: Wen Muheng

current_role: Major individual shareholder, Wens Foodstuff Group (top-10 shareholder, 1.90% at end-2023); no executive role found

profile: Guan Lianping founded BONC, a Beijing big-data and software company whose largest customers are telecom operators, followed by finance, industry and government. He has served as both chairman and general manager, chaired the board as of March 2025, and is co-controlling shareholder with Huo Weiping.

profile: Guangxi pharma-distribution entrepreneur (b. profile: Wang Mingfeng (王明峰, b. c.1958) is the eldest of three brothers from Xiwang village, Zouping, Shandong, who built Shandong Sanxing Group from a roadside repair shop into China's largest edible corn-oil maker (brand Changshouhua 长寿花), plus machinery and aluminium businesses. Changshouhua listed in 2008-09 (Euronext, then HKEX) and was taken private in 2020; it has since prepared for an A-share IPO.
interesting_fact: The group's name comes from the brothers' childhood nicknames: their father gave all three a nickname containing 'xing' (star), hence 'Sanxing' (three stars). Their village, Xiwang, also produced rival corn-oil maker Xiwang Group.
deep_cut_fact: In 1981 he boldly borrowed 600 yuan from the local cooperative to open a roadside farm-machinery repair stand; repairing oil presses there led the brothers to spot unused corn germ as a raw material for corn oil. He also holds a 1983 business-administration degree from Hebei Radio & TV University.

His younger brother Wu Rongzhao became CEO in 2007; Wu Rongguang moved to chairman and then behind the scenes, running Hongxing Erke (Xiamen) Investment, which focuses on health-sector investments.
interesting_fact: ERKE went viral in July 2021 after pledging 50 million yuan in goods and cash for Henan flood relief despite thin profits, triggering a nationwide 'buy ERKE' wave that emptied its livestreams and stores.
deep_cut_fact: The brand was born out of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: as export orders to Jinjiang shoe factories collapsed, Wu converted his father's OEM shoe business into an own-brand company, surviving an early cash crunch.
current_role: Founder and Chairman (behind the scenes) of Hongxing Erke Group (ERKE sportswear), Quanzhou/Xiamen, China
research_notes: Very low public profile; brother Wu Rongzhao is the public face of ERKE. Best route is via Hongxing Erke corporate PR (Xiamen). Sources are Chinese-language.

Jutal builds offshore platforms, process modules, FPSO modules and offshore-wind jackets at yards in Zhuhai, Penglai, Shenzhen, Dalian and Tianjin for clients like ExxonMobil, Chevron, SBM Offshore and CNOOC.

name: Hu Jirong
profile: Co-founded Xingyue with his brother Hu Jishen in 1989 as a small aluminium-ingot workshop in Gushan, Yongkang. It grew into a group of more than 10 companies making motorcycle engines, security doors, tools, carpets and appliances. Under his leadership it has moved into agricultural machinery, pharmaceuticals and silk-based regenerative-medicine devices, and the group reports assets above RMB 8bn.
interesting_fact: In 1996 Xingyue produced China's first GY6-125 scooter engine, and its engines went on to power more than 500 Chinese motorcycle makers. The same year it formed a joint venture with an ordnance-industry plant in Luoyang, which the company calls the first such tie-up between a military enterprise and a private firm in China.
deep_cut_fact: Xingyue started on 6 August 1989 with RMB 750,000 and 12 workers in a 100 m2 workshop. Its first breakthrough came in 1993 with the 147FM motorcycle cylinder head, which won gold at the 1995 China high-tech new products expo. Hu Jirong was also a deputy to the 10th National People's Congress and is honorary principal of Gushan Primary School.
current_role: President (总裁), Xingyue Group Co., Ltd. (星月集团), Yongkang, Zhejiang
research_notes: Chinese-language outreach advised. The group publishes office phone lines but no group-level press email (subsidiary sales emails only). His 'President's message' is at http://www.xingyue.com/president.html.

profile: Beijing robotics engineer (PhD Tsinghua University, 2009) who was a postdoc and associate researcher in Tsinghua's computer science department before co-founding warehouse-robot maker Geek+ with CEO Zheng Yong in February 2015. Geek+ builds autonomous mobile robots for logistics and listed in Hong Kong in 2025; he leads its technology and R&D.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Geek+ he was a postdoctoral researcher and associate researcher in Tsinghua University's Department of Computer Science and Technology.
deep_cut_fact: Recognised as a professor-level senior engineer by Beijing's senior professional qualification committee (May 2019) and receives a special government allowance from China's State Council (since June 2024); also named an Outstanding Young Member of the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing.
current_role: Co-founder, executive Director, CTO and Vice President, Geek+ (Geekplus Technology, HKEX-listed)
research_notes: Chinese-language outreach likely more effective; company IR/PR are the published routes. Li Hongbo is a common name - this is the Geek+ CTO (李洪波).

name: Li Xuelin
profile: Li Xuelin (李学林) founded Hefu Laomian in 2012. The premium Chinese noodle chain is known for its 'noodles in a study room' store concept and central-kitchen supply chain. It raised more than RMB1.6B in six rounds from 2016 to 2022 and reached roughly $1B valuation. Since late 2023 it has pursued expansion through franchising/joint operation, lower-tier cities and overseas markets.
interesting_fact: Before restaurants he ran a leading mobile-phone retailer in Jiangsu. He says he has 'led troops' for over 20 years across phone retail and restaurant chains.
deep_cut_fact: He has said China's restaurant industry has produced no giants 'not because of too few categories or projects, but because of missing systems and core capabilities', which is why Hefu built its own supply chain.
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Hefu Laomian (和府捞面) noodle restaurant chain
research_notes: Based in mainland China and media-light. Chinese-language outreach through Hefu Laomian corporate channels is likely the best route. I found no published contact email.

name: Tian Dihong
profile: Tian Dihong (田第鸿) cofounded Shenzhen Intellifusion (Intellif), an AI vision and AI-inference chip company, with Chen Ning in August 2014, holding 30% at founding. He later left the board for personal reasons and sold part of his stake in 2019; his company NaitMind, Inc. provided technical consulting to Intellif. Intellif listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023.
interesting_fact: Intellif's founding capital was largely intellectual property: Chen and Tian contributed a non-patent technology package for 'extracting crowd feature values through video analysis', valued at RMB 4.7M, in 70/30 proportion.
current_role: Cofounder and former director of Intellif (Shenzhen Intellifusion, SSE STAR: 688343); sole owner of NaitMind, Inc. (current active role not published)
research_notes: Very low profile; no interviews or bio found. Possibly US-based (owns US-registered NaitMind, Inc.) but unconfirmed. Not to be confused with Intellif CEO Chen Ning. Intellif IR is the only published channel and he is no longer a director there.

profile: Wang Yongfeng is a long-time Neusoft Group executive (former VP, president and rotating CEO of Neusoft, 600718.SH) who now chairs and runs Neusoft Reach, Neusoft's intelligent-vehicle spin-off and a Hurun-listed unicorn. Neusoft Reach supplies automotive base software (NeuSAR OS), AI computing platforms, driver-assistance stacks and EV power electronics (BMS) to carmakers.
interesting_fact: Neusoft Reach's NeuSAR automotive OS has been adapted to more than 100 mainstream domestic and international chips; Wang calls the car OS 'the strategic commanding height' of intelligent vehicles (Beijing Auto Show 2026).

Data-center/AI angle: car-cloud AI computing platform. 'Founder' label in input is loose; Neusoft Reach was founded by Neusoft Group.

name: Justin Waldron
profile: American game developer and angel investor who co-founded Zynga at 19 and was lead engineer/designer on its first game, Texas Hold'em Poker (later Zynga Poker). He rose to SVP Product before leaving in October 2013. He then co-founded Playco in Tokyo with Game Closure's Michael Carter; it raised a $100M Series A in September 2020 at just over $1B, making it a unicorn.
interesting_fact: He was only 19 when he built Zynga Poker, Zynga's first game. On leaving in 2013 he wrote that it had been 'six and a half years since we pushed the button to launch our first game, and each moment since has been magic'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Playco he had invested in more than 50 startups, including Snackpass and Substack. He relocated to Tokyo to run Playco as President.
current_role: Co-founder and President, Playco (Tokyo instant-play web games company), per 2020 coverage; current title not re-confirmed
public_contact: contact_form: https://www.play.co/ (inquiry form on Playco site) | podcast: Colossus episode 'Waldron: The Future of Social Gaming'
research_notes: Lower profile than Zynga co-founder Mark Pincus. Playco's site is still live (games: Everwing, Heads Up!, Buruburu Do Butsu), but I found no post-2021 news on the company's status or his current title. The Colossus podcast page blocked automated access, so I confirmed it only from search results. Several sources say he dropped out of UConn to co-found Zynga.

name: Meng Jiange
profile: Most likely Robin (Jiange) Meng, chairman of GenScript, whose CDMO subsidiary Probio provides biologics and cell/gene-therapy manufacturing services; GenScript announced plans in Sept 2026 to spin off Probio on the HKEX. A finance executive with 30+ years' experience, he joined GenScript as CFO (c. 2010-2017) and became chairman around 2020.
interesting_fact: Before GenScript he was CFO of Quay Magnesium (2008-2010), Asia finance controller at Saint-Gobain's Grains and Powder division, and held finance roles at Schering-Plough China and Guangdong Whirlpool.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer - a Bachelor of Engineering from Changsha Communications Institute (now Changsha University of Science & Technology) - before earning a Master's in finance from Queen's University at Kingston, Canada.
current_role: Executive Director & Chairman, GenScript Biotech Corp. (HKEX: 1548), parent of Probio; also a director of Legend Biotech
research_notes: Identity match is probable but not confirmed: Hurun lists him as a Probio 'founder', while GenScript names Frank Zhang, Sally Wang and Larry Wang as co-founders and Meng as chairman. Also known as Robin Meng / Jian Ge Meng.

name: Yang Wei
profile: Yang Wei (杨威) founded Shanghai-based Quicktron in 2014. It makes autonomous mobile robots and warehouse-automation software, and its backers include Alibaba's Cainiao, BEST Inc., KION Group and Aramco's Prosperity7. By 2021 Quicktron served 500+ customers in 30+ industries and was expanding to Europe, the Americas and Asia.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he set the goal of expanding Quicktron from 15 markets to more than 100 countries and shipping one hundred thousand robots, and said: 'Within five years, we hope to achieve tens of billions in revenue.'
deep_cut_fact: At 36Kr's 2017 summit he gave a talk titled 'Intelligent Robots: Giving Warehouses a Soul' (智能机器人——赋予仓库灵魂), arguing that robot clusters could save about 50% of warehouse labor.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Quicktron Robotics (Shanghai Quicktron Intelligent Technology)
research_notes: A common Chinese name; identity is tied to Quicktron via 36Kr and The Wire China (which says he is in his early 40s). Education (Peking University master's) appears only in third-party summaries and was not verified. Low English-language profile; best route is via the company.

name: Ni Fei
profile: Shanghai Jiao Tong University PhD in mechatronic engineering and port-automation engineer who co-founded warehouse-robotics company Quicktron (Shanghai, est. 2014) with CEO Yang Wei. Quicktron builds AMRs and intralogistics automation; investors include Cainiao, KION and Aramco's Prosperity7. Company registry data shows him as a ~10.35% shareholder.
interesting_fact: Quicktron's 2020 C+ round of over $100M was co-led by forklift/supply-chain group KION and Saudi Aramco's Prosperity7 Ventures; Cainiao (Alibaba's logistics arm) is also a major shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: Before Quicktron he was director of the R&D center at ZPMC (Shanghai Zhenhua Heavy Industries) electrical company, where he led development of China's first generation of automated rail-mounted gantry cranes and port AGVs.
current_role: Co-founder, Quicktron Robotics (Shanghai Quicktron Intelligent Technology); current title not verified
research_notes: Very low public profile; Chinese name 倪菲. Bio sourced from 36Kr PitchHub company profile (third-party compiled). Alive status not independently confirmed; no indication otherwise.

name: He Dongdong
profile: He Dongdong (b. 1967; SJTU industrial-management engineering, CEIBS EMBA) spent 2003-2017 at construction-equipment giant SANY, rising to senior VP and head of process IT. In 2016 he launched SANY's spin-out Rootcloud, an industrial-internet (IIoT) platform connecting factory and machinery data; it filed for a STAR Market IPO in 2022 and in 2026 was on Hurun's Global Unicorn list for the sixth year running.
interesting_fact: Rootcloud grew out of SANY's own effort to connect its excavators and cranes worldwide and became one of China's flagship industrial-internet platforms, recognised as a Hurun global unicorn six years in a row (2026).
deep_cut_fact: At SANY he ran businesses abroad, serving as general manager of SANY India and chairman of SANY Germany before becoming SANY's CIO-style process-IT chief; he is also vice president of the Chinese Society of Vocational and Technical Education.
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairman and General Manager/CEO, Rootcloud (树根互联 / 树根科技), Guangzhou
research_notes: Company now brands itself 树根科技 (Rootcloud Technology); still unlisted as of 2026. Frequent speaker on industrial internet/AI in manufacturing. No press email found (site lists only a partner@ address).

name: Cui Dong
profile: Born 1971, Cui Dong worked in government and then as a senior executive at Hua Hong and SMIC, rising to SMIC executive VP for investment and strategy. In 2014 he led the founding of SMIC-Changdian, a JV incubated by SMIC and JCET, which became SJSemi - a leader in bumping, wafer-level and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging for AI chips. SJSemi has cleared review for a STAR Market IPO.
interesting_fact: SJSemi has no controlling shareholder (top holder under 11%), but Cui controls the votes of all 11 employee shareholding platforms; revenue grew from about RMB1.6bn to RMB6.5bn on AI-chip packaging demand, fastest among the global top-10 packaging/test firms.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering the chip industry he worked as a secretary in the General Office of China's Ministry of Electronics Industry, which commentators credit for his feel for national industrial policy.
current_role: Founder, chairman & CEO of SJ Semiconductor (盛合晶微, formerly SMIC-Changdian / 中芯长电), Jiangyin
public_contact: press_email: PR@sjsemi.com | contact_form: https://www.sjsemi.com/contact (在线留言 online message) | official_website: https://www.sjsemi.com
research_notes: Strong AI/data-center angle (advanced packaging for AI accelerators; heavy customer concentration in a large domestic AI-chip client). Media differ on his title (chairman vs CEO); profile details are from media reports, not the prospectus.

name: Li Yang
profile: Li Yang (b. ~1974) is an RF engineer who spent years in the US chip industry before founding Smarter Micro in Guangzhou in November 2011. The company designs RF front-end modules (power amplifiers etc.) for 4G/5G phones and IoT using a reconfigurable RF front-end architecture, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023; he holds ~9.5% directly.
interesting_fact: Smarter Micro bet on a 'reconfigurable' RF front-end architecture - one adaptable PA design covering many frequency bands - as China's answer to the Skyworks/Qorvo-dominated discrete-module approach.
deep_cut_fact: Before returning to China he worked in US RF/semiconductor firms: Principal Engineer at Millennial Net (2004-06), Staff Engineer at Peregrine Semiconductor (2006-08) and Principal Engineer at Skyworks (2008-11), founding Smarter Micro three months after leaving Skyworks.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Guangzhou Smarter Microelectronics (Smarter Micro / 慧智微, SSE STAR: 688512)
public_contact: ir_email: db@smartermicro.com (board office / investor contact) | official_website: http://www.smartermicro.com (company)
research_notes: Common name - identity confirmed via Smarter Micro annual report. Fit is semiconductors (RF for handsets), not data-center power directly.

name: John Schwarz

In 2010 he co-founded people-analytics company Visier in Vancouver with Ryan Wong and his sons Jan and Brett. Has sat on boards including Synopsys and Teradata.
interesting_fact: As CEO of Business Objects he doubled revenue to over $1.5B, made seven acquisitions and negotiated its sale to SAP.
deep_cut_fact: He holds both a BA in political science and a BSc in computer science from the University of Manitoba, plus an executive MBA from the University of Toronto; Dalhousie gave him an honorary law doctorate in 2004.
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman (former CEO), Visier Inc.

name: Wang Anquan
profile: Chinese software engineer (Hunan University CS) who spent 2006-2012 at Alibaba's finance arm, then worked at Hengfeng Bank and as GM of Xiaomi Finance before founding Fumi Technology in 2016, parent of the Webull commission-free trading app. Webull listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in April 2025; he controls the majority of its voting power.
interesting_fact: Xiaomi, where he ran the finance business in 2015-16, was one of Fumi/Webull's early investors.
deep_cut_fact: Webull's first MVP was built in 2013 while he was still at Alibaba: he and an Ali colleague developed it as a market-intelligence tool, years before it became a brokerage.
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Webull Corporation (Nasdaq: BULL)
research_notes: Very low Western media profile; Webull's US face is Anthony Denier. Best route is Webull IR/communications. Ownership/voting figures should be checked against 20-F.

name: Wu Yun
profile: Chinese enterprise-software founder (吴云, 'Will Woo') who set up XforcePlus in 2015 to digitise VAT invoices and supply-chain/finance/tax collaboration for large enterprises. Backed by Temasek (2019 Series C ~$100M) and a 2021 round at ~$1B valuation. Company filings show him holding the large majority of the operating entity.
interesting_fact: Described as a China supply-chain/finance/tax IT expert who led construction of what was billed as China's largest cloud-deployed financial shared-services platform before founding XforcePlus.
deep_cut_fact: Named to Fortune China's 2020 '40 Under 40' business list and is a member of Tsinghua SEM's entrepreneur-scholar DBA programme.
current_role: Founder & CEO, XforcePlus (Shanghai Yunli Information Technology / 票易通)
research_notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable; no press email found.

name: Shen Xiangyang
profile: Harry Shum (沈向洋, b. 1966, Nanjing) earned a CMU robotics PhD (1996), co-founded Microsoft Research Asia and rose to Microsoft EVP of AI & Research, overseeing Bing and Cortana. He left in 2020 as Microsoft spun its Xiaoice chatbot into an independent company he co-founded, then founded the IDEA institute in Shenzhen and has chaired HKUST's Council since 2023.
interesting_fact: HKUST's Chancellor reappointed him Council Chairman for a second three-year term from March 6, 2026. He is also a foreign member of the US National Academy of Engineering and an IEEE Fellow, ACM Fellow and FREng.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Microsoft's AI empire he was a computer-vision researcher: with Richard Szeliski he wrote the SIGGRAPH 1997 paper 'Creating full view panoramic image mosaics and environment maps', showing how to seamlessly stitch handheld-camera photos into 360-degree panoramas.
current_role: Chairman of the HKUST Council (reappointed for 2026-2029); founder of IDEA (International Digital Economy Academy, Shenzhen); co-founder/chair of Xiaoice
research_notes: Hurun lists him under Xiaoice (valued ~$2B); Xiaoice's current status/leadership is unclear in 2025-26 coverage. No personal published contact found. Best routes are institutional: HKUST (Council Chair's office via HKUST communications) or the IDEA institute in Shenzhen. Very high-profile AI figure.

name: Bao chunjian
profile: Chinese engineer (USTC computer science graduate) who spent ~9 years at Tencent, rising to data-centre director in its data platform department, before founding Xiaoe-tech, a SaaS platform that lets creators, educators and brands sell paid knowledge content, courses and live streams. Tencent is a major shareholder (~16.8%); the company has been preparing a Hong Kong listing.
interesting_fact: At Tencent he reached the rare 'T4 expert engineer' technical rank before leaving in 2015 to start his own business.
deep_cut_fact: Xiaoe-tech's prototype was a one-month rebuild of the paid-audio and membership system for finance writer Wu Xiaobo's 'Wu Xiaobo Channel' in 2016; Wu then invested. His first venture, a blue-collar hiring app called 工作帮, shut after about seven months.
current_role: Founder and CEO, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通), Shenzhen
research_notes: Known internally as 'Lao Bao'; hosts Xiaoe-tech's live interview series 老鲍对话标杆客户. Chinese-language outreach via Xiaoe-tech (xiaoe-tech.com) recommended. Education details vary across sources.

name: Yu Qianli
profile: One of the ex-Tencent co-founders of Xiaoe-tech, the Shenzhen SaaS company led by founder-CEO Bao Chunjian (鲍春健). Its tools help merchants, educators and creators run e-commerce, marketing and CRM in their own channels. Investors include Tencent, Hillhouse, IDG and Qiming. Its 2021 Series D valued it at about HK$5.1B. It filed for a Hong Kong IPO in August 2025, and 36Kr reported a new attempt in May 2026.

deep_cut_fact: 36Kr reports that this co-founder was previously responsible for product development on Tencent's QQ Zone (QQ空间). The article spells the name 喻干里, likely a misprint of 喻千里 (Yu Qianli).
current_role: Co-founder, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通, Shenzhen private-domain operations / creator-commerce SaaS)
public_contact: press_email: contact@xiaoe-tech.com (Xiaoe-tech Public Affairs Dept.) | official_website: https://www.xiaoe-tech.com/
research_notes: Very low public profile. The only mention I found is in 36Kr, which spells the name 喻干里 rather than 喻千里, so identity is marked uncertain until checked against the HKEX prospectus. Bao Chunjian is the public face and controlling shareholder (about 44.9% pre-IPO). Chinese-language outreach via the company's public-affairs email is the best route.

name: Wang Lianghu
profile: Wang Lianghu (王良虎) co-founded Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通), a Shenzhen SaaS platform for selling online courses and digital content and running private-domain customer operations. It was founded by ex-Tencent data-center director Bao Chunjian, is backed by Tencent, Hillhouse and IDG, and refiled for a Hong Kong IPO in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech is a 'Tencent alumni' startup: all four co-founders came from Tencent, and co-founder Yu Ganli once handled QQ Zone product development. Revenue grew from RMB 298M (2022) to RMB 521M (2024).
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Xiaoe-tech, Wang Lianghu was a T3-level senior R&D engineer at Tencent, as was fellow co-founder Zeng Yongjun.
current_role: Co-founder and VP of Product & R&D (产研副总裁), Xiaoe-tech / 小鹅通 (Shenzhen)

name: Ze Yongjun
profile: Xiaoe-tech's 2026 Hong Kong IPO filing coverage names co-founders Wang Lianghu and Zeng Yongjun (曾勇军), both former Tencent T3 senior R&D engineers, alongside founder-chairman-CEO Bao Chunjian (ex-Tencent data-centre director). Founded in 2015, Xiaoe-tech sells SaaS tools for online courses and private-domain e-commerce. Tencent invested in its 2020 Series C. It reported 2025 revenue of about RMB 608M and is pursuing an HKEX listing.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech's founding team is heavily ex-Tencent. Founder Bao Chunjian ran Tencent's data centre business, two co-founders were Tencent T3 senior engineers, and another co-founder (Yu Ganli) worked on QQ Zone product development.
current_role: Co-founder, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通, Shenzhen knowledge-commerce / private-domain SaaS); current title not found
research_notes: 'Ze Yongjun' appears to be a romanization of 曾勇军 (Zeng Yongjun), a co-founder named in 36Kr's May 2026 IPO coverage. The match is likely but not confirmed. He is not among the listed executive directors (Bao Chunjian, Wang Tiebo, Hu Yabei, Zhou Shikun). Very low public profile; the best route is via the company once IR contacts appear in the HKEX prospectus.

name: Deng Guobiao
profile: Deng Guobiao ('Bill Deng') spent over a decade in payments, first at Visa and then at Ant Financial's Alipay (joined 2010), before co-founding XTransfer in May 2017 with five former Alibaba/Ant colleagues as a 'B2B version of Alipay'. XTransfer serves 800,000+ enterprises and holds payment licences in multiple markets; he now speaks widely on stablecoins for trade.
interesting_fact: Deng says he jumped to found XTransfer after watching colleagues leave to start businesses including ride-hailing giant Didi; he argues stablecoins suit cross-border B2B trade because 'when it comes to money, there's no 24/7 infrastructure'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alipay he worked at Visa; Alibaba's eWTP fund led XTransfer's $15M Series B1, and Deng has said 'Our background from Alibaba indeed offers a good start'.
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, XTransfer (Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments platform for SMEs)
research_notes: Goes by Bill Deng in English media; active conference speaker (Singapore FinTech Festival, Forum Ekonomi Malaysia). No dedicated press email found; contact page offers general inquiry form.

name: Zheng Kai

Only one aggregator profile names 'Kai Zheng (Co-founder and CSO)'; no official XTransfer source found confirming his role.

He previously spent more than a decade in payments at Visa and Ant Financial. Fortune reported in 2026 that XTransfer serves over 800,000 businesses and processes over $12B a month.

current_role: (If same person) Founder & CEO, XTransfer (Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments)

name: Liu Yanfang
profile: Chinese technologist (刘艳芳) who co-founded XTransfer in 2017 with CEO Bill (Guobiao) Deng and other ex-Alibaba/Ant Group colleagues; she leads engineering as CTO. current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Chief Technology Officer, XTransfer (Shanghai)

interesting_fact: XTransfer's 2017 seed round was just $2.95M at a $12M post-money valuation (from Yunqi Partners and Gaorong); its 2026 Series E valued it at $3.02B.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding XTransfer, Yao was at Ant Group heading international risk and merchant risk management and leading its business-intelligence department.

name: Zhang Buzheng
profile: Zhang Buzhen (张步镇) is the founder of Guangzhou-based Yaoshibang (YSB), a B2B pharmaceutical e-commerce and services platform connecting drug makers and distributors with China's pharmacies and clinics. He became CEO when Xiaoice was spun out of Microsoft in July 2020 and was its second-largest shareholder (about 25%). He left in April 2025 and in December 2025 unveiled Nextie, a MiraclePlus-backed startup of about 30 people, mostly from the original Xiaoice team.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Xiaoice grew from a Microsoft chatbot into a global product line covering China, Japan, the US, India and other markets, and became one of China's first AI unicorns after the 2020 spin-out.
deep_cut_fact: A Tsinghua graduate, he joined Microsoft's Asia internet engineering academy in September 2013, where he pioneered Microsoft's AI emotional-computing framework. He later became the academy's executive vice president.
current_role: Founder, Nextie (明日新程), a 'collective intelligence and cognitive large model' AI startup; former CEO of Xiaoice (left April 2025)
research_notes: Xiaoice is no longer the right route. He debuted Nextie at MiraclePlus (奇绩创坛) Demo Day on Dec 7, 2025, and Nextie was planning a ~$10M funding round. No published Nextie press contact was found. English coverage: https://news.aibase.com/news/23484. He gives long-form interviews to Chinese tech media (36Kr, ifanr).

name: Ruan Chenjie
profile: Ruan Chenjie (阮晨杰) founded Shanghai-based power-management chip designer Southchip in 2015 after leaving Texas Instruments. Southchip makes fast-charging, charge-pump, buck-boost and battery-management ICs for phones, laptops and cars, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023. Ruan is the controlling shareholder (~17%) and still runs the company.
interesting_fact: Southchip's customers include Xiaomi, Honor, OPPO, Vivo, Lenovo, Samsung and DJI, and it has joined Apple's supplier list. It is one of the few Chinese firms offering end-to-end fast-charging solutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Southchip, Ruan worked at Richtek and Texas Instruments. Within a year, Southchip shipped the SC8801, billed as the industry's first buck-boost charging chip supporting USB Type-C Power Delivery. Lei Jun's Shunwei Capital led its 2018 Series A, its first-ever chip-design investment.
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Southchip Semiconductor Technology (Shanghai) Co. (SSE STAR: 688484)
research_notes: Hurun listed Southchip as a unicorn, but it has since listed publicly (STAR Market, 2023). There is no personal social presence; the best route is the company IR mailbox / board secretary's office. Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

After stints at Oppo's AI lab and Huawei's Ascend unit as a 'Genius Youth' hire, he left in Dec 2022 and co-founded humanoid-robot maker AgiBot with CEO Deng Taihua in Feb 2023; it is now one of China's largest humanoid makers.
interesting_fact: His homemade self-driving, self-balancing bicycle went viral on Bilibili in 2021; he has 2.5M+ followers there as 'Zhihui Jun'.
deep_cut_fact: He studied biomedical engineering at UESTC, and in 2021 built 'Dummy', an Iron Man-inspired desktop robotic arm that could thread a needle and stitch grape skins; a 2018 bipedal robot of his won an innovation award at the World Robot Olympiad.
current_role: Co-founder, President and CTO, AgiBot (Zhiyuan Robotics), Shanghai
public_contact: official_website: https://www.agibot.com | office_email: sales@agibot.com (company general/sales inbox, not personal) | other: Bilibili: https://space.bilibili.com/20259914 | other: GitHub: https://github.com/peng-zhihui
research_notes: Very active public creator; Bilibili/GitHub are his own channels. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Yu Enyuan
profile: Yu Enyuan (余恩源) is a logistics-equipment veteran who founded Beijing-based Neolix in 2018 to build L4 autonomous delivery vans. After an early detour into mobile vending, Neolix pivoted to courier logistics, raised a $600M+ Series D and (Oct 2026) a ~$400M Series E, and says it has deployed 13,000+ vehicles in 300+ cities across 15 countries.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Neolix obtained China's first public-road licence for an autonomous delivery vehicle; in 2026 Yu said the industry's real 'blue ocean' is nighttime delivery.
deep_cut_fact: Yu graduated from Chongqing University in automation in 1996, invented a parcel locker and built China's first dedicated courier handheld scanner (PDA). Neolix's first vans used the chassis and Changzhou production lines of Li Xiang's shelved SEV mini-car; Li Auto became its angel investor.
current_role: Founder & CEO, Neolix (新石器无人车), Beijing
research_notes: contacts@neolix.cn is Neolix's general company contact (no separate press address found). Yu speaks often at Chinese mobility conferences; Gasgoo has English coverage of his talks.

name: Guo Lifu
profile: Guo Lifu (郭立阜) is a former Synopsys Fellow and R&D vice president who in 2020 co-founded Shanghai-based EDA firm UniVista with investor Pan Jianyue and ex-Cadence China head Xu Yun; he is co-president. UniVista, which builds domestic chip-verification and design tools, raised ~RMB 3B, was valued around RMB 13B and began A-share IPO tutoring in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: UniVista deliberately chose chip verification as its entry point because verification was the weakest link among Chinese EDA tools; within about a year of founding it had grown to 300 staff, 220+ in R&D.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding UniVista he held the title of Fellow at Synopsys, one of the most senior technical ranks at the US EDA giant, alongside a role as R&D vice president; UniVista's CTO Pei-Hsin Ho is also an ex-Synopsys Fellow.

name: Yang Yufeng
profile: Yang Yufeng (杨玉峰, b. 1976) is a career executive at State Power Investment Corp (SPIC), not a founder in the entrepreneurial sense. In January 2026 SPIC put him in charge of its hydrogen unicorn 国氢科技 (Hurun: ~$1.9B) on top of chairing listed SPIC Green Energy, which renamed itself from Jilin Electric Power in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: 国氢科技's self-developed 'Qingteng' (氢腾) fuel-cell systems powered about 150 hydrogen buses that handled transport during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics. The company has built an in-house supply chain covering catalysts, proton-exchange membranes, carbon paper and full stack/system integration.
deep_cut_fact: Yang came up through HR and power marketing rather than engineering. He headed human resources at China Power International, ran the Pingdingshan Yaomeng coal-fired power plants in Henan, then directed SPIC's electricity-market marketing centre before taking over Jilin Electric. He holds a master's degree and is a senior economist.
current_role: Party Secretary & Chairman, SPIC Hydrogen Energy Technology (国氢科技, 'Spiche'); also Chairman of SPIC Green Energy (电投绿能, formerly Jilin Electric Power, SZ:000875)

name: Wang Kai
profile: Wang Kai (汪凯) holds a BS from UESTC and an EE PhD from Illinois, and is an ex-Broadcom/Freescale executive. In 2019 he became CEO of SiEngine, the auto-chip firm set up in 2018 by Geely's Li Shufu, ECARX and Arm China. SiEngine shipped China's first 7nm automotive cockpit SoC (Longying-1), and at Auto China 2026 it unveiled the 5nm Longying-2 AI chip.
interesting_fact: Rather than start at 28nm or 12nm like local rivals, he bet the company on 7nm automotive-grade silicon when no Chinese firm had done it. Longying-1 has 8.8bn transistors on 83 mm² and went into Geely and FAW cars from 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Before SiEngine he was at HXT Semiconductor (华芯通半导体), which he left in 2019. He has said SiEngine taped out its first chip in just over two years only because its founding team had done chip design and market-building before.
current_role: Founder, Director and CEO, SiEngine Technology (芯擎科技), Wuhan/Shanghai
public_contact: ir_email: ir.info@siengine.com | office_email: siengine@siengine.com | official_website: https://www.siengine.com/

profile: Liu Yu (born 1995) earned his PhD at CUHK's Multimedia Lab and spent about nine years at SenseTime, becoming one of its youngest executive research directors and running ~200 people. In late 2024 he left to found Vivix, which builds real-time interactive character and world models (Vivix-A1, W1) and is reportedly valued at $1.32B.

deep_cut_fact: In 2014, as a college junior, he built a drone flight-control system that automatically tracked people using 3D CNNs and real-time video tracking, before DJI's Phantom 4 came out. He joined SenseTime in late 2015 and helped it win ImageNet while commuting weekly between Beijing and CUHK.

name: Xu Min
profile: Xu Min (许敏) leads Fudan University's magnetic-confinement fusion team. In July 2025 the team spun out SunUp Fusion in Shanghai. It raised an angel round of several hundred million yuan in Jan 2026 (Sequoia China, IDG, Hillhouse and others) and then a $100M round in June 2026 co-led by Qiming, Zhuhai S&T Group, ICBC Capital and CMC Capital. current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Baidu Inc.
research_notes: Known in English as Robin Li. The listed SEC insider roles (Datadog CPO, Equinix director) belong to a different person, Yanbing Li; this is a name-match error, not Robin Li. Best route is via Baidu corporate/IR.
